Specifications for Emirates ID / Residence Visa for UAE ICA Photos – Size and Requirements
Make sure your printed photo looks sharp by following these guidelines for passport and visa photos.
Color
Capture the picture in color against a backdrop, like white or off white.
Resolution
Aim for a resolution of least 600 DPI, ideally ranging from 600 to 1200 DPI. File Size. Make sure your photo file size falls between 1 MB and 15 MB.
Tips, for Capturing an Emirates ID / Residence Visa for UAE ICA Photo
Camera Placement
Position the camera 5-7 feet (1.5-2 meters) away to capture your body.
Pose
Stand tall and relaxed looking directly at the camera.
Lighting
Ensure uniform lighting to avoid any shadows.
How to Take Photos of Babies and Kids

When photographing babies and children follow these suggestions.  •	Newborns. Lay a sheet on the floor and place the baby on it.  •	Older Babies. Seat them in a child’s chair against a white backdrop. For support you can use your hand behind the sheet to steady their head making sure no one else is visible in the frame.
PhotoGov Features
PhotoGov provides functions to assist you in creating the photo.
Cropping
Trim any uneven edges for proper sizing.
Resizing
Adjust the photo to meet required dimensions without distorting it.
Background Removal
Create a neutral background even if one isn't available.
Automatic Adjustments
Enhance brightness, color and contrast, with just one click.
Photos for a UAE Visa
Visitors apply under a separate rule set, and the UAE visa photo requirements page explains the ICP rules for a visa photograph.
Emirates ID Photo Standards
The Emirates ID photo requirements page sets out the ICP specifications for size, background, and facial expression in one place.

children.innerHtml: Take the Right Picture for Your UAE ID Card (4x6 cm)

How to Take the Right Picture for Your UAE ID Card (4x6 cm)  One of the most crucial things to do when applying for a UAE ID card is to send in the right photo.  This picture has to meet tight requirements because it will be used for biometric identification and security.  Even little mistakes can make your application take longer or get turned down.   But don't be alarmed!  You don't need to go to a photo booth or hire a professional photographer to make the perfect UAE ID card photo with PhotoGov.net.
For a visa application, the UAE visa photo rules are explained in a separate guide.

Why the Picture on Your UAE ID Card Is Important

The picture on your UAE ID card is very important for your application. It is used by the government to identify people and is part of the biometric verification procedure. Your application could be delayed or turned down if your photo doesn't match the technical standards.
The travel document is a separate case: the UAE passport photo requirements page describes the 40 x 60 mm biometric image it takes.
You don't have to worry about making mistakes because PhotoGov.net makes sure that your photo automatically fits all the requirements. Everything is checked and changed automatically by our platform.
How PhotoGov Can Help You Take the Best Picture for Your UAE ID Card
PhotoGov makes it easy and quick to take the correct picture for your UAE ID card.  This is how it works:
Take a selfie with your phone in good light.
Your face should be clearly visible, and your expression should be neutral
Upload Your Photo:

Our AI Does the Work:

How to take your own UAE ID card photo

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect employment authorization photo yourself:
1. Take a picture of yourself

Open up the PhotoGov.net photo service and take your picture. Make sure you’re not wearing any headcovers or glasses, do not wear a uniform, and keep your expression neutral. Ensure that the area is well-lit and that you are standing against a neutral background.

children.innerHtml: Things You Shouldn't Do
Here are some typical problems that can make your UAE ID card application take longer or not be approved:
The background must be pure white or light gray
Your photo must be exactly 40 mm x 60 mm
Bad lighting: Make sure there are no shadows or dark areas on your face
You should have a neutral expression on your face, not a smile or frown
If you wear glasses, be sure they don't reflect or glare
PhotoGov automatically fixes these issues for you, making sure your photo is legal
Important Parts of PhotoGov
This is why PhotoGov is the best and easiest way to get a picture of your UAE ID card:
Crop
This feature automatically cuts your picture down to the right size of 4x6 cm
Resize
Changes the size of the picture so that it fits the official size for your UAE ID card photo
Background removal
This feature gets rid of any background that can be distracting and replaces it with a neutral, compatible hue
Auto-adjustment
Changes the brightness, sharpness, and contrast to make sure the picture is of great quality
PhotoGov.net is quick and easy to use
All you have to do is post your selfie, and we'll do the rest
Cheap: You may get great results without spending a lot of money on photo booths
Every Time Compliant: Our system makes sure that your photo fits all the official requirements for UAE ID card photos
We offer both printable and digital versions, so you're ready for any way to submit
How to take UAE ID card photos for babies and kids

When taking pictures of babies and children for employment authorization, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.

UAE Visa Photo — Size and Requirements
Ensure your photo adheres to these specifications:
Technical Requirements: If you are processing the photo yourself through Photoshop or other services:
Size:
300x369 pixels
Color
Photos must be in color with a white or off-white background
Resolution
1-2 DPI, file size between 1 MB and 15 MB
Attire
Wear normal clothes, avoid uniforms, camouflage, head coverings, and glasses
For image quality and background

•	Ensure that the photo is clear focused, free of blur or noise and not pixelated. 
 •	Use a background without any shadows.
Here's how to take your UAE Visa online Emirates.com photo.
1.	Preparation. Find a lit area with a background.
2.	Taking the Photo. Make sure there are no shadows present wear clothing stand upright and either use a tripod or have someone take the picture from 5-7 feet away.
3.	Upload and Edit. Submit your image to PhotoGov AI for adjustments and optimization.
4.	Download. Receive your finalized photo for use.
Tips for photographing babies and children
•	For newborns. Lay them on a sheet.
•	For infants. Seat them in a chair with a sheet, in the background. Here are some tips, for taking passport photos.
Lighting Tips
•	Opt for light whenever possible. Position yourself in front of a window to avoid shadows.
•	If artificial light is necessary use sources to minimize shadows. Place the lights evenly around you. Avoid overhead lighting that can create unwanted shadows on your face.
Camera Settings
•	Set your camera or smartphone to the resolution setting.
•	Make sure the camera is focused on your face. Use autofocus if its available.
•	Keep your camera stable by using a tripod or placing it on a surface to prevent images.
Posture and Expression
•	Stand upright with shoulders back.
•	Maintain an expression. don't smile relax your face with eyes open and mouth closed.
•	Look directly at the camera ensuring that your eyes are visible and not obstructed by hair or glasses.
Background Preparation
•	Opt for a background such, as a white or off white wall.
•	Make sure to avoid any decorations or designs.
•	Distance. Position yourself a couple of feet away, from the wall to prevent shadows from appearing.
•	Substitute Background. If you don't have a wall hang up a sheet behind you for a neat backdrop.
Outfit Choice
•	Opt for casual, attire. Steer clear of uniforms and camouflage clothing.
•	Avoid headwear. Unless its for reasons refrain from wearing hats or head coverings.
•	Eyewear. Take off your glasses to avoid reflections and ensure your eyes are clearly visible.
Preparing for Photo Submission
Preparing Digital Files:
•	File Format. Save your photo, in the specified format (JPEG, PNG, etc.).
•	Naming Guidelines. Follow any naming rules provided by the application instructions.
•	File Size. Make sure the file size falls within the required limits. Use tools to compress it if needed.
Printing Your Photo
•	Paper Selection. Use high quality photo paper, whether matte or glossy finish.
•	Print Resolution. Set your printer to the quality setting. If uncertain seek assistance from a photo printing service.
Before you submit your photo make sure it meets all the specified requirements and consider getting feedback from someone.
Our online photo tool provides features to assist you in creating the photo, including cropping and resizing background removal and auto adjustment of brightness, color and contrast.
When printing your photo opt, for matte or glossy paper. Visit a photo service if necessary.

PhotoGov and the ICP Standards for Visa Photos

PhotoGov applies the official specifications issued by the Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs, and Port Security (ICP) to produce images that match UAE visa photo requirements. The service aligns every technical aspect — from background and head position to proportions and eye level — with national standards based on the biometric framework of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO). Passports are covered by the same ICP framework, and the PhotoGov UAE photo guide sets out those specifications for travel documents.
All compliance parameters are reviewed and updated by PhotoGov’s internal experts to stay consistent with the most recent ICAO and ICP guidelines.
For applications that demand maximum accuracy, PhotoGov also offers Human Verification — a manual quality check carried out by a senior compliance specialist.

To ensure your Austria Passport photo is accepted, it must meet specific technical and appearance guidelines. Here’s a breakdown of what’s required:
Size
Resolution
Minimum 300 DPI
Image Format
JPEG or PNG
File Size
Typically under 1 MB
Background Color
Plain white or light-colored (no patterns or shadows)
Printable
Yes – required for in-person submission at Austrian authorities

children.innerHtml: How to take your own Austria Passport photo

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect passport photo yourself:
1. Take a picture of yourself

Open up the PhotoGov.net photo service and take your picture. Make sure you’re not wearing any headcovers or glasses, do not wear a uniform, and keep your expression neutral. Ensure that the area is well-lit and that you are standing against a neutral background.

attributes.alt: How to take photo for document
attributes.title: Clean background. More light. Not a blurry photo.

children.innerHtml: Watch "How to take a photo" (00:46)
2. Upload your photo to PhotoGov AI
Next, upload your image and process it through our site.

children.innerHtml: 3. Receive your Passport Photo
Finally, you can download your ID photo. These images can be printed off, or you can simply use them as digital photos.
How to take Austria Passport photos for babies and kids

When taking pictures of babies and children for passport, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.
Additional Compliance Tips
No Retouching – Do not use filters or any apps that change’s ones facial features
Sharpness – Make sure the image is not blurry or pixelated
Face Coverage – Your face should take up 70-80% of the photo height
File Format & Size – JPEG or PNG. Less than 1 MB for digital submission
Common Mistakes to Avoid
Using the wrong size (e.g. passport instead of 35x45 mm)
Sporting any glasses or head coverings that obscure your face (unless your religion or a medical issue requires you to)
Misusing blurry, low-quality, or overexposed photos
Backgrounds with shadows, patterns, or objects
These problems will be identified and corrected as part of the flow of the PhotoGov application
Submission & Printing
For Submission In-Person: Print Your Photo on Photo Paper. High Quality Matte or Glossy Finish Paper Only, Size 35x45 mm (3.5x4. 5 cm)
For Digital Submission: You should also submit a digital picture of yours in the Austria visa application portal or consulate system. Make sure it is within the size and resolution guidelines
Frequently Asked Questions

children.innerHtml: Come Away With the Perfect Austrian ID Card Photo at Home
It’s never been simpler to take your ID photo. Follow these steps:
Look for a light background — a white or beige wall will do
Use natural light — face a window or use soft light
Keep the phone at eye level — or use a little help.Involve other people
Maintain a neutral expression — don’t smile and don’t frown
Import your selfie into PhotoGov — let our AI do the rest
Download the outcome — your file is ready for printing and submission safe
How to take your own Austrian ID card photo

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect employment authorization photo yourself:
1. Take a picture of yourself

Open up the PhotoGov.net photo service and take your picture. Make sure you’re not wearing any headcovers or glasses, do not wear a uniform, and keep your expression neutral. Ensure that the area is well-lit and that you are standing against a neutral background.

Rules to apply in Composition

You should have centered your head both vertically and horizontally
Please Keep the head height at 32-36 mm
The background should be plain and without any shadows
Wear no bright white to blend with the background
No filters, color correction or retouching is permitted

Your file should be in JPEG or PNG with appropriate resolution and dimensions. Austrian e-government websites generally have provisions for digital contributions
Physical submission:

children.innerHtml: How to take Austrian ID card photos for babies and kids

When taking pictures of babies and children for employment authorization, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.
Where Can You Print?
After you see the perfect photo on PhotoGov, you can:
Print at home with a high-quality printer
Utilize a photo kiosk at your local pharmacy or grocery store
Post the file out for online printing
All files are precisely scaled to 35mm x 45mm and ready for printing

children.innerHtml: What is an Australian Passport Photo?
The official photo format required for an Australian passport.
Automatically prepared by PhotoGov as a correctly sized, DFAT‑compliant, and application-ready file.
Accepted for digital upload in online passport applications, and suitable for professional printing if required.
Your Final Australian Passport Photo from PhotoGov

PhotoGov automatically applies the official parameters to your original photo. You don’t need to adjust or verify any technical details manually. Below are the technical parameters of your final Australian passport photo from PhotoGov.
For a full overview of official standards, please see our Australian Passport Photo Requirements Guide.

children.innerHtml: Your photo is processed in a private session in a secure environment. Facial features are never altered — our Australian passport photo checker only resizes, crops, and replaces the background. If you want extra reassurance, optional Human Verification is available at checkout.

Why Use the PhotoGov Service
Convenience
Photos accepted for online and in-person submissions
Compliance-Aligned Output
Designed to meet the current DFAT photo specs
Availability
No registration, installation, or studio visits
Extra Assurance
Optional Human Verification by an in-house compliance specialist
Secure Processing
Your data is secure and not transferred to third parties
PhotoGov and DFAT Standards for Australian ID Pictures

PhotoGov adheres to the ID specifications issued by the Australian Passport Office, as well as the international rules for biometric images defined in ICAO Document 9303. Official guidelines are automatically applied to our Australian passport photo template and are manually updated by our ID photo and compliance experts on a regular basis.

Our online service is built to meet all current rules established by the Australian Passport Office. The image created through our service follows all critical parameters: the correct size 35–40 × 45–50 mm, 32–36 mm face scale, proper centering within the frame, light-coloured background, and even lighting. The platform processes the original portrait without modifying facial features. The final file can be downloaded in a digital or printable format, in under 30 seconds from the selfie upload.

For users who require an additional layer of certainty, we offer the Human Verification service — a manual review performed by a senior compliance expert. This optional step is helpful for applications that must meet strict acceptance criteria or need rapid approval.
Photo Rules for Australian Visas
A visa application follows a separate standard. The Australia visa photo requirements page describes the 35-40 mm by 45-50 mm image on a plain light grey background.

To make a compliant ID photo with your iPhone, follow these simple steps:<\/p>

Stand about 1-1.5 meters from the camera in front of a plain, light, non\u2011textured wall, making sure the whole head and upper shoulders fit into the frame.<\/p>

Use natural daylight from a window or soft, even indoor lighting, avoiding strong backlight, harsh shadows on the face, and any colour casts from lamps.<\/p>

Hold the phone at eye level or place it on a stable surface, look straight into the camera with a neutral expression, keep your mouth closed, and remove hats, sunglasses, and large accessories that cover the face.<\/p>

Take several photos to choose the sharpest one, checking that your face is in focus, eyes are clearly visible, and the background looks clean and evenly lit.<\/p>

It is very convenient when you\u2019ve saved your Australian passport photo from PhotoGov in a printable format.<\/p>"},{"q":"Can you Smile in Australian Passport Photo?","a":"

No. You cannot smile or show any exaggerated emotions, such as frowning or raising eyebrows, in the official ID images. You must look directly into the camera with a neutral expression. Your mouth should be closed and your eyes open.<\/p>"}]

schemaOrg: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"FAQPage","mainEntity":[{"@type":"Question","name":"What Is the Easiest Way to Take an Australian Passport Photo at Home and Edit It Online for Free to Meet All Rules?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"The easiest way to take an Australian passport photo at home and edit it online for free to meet all rules is to use convenient tools like PhotoGov.This is how to use our Australian photo checker, step-by-step:Take a clear selfie against a plain, light‑coloured background, making sure your face is fully visible, and you are looking straight at the camera.Browse PhotoGov.net on your desktop or smartphone, choose “Australia – Passport”, and upload your picture.Wait for about 30 seconds — the tool will automatically crop and resize the image, adjust head position and margins, and prepare a digital file or printable that meets theDepartment of Foreign Affairs and Tradephoto standards."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"How Can I Make an Australian Passport Photo Online for Free Without Installing Any Apps and Then Order Prints?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"You can make an Australian passport photo online for free without installing any apps by using PhotoGov. It is available in any browser, without app installation or registration.Take a selfie in good light, looking directly into the camera, with your shoulders square in the shotBrowse PhotoGov.net on your phone, tablet, or computerSelect “Australia – Passport” as your document typeUpload your photo and follow the on-screen instructionsThe system will format it to the correct size, crop, and background for an Australian passportDownload the high‑resolution file and print it on high-quality photo paper at home, or at a local print shop."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Where Can I Create an Australian Passport Photo Online for Free That Fully Meets Official Department of Home Affairs Requirements?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"You can use free online passport photo editors that specifically support Australian passport standards to create a compliant image from a picture taken with your phone or camera. These tools rely on a built‑in Australian passport photo template that converts your portrait to the official size (35–40 mm × 45–50 mm) and automatically applies the correct dimensions, background colour, head size, positioning, and framing rules. The result is a technically compliant file that you can download for digital use or printing, although final acceptance is always at the discretion of the Department of Home Affairs."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Where Can I Upload a Photo and Get a Free Australian Passport Photo Template Ready for Printing on Standard Photo Paper?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"You can upload your image to an online Australian passport photo editor that prepares a ready‑to‑print template for standard photo paper. Once you upload your image and select “Australia – Passport”, the tool will apply all the necessary technical parameters. After your original image has been processed, you can save a high‑quality digital copy suitable for both online lodgement and professional prints."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Which Online Service Offers Free Australian Passport Photo Checks to Ensure My Picture Will Be Accepted?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"PhotoGov offers free automatic checks for Australian passport photos. The process is simple: you upload your selfie to our platform, and our Australian passport photo checker compares it to an Australian passport photo template stored in our system based on all the recent Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade standards.This automatic check converts your original photo into an official Australian passport photograph. The accuracy and technical compliance are guaranteed by our service if your original photo has been shot according to the rules (it is a sharp, well-lit image without harsh shadows, with your head and shoulders squared in the frame, looking directly into the camera with a neutral expression, taken against a plain light background)."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"How to Take Passport Size Photo From iPhone?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"To make a compliant ID photo with your iPhone, follow these simple steps:Stand about 1-1.5 meters from the camera in front of a plain, light, non‑textured wall, making sure the whole head and upper shoulders fit into the frame.Use natural daylight from a window or soft, even indoor lighting, avoiding strong backlight, harsh shadows on the face, and any colour casts from lamps.Hold the phone at eye level or place it on a stable surface, look straight into the camera with a neutral expression, keep your mouth closed, and remove hats, sunglasses, and large accessories that cover the face.Take several photos to choose the sharpest one, checking that your face is in focus, eyes are clearly visible, and the background looks clean and evenly lit.After that, upload your best photo to any reliable online passport‑photo editor that supports Australian passport official requirements, and let the tool crop, resize, and place it into a passport‑size template for digital use or printing."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"How To Resize Photo To Australian Passport Size?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"You can resize your photo with the PhotGov Australian passport photo checker. children.innerHtml: PhotoGov is an independent service. We are not affiliated with any government, embassy, or consulate. All information on this website is based on official government requirements and verified primary sources. Final acceptance is determined solely by the issuing authority.
Turn Your Selfie into an Australian Visa Photo
Create an Australian visa photo without leaving your home: just upload your selfie to our online photo editor, and it will convert it into a visa-ready picture. Just follow the on-screen steps below.
Get photo for: Australia Visa 35x45 mm (3.5x4.5 cm)
If you need assistance, don't hesitate to contact our Support team, which is always there to help.
How Our Australia Visa Photo Tool Works

PhotoGov is a software‑based visa photo tool with a built‑in Australian visa photo template. It automatically adjusts your portrait to current DFAT‑derived standards for size, head position, and background, and produces a submission‑ready image for online upload or printing. You can also add optional services such as business‑style clothing adjustment or Human Verification of your final photo.

children.innerHtml: What is an Australia Visa Photo?
The official photo format required for an Australian visa application.
Automatically prepared by PhotoGov as a correctly sized, DFAT‑compliant, and submission-ready file.
Accepted for digital upload in online visa applications, and suitable for professional printing if required.
Your Final Australian Visa Photo from PhotoGov

PhotoGov automatically applies the official parameters to your original photo. You don’t need to adjust or verify any technical details manually. Below are the technical parameters of your final Australian visa photo from PhotoGov.

children.innerHtml: Our service is built to meet all current Australian visa photo rules. However, the final acceptance of your photo is always at the full discretion of the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT).
PhotoGov and DFAT Standards for Australian ID Pictures

PhotoGov is a software‑based visa photo tool with a built‑in Australian visa template aligned with DFAT and ICAO photo rules. The official standards are regularly reviewed and manually approved by an in‑house team of ID‑photo and compliance specialists. When you upload a portrait, PhotoGov applies the required parameters for size, centering, and background while preserving your natural facial features and not altering your face in any way. The tool then produces a submission‑ready digital or printable photo for your Australian visa application.

Australian visa applications are assessed under very strict technical rules, so you can enable Human Verification: a senior specialist manually checks that your image complies with all current Australian visa photo requirements before you submit it.
For other Singapore document services, see our dedicated pages: Australia Passport Photo Tool.
Frequently Asked Questions

attributes.model:
[{"q":"Can I Make an Australian Visa Photo Online for Free?","a":"

Yes. You can create a compliant Australian visa photo online at no cost by uploading a portrait to an Australian visa photo tool, letting it automatically crop and format the image to 35 × 45 mm with the correct head size and background, and then downloading the standard digital file for your application.

"},{"q":"What is an Australian Visa Photo Maker?","a":"

An Australian visa photo maker is an online tool that takes a simple portrait and converts it into a 35 × 45 mm image with a 32–36 mm head height, plain light grey background, and correct framing for Australian visa applications.

"},{"q":"Is it Really Free to Make an Australian Visa Photo with PhotoGov?","a":"

Yes. With PhotoGov, you can upload your portrait, have it automatically formatted to the Australian visa photo size, background, crop, and other essential requirements, and download a standard digital file for free. You only pay if you add extras such as Human Verification, business clothing adjustment, or printed copies.

"},{"q":"What is the Size of Australian Visa Photo?","a":"

An Australian visa photo size is 35 × 45 mm — it must fall within the official 35–40 mm by 45–50 mm range, with the head measuring about 32–36 mm from chin to crown and taking roughly 70–80% of the image.

"},{"q":"Can I use a Selfie in My Australian Visa Picture?","a":"

Yes, but only if it is taken correctly and processed by a professional service like PhotoGov that enforces DFAT‑aligned rules for size, crop, head positioning, background, and framing.

"},{"q":"How to Make an Australian Visa Photo Online for Free?","a":"

Take a photo in good daylight against a plain light or light grey background, upload it to an Australian visa photo editor, select the document type, let the system crop and adjust the image, and then download the ready digital file for ImmiAccount or printing.

"},{"q":"Can I Print My Free Australian Visa Photo at a Local Store?","a":"

Yes. Once you have a correctly formatted 35 × 45 mm file with the proper head size, you can send it to any photo lab, pharmacy photo counter, or print kiosk and ask them to print it on high‑quality photo paper.

"},{"q":"Is a Free Online Australian Visa Photo Accepted by the Embassy?","a":"

Yes. It can be accepted on the same basis as a studio photo, provided it meets all technical rules: 35–40 × 45–50 mm size, 32–36 mm head height, plain light grey background, neutral expression, no digital retouching, and good print or file quality.

"},{"q":"Do I Need a Different Photo for Each Australian Visa Type?","a":"

No, different Australian visa subclasses require the same characteristics —  35–40 × 45–50 mm size, 32–36 mm head height, plain light grey background, neutral expression. The photo must be taken within the past six months, reflecting your current appearance.

"},{"q":"Can I Edit the Background Before Uploading My Australian Visa Photo?","a":"

You may only remove distractions and make the background uniformly light; any editing that reshapes facial features, smooths skin, applies beauty filters, or changes colours unnaturally is not acceptable.

"},{"q":"How Do I Know if My Australian Visa Photo Is Compliant?","a":"

There are two ways to know if your Australian visa photo is compliant:
1. Manually check that the final image size is 35–40 × 45–50 mm, the head height is 32–36 mm, the background is plain light grey, and your face is neutral and unobstructed.

2. Use an online visa photo tool to automatically adjust your portrait to an Australian visa photo that follows DFAT rules. This is a reliable option, as reputable services use built‑in templates based on official Australian visa photo specifications. PhotoGov additionally offers Human Verification, where a senior expert manually confirms that your photo meets current Australian visa photo rules before you submit it.

"}]

children.innerHtml: Our platform is built to meet all official infant, baby, and child passport photo rules. However, the final acceptance of your photo is always at the full discretion of the issuing authority — for example, the U.S. Department of State for the U.S. baby passport photos.
PhotoGov and International Standards for Baby Passport Photos

PhotoGov is a passport photo-making tool built to create compliance-aligned baby passport photos. We strictly follow the U.S. Department of State and other key international authorities' child passport photo rules, and our built-in templates adhere to the biometric guidelines of the International Civil Aviation Organization Document 9303. All official passport photo guidelines are regularly monitored and updated by our compliance team.

For US baby passport photos, the images produced by our online passport photo maker tool are tailored to the 2 x 2-inch (600 x 600 to 1,200 x 1,200-pixel) format with a 1 – 1⅜ inches, 50-69% of the image head size, centered in the frame, and a plain white/off-white background with soft, even lighting. Background and lighting cause many rejections. The page on even lighting and background in photos shows exactly what the validator checks.

Your baby passport photo is adjusted only in terms of size, crop, and background — the facial features are not altered in any way. The final file is prepared for printing or digital submission in just a few seconds.

If your child’s visa, ID, or passport photo application is time-sensitive, or you just want an extra level of assurance, select our Human Verification service upon checkout. Our senior compliance specialist will manually review your infant's photo against the latest official requirements of your selected document. This option is particularly suitable for applications or situations where a rejection would cause significant inconvenience.
For other U.S. ID photos, see our dedicated tools: US Passport Photo Maker, US Visa Photo Tool, DV Lottery Photo Tool, US Green Card Photo Tool, US Digital Passport Photo Tool.

[{"q":"Can I Make a Bangladesh Passport Size Photo Online for Free?","a":"

Yes, you can make a Bangladesh passport-size photo online for free. Upload a clear photo to PhotoGov by choosing “Bangladesh” → “Passport Photo,” and download the finished passport photo without installing an app. Human Verification and other optional extras are charged only if you add them.

"},{"q":"How Do I Take a Bangladesh MRP Photo at Home?","a":"

Ask someone to take a photo of you or use a tripod and a timer for a more reliable result, using the rear, not the selfie camera. Stand at a well-lit spot against a plain, light backdrop. Look directly at the camera with a neutral expression, keep both eyes open, and turn off filters or portrait effects. Click a few photos, choose the best one, and upload it to PhotoGov. It will make all the necessary adjustments, apply a 45 x 55 mm crop, light grey background, and produce an application-ready digital or printable file.

"},{"q":"How Do I Convert a Photo to Passport Size Online?","a":"

Upload the original full-resolution image to a free Bangladesh passport size photo converter. It detects the face, crops the picture to 45 x 55 mm, centres the head, prepares the light grey background, and creates the final file for online or in-person submission.

"},{"q":"Does PhotoGov Work as a Bangladesh Passport Size Photo Checker?","a":"

Yes. Our automated Bangladesh passport photo checker reviews the dimensions, head position, framing, background, lighting, sharpness, and facial visibility. If the source photo is of sufficient quality, PhotoGov prepares the final file automatically; if it is too blurred, dark, or distorted, you will need to upload a better photo. Human Verification adds a manual check by a compliance specialist.

"},{"q":"What Does “PP Size Photo” Mean in Bangladesh?","a":"

“PP size photo” is a common shorthand for “passport-size photo” in Bangladesh. The phrase does not always identify the dimensions, so check the form or mission instructions before printing. On this page, PP size means the 45 x 55 mm Bangladesh passport format.

"},{"q":"Can I Use This Tool for a Child’s Bangladesh Passport Photo?","a":"

Use this tool only if the passport office or mission specifically asks for a 45 x 55 mm child photo. Under the official e-passport process, the face image is normally taken during enrolment; for children under 6, a separate 3R photo may be requested instead. Follow the instructions for the child’s age and application route. When 45 x 55 mm is required, Human Verification can add a manual compliance check.

"},{"q":"Can I Print the Bangladesh Passport Size Photo?","a":"

Yes. Choose the printable option to download a PDF with the 45 x 55 mm photos. Print at 100% or actual size on photo paper, without “fit to page” or further resizing. You can print it at home on photo paper or send the file to a copy shop for professional printing.

"},{"q":"What Does Human Verification Add to a Bangladesh Passport Photo?","a":"

Human Verification adds a manual review by a PhotoGov compliance specialist. The reviewer checks the 45 x 55 mm dimensions, head position, background, lighting, sharpness, and facial visibility, then confirms the file is ready or asks you to upload a better source photo. It is especially useful for child photos, previous rejections, or applications with a tight deadline.

"},{"q":"What Should I Do If My Bangladesh Passport Photo Is Rejected?","a":"

Read the reason first. If it concerns blur, shadows, pose, or facial visibility, take a new source photo. If a rejection is caused by a technical problem on PhotoGov’s side, we provide a free retake or refund under the applicable terms. Contact our Support team, and we will help.

"},{"q":"Can I Use a BD Passport Size Photo Maker on My Phone?","a":"

Yes. The BD passport size photo maker works in a mobile browser on iPhone and Android, so there is no app to install. Upload the original camera image rather than a screenshot or a version compressed by a messaging app, then download the finished photo to your phone.

"},{"q":"Can I Use a Selfie for a Bangladesh Passport Photo?","a":"

Yes. But it has to be taken correctly. A close arm’s-length selfie can distort the face and make the head look too large. For the best result, ask someone else to take the picture, or use the rear camera with a timer and place the phone at eye level. Keep the camera straight, step back, and turn off portrait mode, filters, and beauty settings.

"},{"q":"Is My Photo and Personal Data Safe With PhotoGov?","a":"

Yes. PhotoGov handles uploaded information under its current Security and Privacy policies. The Privacy Policy explains what data is collected, how it is used, when it may be disclosed, and how long it is retained.

"},{"q":"Is PhotoGov Part of the Bangladesh Government?","a":"

No. PhotoGov is an independent photo-preparation service. It does not submit, assess, approve, or issue a Bangladesh passport; it only prepares the photo file. The Bangladesh passport office or mission processing the application makes the final decision.

"}]

Stand at a well-lit spot against a plain, light backdrop. Look directly at the camera with a neutral expression, keep both eyes open, and turn off filters or portrait effects. Click a few photos, choose the best one, and upload it to PhotoGov. It will make all the necessary adjustments, apply a 45 x 55 mm crop, light grey background, and produce an application-ready digital or printable file."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"How Do I Convert a Photo to Passport Size Online?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Upload the original full-resolution image to a free Bangladesh passport size photo converter. It detects the face, crops the picture to 45 x 55 mm, centres the head, prepares the light grey background, and creates the final file for online or in-person submission."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Does PhotoGov Work as a Bangladesh Passport Size Photo Checker?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes. Our automated Bangladesh passport photo checker reviews the dimensions, head position, framing, background, lighting, sharpness, and facial visibility. Human Verification adds a manual check by a compliance specialist."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"What Does “PP Size Photo” Mean in Bangladesh?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"“PP size photo” is a common shorthand for “passport-size photo” in Bangladesh. The phrase does not always identify the dimensions, so check the form or mission instructions before printing. On this page, PP size means the 45 x 55 mm Bangladesh passport format."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Can I Use This Tool for a Child’s Bangladesh Passport Photo?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Use this tool only if the passport office or mission specifically asks for a 45 x 55 mm child photo. Follow the instructions for the child’s age and application route. When 45 x 55 mm is required, Human Verification can add a manual compliance check."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Can I Print the Bangladesh Passport Size Photo?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes. Choose the printable option to download a PDF with the 45 x 55 mm photos. Print at 100% or actual size on photo paper, without “fit to page” or further resizing. You can print it at home on photo paper or send the file to a copy shop for professional printing."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"What Does Human Verification Add to a Bangladesh Passport Photo?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Human Verification adds a manual review by a PhotoGov compliance specialist. It is especially useful for child photos, previous rejections, or applications with a tight deadline."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"What Should I Do If My Bangladesh Passport Photo Is Rejected?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Read the reason first. children.innerHtml: What Is a Canadian Citizenship Photo?
The official biometric photo format required for Canadian citizenship applications, certificates, and proof of citizenship submissions.
Automatically prepared by PhotoGov as a correctly sized, application-ready sample, aligned with IRCC standards.
Suitable as a reference for digital upload to the online citizenship application, or professional printing for in-person and mail-in applications.
Your Canada Citizenship Photo Sample from PhotoGov

PhotoGov automatically applies all official IRCC technical requirements to your original photo. The sample image is ready as a layout template and doesn't require any adjustments from you. Below are the key technical parameters of your Canada citizenship photo sample from PhotoGov.
For a full overview of official standards, please see our Canada Citizenship Photo Requirements Guide.

children.innerHtml: Our platform is designed to align with IRCC citizenship photo rules. Final acceptance is determined by the citizenship officer reviewing your application. IRCC requires that printed citizenship photos include studio details (full name, photographer's or studio's name, studio address, and date) on the back of one image.
PhotoGov and IRCC Standards for Citizenship Photos

IRCC sets its own detailed rules for Canadian citizenship photos, and PhotoGov is built to follow those requirements together with the biometric principles laid out in ICAO Doc 9303. Our team keeps track of IRCC updates and adjusts the underlying templates and technical settings whenever the official specifications change, so the citizenship photo format in the tool stays current. Permanent resident cards use the same 50 x 70 mm print, and our Canada PR card photo requirements guide sets out the rest.

For Canadian citizenship applications, PhotoGov generates sample images in the 50 × 70 mm (2 × 2¾ inch / 420 × 540 px) format with a head size of 31–36 mm, centred in the frame, and a plain white or light‑coloured background with even, shadow‑free lighting. The tool only standardises size, crop, and background; it does not alter or enhance any facial features. The resulting sample file is ready to be printed on compliant photo paper or attached to a digital application in just a few seconds.

If you want additional reassurance, you can add Human Verification. In this mode, a senior compliance specialist checks your image against the latest IRCC citizenship photo instructions before you submit your application. This is particularly helpful for urgent timelines, citizenship applications for children, or cases where a retake would be difficult or cause delays.
For other Canadian document photos, see our dedicated tools: Canada Passport Photo Tool, Canada Visa Photo Tool, Canada PR Card Photo Tool, Canada Study Permit Photo Tool.

[{"q":"Can I Get My Canada Citizenship Photo Online for Free?","a":"

Yes \u2014 services like PhotoGov let you get a Canadian citizenship photo sample online for free. Just upload your selfie, choose \"Canada\" \u2192 \"Citizenship Photo 50 \u00d7 70 mm\" as your document type, and download your ready-to-apply sample. The first photo is free in most countries; in the US, UK, and Canada, our affordable pricing<\/a> applies. Keep in mind that IRCC only accepts photos signed by a studio for citizenship applications, so you may only use the photo that you\u2019ve produced online as a reference.<\/p>"},{"q":"How Do I Convert a Photo to 50 \u00d7 70 mm Citizenship Size Online for Free?","a":"

You can use a reliable online passport photo editor to convert your photo into the official 50 \u00d7 70 mm (2 \u00d7 2\u00be inch \/ 420 \u00d7 540 px) Canada citizenship format. You need to upload your photo to the online photo maker, and it will automatically resize, crop, and apply a plain white or light-coloured background. At PhotoGov, the first conversion is free in most countries; in the US, UK, and Canada, our affordable pricing<\/a> applies. No registration or installation required.<\/p>"},{"q":"How Do I Resize a Photo to the Official Canada Citizenship Size Online?","a":"

To resize a photo to the official Canada citizenship size, use a reliable Canada citizenship photo resizer such as PhotoGov. Upload your image to our online Canada citizenship photo tool, and the system will automatically detect your face, crop the frame, adjust head size and margins, set a plain white background, and instantly generate a 50 \u00d7 70 mm (420 \u00d7 540 px) sample file suitable for both printing and digital submission. No manual editing required.<\/p>"},{"q":"How to Edit a Citizenship Photo Online for Free?","a":"

You can use a reliable citizenship photo editor online for free by uploading your selfie and letting the tool adjust it to all official specifications \u2014 resize, reframe, crop, and apply a plain white or light-coloured background.<\/p>"},{"q":"Will My 420 \u00d7 540-Pixel File Be Accepted for the Online Citizenship Application?","a":"

Yes. A 420 \u00d7 540-pixel JPG\/JPEG file meets the technical specs of the online IRCC citizenship application<\/a> and will be accepted if you provide a studio confirmation letter. It must contain the following information:<\/p>

Applicant\u2019s name<\/p>

Applicant\u2019s date of birth<\/p>

The date the photo was taken<\/p>

Full studio\u2019s name<\/p>

Full studio\u2019s address<\/p>"},{"q":"Where Do I Get the Studio Signature on the Back of My Photo?","a":"

At any commercial photo studio \u2014 that's the only source IRCC accepts. After you generate your Canada citizenship photo sample with PhotoGov, take the printable file (or just the layout reference) to a local studio. They print on photo paper and either stamp or handwrite their full name, address, and the date the photo was taken on the back of one of the two prints. The applicant's full name is also added to the back.<\/p>"},{"q":"Can I Take My Canadian Citizenship Photo at Home?","a":"

You can take a selfie at home and use an online passport photo maker to format it into an IRCC-aligned sample. To complete the application, however, the printed photo still has to go through a commercial studio for paper-grade printing and the studio signature on the back. Home printer outputs are not accepted by IRCC.<\/p>"},{"q":"Is Human Verification Available for My Canada Citizenship Photo?","a":"

Yes. A senior PhotoGov compliance specialist reviews your sample against the current IRCC citizenship photo specs and the IRCC-published examples of acceptable and unacceptable photos before you take the file to a studio. Particularly useful close to a deadline, with a child applicant, or with anything borderline \u2014 religious head covering, medical glasses, hair partially covering the face.<\/p>"},{"q":"Do I Need a Studio Stamp on the Back of My Canada Citizenship Photo?","a":"

Yes \u2014 for printed Canada citizenship applications, IRCC requires that the back of one photo include the applicant's full name, the photographer's or studio's name, the studio address, and the date the photo was taken. The information may be handwritten or stamped. For online citizenship applications with a digital photo, studio details are usually provided as a separate file (a studio letter and a receipt). PhotoGov generates a print-ready sample, and the studio signature is added by the commercial studio that prints your photo.<\/p>"},{"q":"Is My Personal Data and Photo Safe With PhotoGov?","a":"

Yes. We treat your personal data and images with great care. PhotoGov uses your information solely to generate an official ID photo sample and deletes it from our servers once the process is complete. We never share your data with third parties or external AI services. If you have any questions, you can always contact our Customer Support<\/a> team or read more details in our Privacy Policy<\/a>.<\/p>"},{"q":"Is There an Official IRCC Citizenship Photo Tool?","a":"

IRCC does not provide an official online citizenship photo maker; instead, it publishes detailed photo specifications and a list of acceptable and unacceptable examples on the Government of Canada website. Our PhotoGov tool is built around these official specifications, and features a more user-friendly interface and a broader range of services. Besides the regular photo maker options, you can add Human Verification \u2014 and our compliance and ID photo experts will manually review your photo, giving you an extra layer of assurance before the application<\/b>.<\/p>"}]

schemaOrg: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"FAQPage","mainEntity":[{"@type":"Question","name":"Can I Get My Canada Citizenship Photo Online for Free?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes — services like PhotoGov let you get a Canadian citizenship photo sample online for free. Just upload your selfie, choose \"Canada\" → \"Citizenship Photo 50 × 70 mm\" as your document type, and download your ready-to-apply sample. The first photo is free in most countries; in the US, UK, and Canada, our affordable pricing applies. Keep in mind that IRCC only accepts photos signed by a studio for citizenship applications, so you may only use the photo that you’ve produced online as a reference."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"How Do I Convert a Photo to 50 × 70 mm Citizenship Size Online for Free?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"You can use a reliable online passport photo editor to convert your photo into the official 50 × 70 mm (2 × 2¾ inch / 420 × 540 px) Canada citizenship format. You need to upload your photo to the online photo maker, and it will automatically resize, crop, and apply a plain white or light-coloured background. At PhotoGov, the first conversion is free in most countries; in the US, UK, and Canada, our affordable pricing applies. No registration or installation required."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"How Do I Resize a Photo to the Official Canada Citizenship Size Online?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"To resize a photo to the official Canada citizenship size, use a reliable Canada citizenship photo resizer such as PhotoGov. Upload your image to our online Canada citizenship photo tool, and the system will automatically detect your face, crop the frame, adjust head size and margins, set a plain white background, and instantly generate a 50 × 70 mm (420 × 540 px) sample file suitable for both printing and digital submission. No manual editing required."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"How to Edit a Citizenship Photo Online for Free?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"You can use a reliable citizenship photo editor online for free by uploading your selfie and letting the tool adjust it to all official specifications — resize, reframe, crop, and apply a plain white or light-coloured background."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Will My 420 × 540-Pixel File Be Accepted for the Online Citizenship Application?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes. A 420 × 540-pixel JPG/JPEG file meets the technical specs of the online IRCC citizenship application and will be accepted if you provide a studio confirmation letter. It must contain the following information:Applicant’s nameApplicant’s date of birthThe date the photo was takenFull studio’s nameFull studio’s address"}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Where Do I Get the Studio Signature on the Back of My Photo?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"At any commercial photo studio — that's the only source IRCC accepts. After you generate your Canada citizenship photo sample with PhotoGov, take the printable file (or just the layout reference) to a local studio. They print on photo paper and either stamp or handwrite their full name, address, and the date the photo was taken on the back of one of the two prints. The applicant's full name is also added to the back."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Can I Take My Canadian Citizenship Photo at Home?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"You can take a selfie at home and use an online passport photo maker to format it into an IRCC-aligned sample. To complete the application, however, the printed photo still has to go through a commercial studio for paper-grade printing and the studio signature on the back. Home printer outputs are not accepted by IRCC."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Is Human Verification Available for My Canada Citizenship Photo?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes. A senior PhotoGov compliance specialist reviews your sample against the current IRCC citizenship photo specs and the IRCC-published examples of acceptable and unacceptable photos before you take the file to a studio. Particularly useful close to a deadline, with a child applicant, or with anything borderline — religious head covering, medical glasses, hair partially covering the face."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Do I Need a Studio Stamp on the Back of My Canada Citizenship Photo?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes — for printed Canada citizenship applications, IRCC requires that the back of one photo include the applicant's full name, the photographer's or studio's name, the studio address, and the date the photo was taken. The information may be handwritten or stamped. For online citizenship applications with a digital photo, studio details are usually provided as a separate file (a studio letter and a receipt). PhotoGov generates a print-ready sample, and the studio signature is added by the commercial studio that prints your photo."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Is My Personal Data and Photo Safe With PhotoGov?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes. We never share your data with third parties or external AI services. If you have any questions, you can always contact our Customer Support team or read more details in our Privacy Policy."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Is There an Official IRCC Citizenship Photo Tool?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"IRCC does not provide an official online citizenship photo maker; instead, it publishes detailed photo specifications and a list of acceptable and unacceptable examples on the Government of Canada website. children.innerHtml: What is a Canadian Passport Photo?
The official biometric photo format required for a Canadian passport.
Automatically prepared by PhotoGov as an IRCC-compliant photo template.
Properly formatted, framed, and sized photo, useful for Canadian passport photo preparation.
Your Canadian Passport Photo Template from PhotoGov

PhotoGov automatically applies key IRCC technical requirements to your original photo. The final image that you get is a template with technical parameters already set, so you don’t need to adjust the size or crop manually. Below are the key technical parameters for your final Canada passport photo from PhotoGov.
For a full overview of official standards, please see our Canadian Passport Photo Requirements Guide.

IRCC Canada Passport Photo Template from PhotoGov

PhotoGov applies the official IRCC Canada passport photo specifications to every uploaded image and generates sample Canada photos that meet all current requirements for size, crop, head proportion, and background layout. Our official template database is continuously updated to reflect current Government of Canada passport photo rules and is manually reviewed by our specialists.
The output is a technically compliant reference file that helps users understand the exact Canada passport photo layout before obtaining the final photo, as required by the Government of Canada.
Permanent Resident Card Photos
A PR card photo follows different digital specifications from a passport photo. Full requirements for that document: https://photogov.net/knowledge/requirements/pr-card-photo-requirements/
Photos for Canadian Citizenship
Citizenship applications follow their own specification. Our Canada citizenship application photo requirements 2026 guide sets out the size, head height, and background rules.
Frequently Asked Questions

[{"q":"Can I Make a Canadian Photo Online for Free?","a":"

Yes, you can make a Canadian photo online for free using a reliable free Canadian passport photo maker. But keep in mind that the final photo produced with an online tool can only be used as a sample, as the IRCC (Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada) accepts the originals taken at photo studios with a studio signature on the back of the photo (or as a letter that is attached to your online passport renewal application). Learn more from our Complete Canada passport photo requirements 2026 Guide<\/a>.<\/p>"},{"q":"Can I Take My Own Passport Photo in Canada?","a":"

You can take your own photo and use a free Canadian passport photo maker to create the correct layout and size. However, the passport photo you submit with your application must still meet IRCC rules for professional capture or studio processing, photographic-paper printing for physical applications, and studio details on the back of the photo.<\/p>"},{"q":"What Does the Canada Passport Photo Checker Do?","a":"

Canada passport photo checker verifies that your image follows the official Canadian passport photo rules for both print and digital submissions. It checks that the final photo that you prepare follows all IRCC standards:<\/p>

50 \u00d7 70 mm (or 1,200 \u00d7 1,800 to 3,000 \u00d7 4,500 pixels) photo size<\/p>

31-36 mm head height<\/p>

Plain, white, off-white, or light-coloured background<\/p>

Centered crop<\/p>

JPEG format<\/p>

200 KB-5 MB file size.<\/p>

After the photo is prepared with an online Canada passport photo checker, it must be professionally printed and signed by a photo studio.<\/p>"},{"q":"Can I Create a Canada Passport Photo Online for Free, and Then Print It?","a":"

Yes. You can use a Canada passport photo online free tool to create the correctly formatted file, and then get it professionally printed by a commercial photo service.<\/p>"},{"q":"How Fast Can I Get a Canada Passport Photo Online?","a":"

Online passport photo makers generate a Canadian passport photo template within a few seconds. All you need is to upload a recent portrait, choose \u201cCanada\u201d as your country and \u201cPassport\u201d as your document type, and wait until the tool processes your image, adjusting it to the official IRCC rules. With PhotoGov, the process takes around 30 seconds.<\/p>"},{"q":"What is the Correct Canada Passport Photo Size?","a":"

The correct Canada passport photo size for paper applications is 50 x 70 mm, with your face measuring between 31 mm and 36 mm from chin to crown. For an online passport renewal, you must submit a digital image measuring 1,200 \u00d7 1,800 to 3,000 \u00d7 4,500 pixels. The Canadian passport photo size in cm is 5 \u00d7 7 cm.<\/p>"},{"q":"Can You Take Canadian Passport Photos at Home?","a":"

You can take a selfie at home, upload it to a Canada passport photo editor online for free, and get a digital or a printable file. Reliable tools like PhotoGov use a built-in IRCC template \u2014\u00a0and adjust your original photo to all official requirements, including crop, framing, positioning, background, and colour profile. To submit the photo with your passport application, you must print it on photo paper at a commercial studio (which must sign the back of the photo).<\/p>"},{"q":"What is the Required Digital Size for a Canada Passport Photo?","a":"

A required digital size for a Canada passport photo is from 1,200 \u00d7 1,800 to 3,000 \u00d7 4,500 pixels. The file size must be at least 200 KB and 5 MB maximum. Canadian passport digital photos are only used for online passport renewals \u2014\u00a0first-time passport applications and mail-in submissions require two identical prints.<\/p>"},{"q":"Why Use Canada Passport Photo Editor Online for Free?","a":"

Because it\u2019s the easiest way to create your Canadian passport photo online and get an IRCC- technically aligned template. By using reliable online tools like PhotoGov, you instantly verify the crop, background, and passport photo size in cm \/ mm \/ px before you professionally print it at a studio.<\/p>"},{"q":"Can a Canada Passport Photo Checker Fix Image Mistakes Automatically?","a":"

Yes. A reliable Canada passport photo checker will automatically fix all image errors that contradict the official IRCC rules. If the background is of the wrong color, it will be changed to a plain white, off-white, or light-colored one; if the image size isn\u2019t 50x70 mm, the tool will automatically crop the original portrait to the required dimensions; if the head size falls out of the 31-36 mm range, it will be re-framed to the correct proportions; if the subject is misaligned in the frame, it will be centered in it. The PhotoGov passport photo maker also offers a casual-to-formal clothes change and professional lighting adjustment, preparing a studio-grade image from your original photo that contained mistakes.<\/p>"},{"q":"Does a Canada Passport Photo Checker Guarantee that My Passport Photo Will Be Accepted?","a":"

No. Passport photo checkers only provide image adjustment services and do not guarantee your photo acceptance, as it solely lies in the discretion of the ID issuing authority.<\/p>"},{"q":"Can I Use the Canadian Passport Photo Template for a Visa or a PR Card?","a":"

No. Even though Canada passport and PR card photos both use a printed size of 50 \u00d7 70 mm, they follow different digital specifications and technical rules, so a single template should not be reused for every document. Canadian visa photos use a completely different size \u2014 35 \u00d7 45 mm in print with their own digital dimensions and file limits \u2014 so they always require a separate photo template.<\/p>"}]

For an online passport renewal, you must submit a digital image measuring 1,200 × 1,800 to 3,000 × 4,500 pixels. The Canadian passport photo size in cm is 5 × 7 cm."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Can You Take Canadian Passport Photos at Home?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"You can take a selfie at home, upload it to a Canada passport photo editor online for free, and get a digital or a printable file. To submit the photo with your passport application, you must print it on photo paper at a commercial studio (which must sign the back of the photo)."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"What is the Required Digital Size for a Canada Passport Photo?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"A required digital size for a Canada passport photo is from 1,200 × 1,800 to 3,000 × 4,500 pixels. A reliable Canada passport photo checker will automatically fix all image errors that contradict the official IRCC rules. If the background is of the wrong color, it will be changed to a plain white, off-white, or light-colored one; if the image size isn’t 50x70 mm, the tool will automatically crop the original portrait to the required dimensions; if the head size falls out of the 31-36 mm range, it will be re-framed to the correct proportions; if the subject is misaligned in the frame, it will be centered in it. children.innerHtml: If your photo is rejected due to technical issues on PhotoGov's side, we provide a free retake or a full refund.
Output, Aligned With IRCC Standards for Size, Crop, and Background of PR Card Photos

PhotoGov uses advanced image‑processing technology to check every uploaded photo against the official Canada PR card photo requirements. Our internal database is regularly updated and manually reviewed by our compliance specialists.

When we produce your PR card photo template, we aim for the full technical alignment with the official IRCC photo requirements for size, crop, and background. Citizenship applications run under the same IRCC framework, and PhotoGov keeps a separate guide to the photo rules for that document.

PhotoGov users can choose the optional Human Verification service — a manual review performed by an experienced compliance expert for an extra layer of accuracy and assurance, especially for high‑priority or time‑sensitive PR applications.
Frequently Asked Questions

attributes.model:
[{"q":"What Is the Canada PR Card Photo Editor?","a":"

The Canada PR Card photo editor is an online tool that helps you check, crop, and format an image for Canada PR card photo specifications. It is designed to help you prepare a photo preview based on official IRCC size, framing, and background rules.<\/p>"},{"q":"How Does the Canada PR Photo Editor Work?","a":"

Upload your image, and the Canada PR Photo Checker reviews the photo format, crop, and framing against current PR card photo specifications. It helps you preview how your image should look when adjusted to the required size, head position, and background style.<\/p>"},{"q":"How to Edit a Photo for PR Card?","a":"

To edit a photo for a PR card, you should only adjust technical elements such as crop, alignment, and size so the image matches IRCC\u2019s permanent resident photo specifications. Use a Canada PR card photo editor like PhotoGov to center your face, set the correct 50\u00d770 mm format (or required pixel range for online use), keep a plain white background, and ensure the head height is between 31 mm and 36 mm without retouching your facial features.<\/p>"},{"q":"Can I Upload a Selfie to Check My PR Card Photo?","a":"

Yes, you can upload a selfie to check whether your image adheres to the required PR card photo layout. The PhotoGov passport photo maker can help you preview the crop, face position, and background before you use a final photo for your application.<\/p>"},{"q":"Can I Upload a Studio Photo to Format It for a Canada PR Card?","a":"

Yes, you can upload a studio photo and use the Canada PR Photo Checker to adjust the crop and digital format. This is especially useful when you need a Canada PR photo digital file that matches the required dimensions for upload.<\/p>"},{"q":"What Photo Size Does the Passport Photo Maker Use for Canada PR Card Photos?","a":"

Canada PR card photos use a printed size of 50 mm wide by 70 mm high, and the digital size between 715 \u00d7 1000 and 2000 \u00d7 2800 pixels. The passport photo maker formats your preview exactly to this official PR card photo size and framing standard.<\/p>"},{"q":"Does the Online Photo Checker Set the Correct PR Card Photo Dimensions Automatically?","a":"

Yes, the Canada PR photo checker automatically crops and outputs the digital format between 715\u00d71000 and 2000\u00d72800 pixels, according to the IRCC standards.<\/p>"},{"q":"Can I Crop My Photo to the Correct PR Card Format Online?","a":"

Yes, an online passport photo maker like PhotoGov can help crop your image to match the required PR card framing and proportions. This includes adjusting the image to the official 50 \u00d7 70 mm layout, or 715\u00d71000 and 2000\u00d72800 pixels, with the head size 31-36 mm.<\/p>"},{"q":"Can I Remove or Clean Up the Background of My Canada PR Card Photo?","a":"

Yes. A Canada PR Card photo maker will automatically remove the original backdrop, replacing it with a clean white background, as required by the IRCC.<\/p>"},{"q":"Does the Online Tool Help Position My Face Correctly in the Frame?","a":"

Yes, a reliable PR \u0441ard photo maker automatically centers your face and shoulders in the frame, preparing a template that is technically compliant with the official standards for your PR card photo framing.<\/p>"},{"q":"Can I Make a PR Photo Online?","a":"

You can make a PR photo online as a digital file, but IRCC requires that PR card photos be taken by a commercial studio, with an official confirmation provided as a letter. The digital photo you upload must be a professional\u2011quality image in the required pixel range (715\u00d71000 to 2000\u00d72800 pixels), a file size of 4 MB or less, and an accepted format, JPG or PNG.<\/p>"}]

children.innerHtml: Photo for Canada Permanent Resident Card: 5x7 cm

The most crucial thing you need to do when applying for a Canada Permanent Resident Card is to send in a photo that meets the requirements. For digital purposes, the standard size for the photo is 5x7 cm (or 715x1000 pixels - 2000x2800 pixels). An application with a photo that doesn't meet the requirements could be delayed or even turned down. We make it easier to take a photo for a Canada Permanent Resident Card that meets all the requirements at PhotoGov. We will automatically resize, crop, and optimize your selfie or high-quality photo according to the official guidelines so that you can submit it digitally or physically. Every specification is set out in full on the page with the Canada PR card photo rules, from framing to background.

children.innerHtml: Step-by-Step Guide to Making Your Canada Permanent Resident Card Photo
Choose the Type of Document
On PhotoGov.net, look for the document called "Canada Permanent Resident Card – 5x7 cm"
Get Your Picture
Use a smartphone or digital camera that works well.  Stand 1.5 to 2 meters away from a white or light-colored background.  Make sure the lighting is gentle and even
Put your picture up
Send your picture to PhotoGov.  Make sure the lighting is even and your face is easy to see
Resize and optimize automatically
Our platform will cut your picture down to the exact size of 5x7 cm (715x1000 to 2000x2800 pixels for digital formats) and make it look better
Get it and send it in
Download your final file, which is ready to be sent in, or print it off to hand in in person
Best Ways to Do Things in Canada Photo of a Permanent Resident Card
Lighting: To keep shadows from forming, use natural light or moderate artificial light
Background: Stand in front of a wall that is plain white or light-colored. Stay away from patterns and textures
Positioning: Make sure your face is in the middle and facing straight forward. The head should fill about 70–80% of the height of the picture
Wear dark, solid-colored garments to stand out against the background. Don't wear white tops
How to take your own Canada Permanent Resident Card photo

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect employment authorization photo yourself:
1. Take a picture of yourself

Open up the PhotoGov.net photo service and take your picture. Make sure you’re not wearing any headcovers or glasses, do not wear a uniform, and keep your expression neutral. Ensure that the area is well-lit and that you are standing against a neutral background.

children.innerHtml: 3. Receive your Passport Photo
Finally, you can download your ID photo. These images can be printed off, or you can simply use them as digital photos.
Don't make these mistakes
Using a passport-sized photo instead of the appropriate 5x7 cm (50x70 mm) size
Wearing glasses or hats that cover your face (unless you have to for medical or religious reasons)
Photos that are low resolution, fuzzy, or too bright
Background with patterns, shadows, or things
Smiling or moving your head
During photo processing, PhotoGov will automatically find and fix these problems
More tips for being compliant
No Retouching: Don't use filters or editing programs that change how your face looks
Sharpness: Make sure the picture is crisp and not pixelated or blurry
Face Coverage: Your face should take up 70–80% of the height of the picture
File Format and Size: JPEG or PNG, less than 1 MB for digital submission
How to take Canada Permanent Resident Card photos for babies and kids

When taking pictures of babies and children for employment authorization, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.
Rules for Sending and Printing
For Sending by Mail: Make sure your photo is exactly 5x7 cm (50x70 mm) and print it on high-quality matte or glossy photo paper
To submit digitally, upload your photo to the right portal or consular system. Make sure the file is the right size and resolution

children.innerHtml: Our service is built to meet all current Canadian visa photo rules. However, the final acceptance of your photo is always at the full discretion of the Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC).
Your Canada Visa Photo With PhotoGov & IRCC Standards

PhotoGov is a technology platform powered by advanced software that works as a Canada visa photo editor. The service matches the uploaded image to the official Canadian visa photo specifications stored in the system. The database is regularly updated, and our photo specialists, together with compliance experts, manually review all standards every eight weeks.
Citizenship is a different application: the citizenship photo requirements in Canada call for a larger 50 x 70 mm image.

Our service is built to meet all current requirements set by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC). The photo you create with our service meets all key criteria: correct size (35×45 mm), framing, head position, and lighting. PhotoGov also lets you refine clothing in the image without changing facial features. As a result, you receive a compliant photograph ready to submit with your Canadian visa application. The PR card template is not interchangeable: how to make a PR card photo is explained on its own page.

PhotoGov users can select Human Verification as an add-on service — a detailed manual check performed by an experienced compliance expert. This extra review provides maximum accuracy and is especially useful for applications that require strict official approval or faster processing.
For other Canadian ID photo services, see our dedicated pages: Canada Passport Photo Tool, Canada PR Card Photo Maker, Canada Temporary Resident Visa Photo Maker.
Full Canada Visa Photo Rules
Our Canada visa photo requirements 2026 guide documents the specification behind this page: size, crop, background, and file quality.
Frequently Asked Questions

To get a Canada visa photo size online free, you can upload a regular portrait taken with your phone to a dedicated Canadian visa photo tool, like PhotoGov, and choose \u201cCanada visa 35x45 mm\u201d as the target format. A Canada visa photo tool is an online service or an app that automatically adjusts your picture to official Canadian visa photo standards. You upload your image, choose \u201cCanada visa\u201d as the document type, and the tool sets the canvas to 35x45 mm, adjusts head size, and aligns your eyes within the acceptable area.
