With German and Schengen photo standards
I already have a digital visa photo. How do i print it?

If you have a digital photograph, unfortunately, you won’t just be able to print it out on printer paper. You specifically need a high-quality print on either matte or glossy photo paper. You can either achieve this by visiting any photo service or by using our tool to print your image off at home.
Where to get a visa photo
Pharmacies and drug stores
Well-known medicinal retail brands, namely Walgreens, CVS, and Rite Aid, proffer immediate passport photo solutions in-store. Do anticipate a charge, with most services priced around the $15 mark.
Shipping centers

Shipping giants like UPS, FedEx, and adjacent shipping facilities also cater to passport photo needs, mirroring the services of typical drugstores. At a going rate of around $15, it stands as a worthy alternative if you're considering external providers for your passport imagery.
Post offices and other passport acceptance agents

It's customary for post offices and agencies of a similar function to be equipped for passport applications, which includes offering photographic sessions. Maintaining the price consistency as observed earlier, you can typically expect a fee around the $15 ballpark.
Retail stores

Retail venues frequently host areas meant for passport photo shoots, assuring quality pictures in line with norms. Even though each establishment might set its own rate, you can usually anticipate a decent pricing range.

The page on digital vs printed passport photos sets out where each format is required and why the two sets of rules are not interchangeable.
PhotoGov and the Official Digital Passport Photo Standards

PhotoGov builds its digital passport photo maker around the official specifications published by the U.S. Department of State, together with the biometric framework defined in ICAO Doc 9303. Our team tracks these standards continuously, and whenever a requirement changes, the engineering team updates the processing engine so every template stays current.

A digital passport photo generated through our tool is automatically sized to a 600 × 600 px square canvas, saved as a JPEG file within the accepted file-size range, with the head centered and occupying roughly 50–69% of the frame against a plain white or off-white background under even, shadow-free lighting. Only the size, crop, and background are adjusted — your facial features remain untouched. The finished digital file, ready for online upload, is delivered in under a minute.

If you'd like extra confidence before submitting, our Human Verification service lets a senior compliance specialist manually check your digital photo against the current Department of State template. This is especially useful for online passport renewal, urgent applications, photos of infants or young children, or any case where a rejected file would create real problems.
Need a digital photo for another U.S. document? Explore our other tools: US Visa Photo Tool, DV Lottery Photo Tool, US Green Card Photo Tool.

attributes.model:
[{"q":"How Do I Get a Digital Passport Photo?","a":"

To create a digital passport photo, take a clear, well-lit photo of yourself — or upload one you already have — through the PhotoGov passport photo maker. Select your country, and the tool automatically applies the correct crop, head positioning, background, and file format required for a digital passport photo in that country. Within seconds, you receive a compliant digital passport photo ready to download and upload directly to the relevant application portal.

"},{"q":"Can I Make a Digital Passport Photo Online for Free?","a":"

In most countries, yes — PhotoGov lets you generate and download a compliant digital passport photo at no cost. In the United States, United Kingdom, and Canada, PhotoGov charges a small, transparent fee to cover local compliance checks and support; current pricing for these countries is listed on our Pricing page. Regardless of country, optional add-ons — such as Human Verification by a compliance specialist, additional clothing variations, or extra file formats — are paid services you can add at checkout.

"},{"q":"Where Can I Get a Digital Passport Photo?","a":"

Getting a passport photo online is straightforward — you have three main options: a service like PhotoGov, a local photo studio or pharmacy that offers digital files, or an authority-approved photo provider where your application specifically requires one. PhotoGov is the fastest browser-based route — no appointment, no travel, no waiting in line. Upload a photo, let the tool process it against the correct requirements, and download a ready-to-submit file in under a minute.

"},{"q":"Is an Online Passport Photo Maker a Good Alternative to Passport Photos Near Me?","a":"

Yes, in any case where your application accepts a digital upload rather than a physical print. Searching for passport photos near me usually leads to a pharmacy or studio visit, an appointment, and a per-print fee — useful if you specifically need a physical photo or an authority-issued photo code, but unnecessary overhead for a digital submission. Whether you searched for passport photos near me or passport pictures near me, an online passport photo maker like PhotoGov removes that step entirely: you take the photo yourself, and the tool handles the sizing, cropping, and compliance check a studio would otherwise do manually.

"},{"q":"Can I Take a Digital Passport Photo at Home?","a":"

Yes, and for most applicants it's the simplest option. Use a recent photo taken at eye level in even, natural light, with a plain wall or blank background behind you and no shadows across your face. PhotoGov's tool then handles the technical part — cropping to the correct canvas, resizing the head and shoulders to the required proportions, and adjusting the background to meet the standard. What it can't fix is the source image itself: a blurry photo, an obscured face, sunglasses, or a very low-resolution image will still need to be retaken before processing.

"},{"q":"Can I Use an iPhone or an Android Phone to Make a Digital Passport Photo?","a":"

Yes. PhotoGov runs entirely in your phone's browser, so you can take a new selfie or upload an existing photo from your camera roll on either iOS or Android. There's no separate app to install and no account required — the tool works the same way on a phone, tablet, or desktop computer.

"},{"q":"How Do I Upload a Passport Photo Online?","a":"

Once PhotoGov has processed your photo, download the finished file to a location you can easily find, such as your device's Files or Downloads folder. Then open the official application portal for your document, locate its photo-upload field, select the saved file, and wait for the portal to run its own validation check. If the portal flags an issue with the file's technical properties, our step-by-step Digital photo upload guide covers the most common causes and fixes.

"},{"q":"Does PhotoGov Replace a Passport Photo Scanner?","a":"

For creating a new digital photo, yes — starting from a phone camera image is simpler and produces better results than scanning a print, since scans often pick up paper texture, glare, or color shifts. If a printed passport photo is all you have, scan it in full color at a reasonably high resolution and upload the scan; PhotoGov will still crop and format it correctly. Whenever possible, though, a fresh photo taken directly on your phone gives the processing engine more detail to work with.

"},{"q":"What Is the Difference Between a Digital and a Printable Passport Photo?","a":"

A digital passport photo is a JPEG file sized specifically for an online upload field — it has no physical dimensions until it's printed. A printable passport photo, by contrast, is laid out at an exact physical size (for example, 2×2 inches or 35×45 mm) on a print sheet, ready to be cut and submitted in person or by mail. PhotoGov's digital passport photo maker is built for the online-upload use case; if your application specifically requires a physical print, check your document's pricing page for the printable option before you submit.

"},{"q":"How Long Does the Online Passport Photo-Making Process Take?","a":"

Automatic processing — cropping, resizing, and background adjustment — typically takes about 30 seconds once you've uploaded a suitable photo and selected your country. If you add Human Verification, expect a short additional wait while a compliance specialist manually reviews the result against the current official template before releasing your final file.

"},{"q":"What Does the Digital Passport Photo Tool Change?","a":"

PhotoGov's tool adjusts only the technical properties required for compliance: crop, canvas size, head placement, background color, pixel dimensions, and file format. It never changes your facial features, skin, or expression, and it never generates or synthesizes a new likeness — the person in the final photo is exactly who uploaded it. This matters because most issuing authorities, including the U.S. Department of State, explicitly prohibit digitally altered or retouched ID photos, and PhotoGov's process is built to stay within that boundary.

"},{"q":"What Does PhotoGov Not Do?","a":"

PhotoGov prepares your photo file — it doesn't fill out your passport application, submit it on your behalf, book appointments, issue travel documents, or guarantee approval. Final acceptance always rests with the government agency or consulate reviewing your application; our role is limited to delivering a technically compliant photo file for you to submit yourself.

"},{"q":"Why Must I Select a Country Before Processing?","a":"

Digital passport photo requirements aren't universal — each country sets its own standard. Pixel dimensions, aspect ratio, head-size percentage, background color, and file format can all differ meaningfully from one country's passport photo standard to another's. Selecting your country tells PhotoGov exactly which profile to apply, so the file you download matches the standard your application will actually be checked against.

"},{"q":"Can I Use the Same Digital Passport Photo for Two Applications?","a":"

Only if both applications require the identical technical and biometric profile and the photo is still recent enough to meet each authority's currency requirement (most require a photo taken within the last six months) — for example, two passport renewals processed under the same country's standard. If you're applying in two different countries, each with its own passport photo standard, reprocess your source photo separately under each country's profile rather than reusing one output file; even small differences in crop or head proportion can cause a rejection.

"},{"q":"Can PhotoGov Check My Photo Before I Submit It?","a":"

Yes, in two ways. Every photo automatically goes through PhotoGov's compliance check as part of standard processing, verifying crop, size, background, and other technical requirements against your selected country's standard. For extra confidence, add Human Verification at checkout, and a compliance specialist will personally review your finished photo against the current official template before you download it.

"},{"q":"What If the Government Portal Rejects My Digital Passport Photo?","a":"

Start by reading the portal's exact rejection message — it usually points to a specific technical property, like file size, background color, or head positioning. If the issue relates to something PhotoGov's profile is meant to handle, contact our Support with the error message and your country; if the rejection traces back to a processing error on our side, we'll provide a free retake or a full refund. If the rejection instead concerns your application's eligibility or a rule unrelated to the photo itself, follow the instructions provided by the issuing authority.

"},{"q":"Is My Photo and Personal Data Safe?","a":"

Yes. PhotoGov processes each photo in a private session and does not share your image with third parties as part of the photo-making workflow. For full details on how long files are retained and how your data is handled, see our current Privacy Policy.

"},{"q":"Is PhotoGov a Government Website?","a":"

No. PhotoGov is an independent online service — a passport photo maker, not a government agency. We are not affiliated with any national passport office, embassy, consulate, or issuing authority, including the U.S. Department of State, and we cannot guarantee how any government will rule on your application.

"},{"q":"Where Can I See Digital Passport Photo Examples and Sample Photos?","a":"

If you want to see sample passport photos before you submit, two resources are useful here. Your country's passport-issuing authority typically publishes its own approved examples — for US applicants, that's the Department of State's Digital Passport Photo Page, which you can use to compare your finished photo against official samples. PhotoGov's own Digital passport photo examples article goes further, walking through specific acceptable and rejected photos so you can spot common mistakes before you submit.

"},{"q":"Do I Need Photo-Editing Skills to Make a Digital Passport Photo Online?","a":"

No. PhotoGov's passport photo maker is built for an easy, hassle-free process — you don’t need to crop the image, calculate pixel dimensions, or remove a background by hand. All the technical work — sizing, positioning, and background correction — is automated. Your only real tasks are choosing the correct country and supplying one clear, well-lit source photo.

"}]

schemaOrg: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"FAQPage","mainEntity":[{"@type":"Question","name":"How Do I Get a Digital Passport Photo?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"To create a digital passport photo, take a clear, well-lit photo of yourself — or upload one you already have — through the PhotoGov passport photo maker. Select your country, and the tool automatically applies the correct crop, head positioning, background, and file format required for a digital passport photo in that country. Within seconds, you receive a compliant digital passport photo ready to download and upload directly to the relevant application portal."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Can I Make a Digital Passport Photo Online for Free?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"In most countries, yes — PhotoGov lets you generate and download a compliant digital passport photo at no cost. In the United States, United Kingdom, and Canada, PhotoGov charges a small, transparent fee to cover local compliance checks and support; current pricing for these countries is listed on our Pricing page. Regardless of country, optional add-ons — such as Human Verification by a compliance specialist, additional clothing variations, or extra file formats — are paid services you can add at checkout."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Where Can I Get a Digital Passport Photo?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Getting a passport photo online is straightforward — you have three main options: a service like PhotoGov, a local photo studio or pharmacy that offers digital files, or an authority-approved photo provider where your application specifically requires one. PhotoGov is the fastest browser-based route — no appointment, no travel, no waiting in line. Upload a photo, let the tool process it against the correct requirements, and download a ready-to-submit file in under a minute."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Is an Online Passport Photo Maker a Good Alternative to Passport Photos Near Me?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes, in any case where your application accepts a digital upload rather than a physical print. Searching for passport photos near me usually leads to a pharmacy or studio visit, an appointment, and a per-print fee — useful if you specifically need a physical photo or an authority-issued photo code, but unnecessary overhead for a digital submission. Whether you searched for passport photos near me or passport pictures near me, an online passport photo maker like PhotoGov removes that step entirely: you take the photo yourself, and the tool handles the sizing, cropping, and compliance check a studio would otherwise do manually."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Can I Take a Digital Passport Photo at Home?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes, and for most applicants it's the simplest option. Use a recent photo taken at eye level in even, natural light, with a plain wall or blank background behind you and no shadows across your face. PhotoGov's tool then handles the technical part — cropping to the correct canvas, resizing the head and shoulders to the required proportions, and adjusting the background to meet the standard. What it can't fix is the source image itself: a blurry photo, an obscured face, sunglasses, or a very low-resolution image will still need to be retaken before processing."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Can I Use an iPhone or an Android Phone to Make a Digital Passport Photo?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes. PhotoGov runs entirely in your phone's browser, so you can take a new selfie or upload an existing photo from your camera roll on either iOS or Android. There's no separate app to install and no account required — the tool works the same way on a phone, tablet, or desktop computer."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"How Do I Upload a Passport Photo Online?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Once PhotoGov has processed your photo, download the finished file to a location you can easily find, such as your device's Files or Downloads folder. Then open the official application portal for your document, locate its photo-upload field, select the saved file, and wait for the portal to run its own validation check. If the portal flags an issue with the file's technical properties, our step-by-step Digital photo upload guide covers the most common causes and fixes."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Does PhotoGov Replace a Passport Photo Scanner?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"For creating a new digital photo, yes — starting from a phone camera image is simpler and produces better results than scanning a print, since scans often pick up paper texture, glare, or color shifts. If a printed passport photo is all you have, scan it in full color at a reasonably high resolution and upload the scan; PhotoGov will still crop and format it correctly. Whenever possible, though, a fresh photo taken directly on your phone gives the processing engine more detail to work with."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"What Is the Difference Between a Digital and a Printable Passport Photo?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"A digital passport photo is a JPEG file sized specifically for an online upload field — it has no physical dimensions until it's printed. A printable passport photo, by contrast, is laid out at an exact physical size (for example, 2×2 inches or 35×45 mm) on a print sheet, ready to be cut and submitted in person or by mail. PhotoGov's digital passport photo maker is built for the online-upload use case; if your application specifically requires a physical print, check your document's pricing page for the printable option before you submit."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"How Long Does the Online Passport Photo-Making Process Take?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Automatic processing — cropping, resizing, and background adjustment — typically takes about 30 seconds once you've uploaded a suitable photo and selected your country. If you add Human Verification, expect a short additional wait while a compliance specialist manually reviews the result against the current official template before releasing your final file."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"What Does the Digital Passport Photo Tool Change?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"PhotoGov's tool adjusts only the technical properties required for compliance: crop, canvas size, head placement, background color, pixel dimensions, and file format. It never changes your facial features, skin, or expression, and it never generates or synthesizes a new likeness — the person in the final photo is exactly who uploaded it. This matters because most issuing authorities, including the U.S. Department of State, explicitly prohibit digitally altered or retouched ID photos, and PhotoGov's process is built to stay within that boundary."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"What Does PhotoGov Not Do?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"PhotoGov prepares your photo file — it doesn't fill out your passport application, submit it on your behalf, book appointments, issue travel documents, or guarantee approval. Final acceptance always rests with the government agency or consulate reviewing your application; our role is limited to delivering a technically compliant photo file for you to submit yourself."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Why Must I Select a Country Before Processing?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Digital passport photo requirements aren't universal — each country sets its own standard. Pixel dimensions, aspect ratio, head-size percentage, background color, and file format can all differ meaningfully from one country's passport photo standard to another's. Selecting your country tells PhotoGov exactly which profile to apply, so the file you download matches the standard your application will actually be checked against."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Can I Use the Same Digital Passport Photo for Two Applications?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Only if both applications require the identical technical and biometric profile and the photo is still recent enough to meet each authority's currency requirement (most require a photo taken within the last six months) — for example, two passport renewals processed under the same country's standard. If you're applying in two different countries, each with its own passport photo standard, reprocess your source photo separately under each country's profile rather than reusing one output file; even small differences in crop or head proportion can cause a rejection."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Can PhotoGov Check My Photo Before I Submit It?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes, in two ways. Every photo automatically goes through PhotoGov's compliance check as part of standard processing, verifying crop, size, background, and other technical requirements against your selected country's standard. For extra confidence, add Human Verification at checkout, and a compliance specialist will personally review your finished photo against the current official template before you download it."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"What If the Government Portal Rejects My Digital Passport Photo?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Start by reading the portal's exact rejection message — it usually points to a specific technical property, like file size, background color, or head positioning. If the issue relates to something PhotoGov's profile is meant to handle, contact our Support with the error message and your country; if the rejection traces back to a processing error on our side, we'll provide a free retake or a full refund. If the rejection instead concerns your application's eligibility or a rule unrelated to the photo itself, follow the instructions provided by the issuing authority."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Is My Photo and Personal Data Safe?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes. PhotoGov processes each photo in a private session and does not share your image with third parties as part of the photo-making workflow. For full details on how long files are retained and how your data is handled, see our current Privacy Policy."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Is PhotoGov a Government Website?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"No. PhotoGov is an independent online service — a passport photo maker, not a government agency. We are not affiliated with any national passport office, embassy, consulate, or issuing authority, including the U.S. Department of State, and we cannot guarantee how any government will rule on your application."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Where Can I See Digital Passport Photo Examples and Sample Photos?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"If you want to see sample passport photos before you submit, two resources are useful here. Your country's passport-issuing authority typically publishes its own approved examples — for US applicants, that's the Department of State's Digital Passport Photo Page, which you can use to compare your finished photo against official samples. PhotoGov's own Digital passport photo examples article goes further, walking through specific acceptable and rejected photos so you can spot common mistakes before you submit."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Do I Need Photo-Editing Skills to Make a Digital Passport Photo Online?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"No. PhotoGov's passport photo maker is built for an easy, hassle-free process — you don’t need to crop the image, calculate pixel dimensions, or remove a background by hand. All the technical work — sizing, positioning, and background correction — is automated. Your only real tasks are choosing the correct country and supplying one clear, well-lit source photo."}}]}

children.innerHtml: DV Lottery Photo Tool: Make a DV Lottery Photo Online for Free

One DV Lottery photo. One shot per year — and no way to swap it out once your DV entry is in. Use the PhotoGov DV Lottery Photo Tool to create an entry-ready digital photo aligned with the U.S. Department of State DV Lottery photo requirements: 600×600 to 1200×1200 pixels, plain white/off-white background, JPEG format, up to 240 KB, sRGB color space. Works on any laptop, smartphone, or browser — no editing skills needed.

DV Lottery entry-ready · No app · 30 seconds

How Our DV Lottery Photo Tool Works

Our DV Lottery photo tool automatically applies all official DV Lottery photo parameters to your original portrait. It crops the image to 600 × 600 pixels and saves the file as a JPEG of up to 240 KB in the sRGB color space required by the U.S. Department of State.

Since DV Lottery applicants have only one chance to submit their entry, strict photo compliance is critical. At checkout, you can add Human Verification — a manual review by a senior compliance specialist who evaluates your photo and outlines its acceptance likelihood. We also recommend our Clothing Swap option, as inappropriate attire is one of the most frequent reasons for an automatic rejection of DV Lottery photos.

children.innerHtml: What is a DV Lottery Photo?
The official digital photograph required for entry into the Diversity Visa (DV) Lottery program.
Created by PhotoGov as a submission-ready JPEG file that follows all U.S. Department of State requirements for DV Lottery photos.
Submitted electronically at dvlottery.state.gov during the annual DV entry window as part of a single, non-repeatable application session.

DV Lottery Photos That Pass the U.S. Department of State Automated Checks

Plain white/off-white background, 600x600 to 1200x1200 pixels, JPEG, 240 KB, sRGB, head centered at 50–69% of frame height, neutral expression, mouth closed, eyes open, no glasses, no facial obstructions, no military wear, religious clothes don’t cover the face, no filters, no shadows.
DV Lottery Photos That Don’t Pass the U.S. Department of State Automated Checks

Colored or patterned background, head too small or too large, head off-center or tilted, glasses on, smiling with teeth, shadows on face or wall, beauty filters, military or camouflage clothing, religious clothes that cover the face, resolution lower than 600×600 pixels, non‑JPEG formats (such as PNG or HEIC), file larger than 240 KB.

children.innerHtml: Our platform is designed to align with the U.S. Department of State Diversity Visa Lottery photo rules. Final acceptance of your DV Lottery photo is determined by the automated screening system at dvlottery.state.gov.
Important: Read Before You Submit Your DV Entry
The Diversity Visa entry process leaves no room to fix a bad photo once it is submitted. Four things every applicant should know before uploading anything to dvlottery.state.gov:
1. One entry per person, per year

The US Department of State accepts only a single DV entry per applicant per fiscal year. Submitting more than one disqualifies all your entries without a refund or appeal — under 9 FAM 502.6 and INA 204(a)(1)(I)(i). Trying to fix a bad photo by submitting a second entry is the fastest way to lose your chance for the year.
2. Your photo cannot be replaced after submission

Once you receive your confirmation number from the DV Entrant Status Check system, the entry — and the photo attached to it — is final. There is no facility to log back in and upload a corrected image.
3. The upload check is automated and gives no feedback

The dvlottery.state.gov system runs an automated photo check the moment your file is uploaded, but it does not tell you which parameter failed or whether anything looks borderline. A photo that goes through at upload can still be reviewed at the consular interview stage — and if a problem is found there, it can disqualify an otherwise selected entry.
4. PhotoGov produces the photo; its acceptance is at the discretion of an automated system

PhotoGov is an independent photo service — a photo maker and a DV Lottery photo checker. We prepare a digital file aligned with the Diversity Visa Lottery Photo Specifications, but we do not file DV entries on your behalf, and we cannot guarantee that any individual photo will be accepted. The photo is one component of an entry you are responsible for submitting yourself.
How PhotoGov Aligns Your Photo with the Diversity Visa Lottery Photo Specifications

PhotoGov turns a regular selfie into a compliance-aligned Diversity Visa photo file. It applies every parameter set out in the Diversity Visa Lottery Photo Specifications: 600×600/1200x1200 pixel dimensions, plain white background, head height at 50–69% of the frame, JPEG output up to 240 KB, sRGB color space, 600 DPI. All photos produced are aligned with the biometric photo standards defined in ICAO Document 9303. Final acceptance of any DV entry photo remains at the full discretion of the issuing authority. Our internal DV lottery photo template is reviewed by our compliance team every eight weeks.
If you are uncertain about your photo, add a Human Verification service upon checkout: our senior compliance specialist reviews your image and gives expert feedback on the acceptance likelihood.

The DV Lottery runs on an annual cycle. However, as of August 10, 2026, the DV‑2027 registration dates have not yet been announced. According to the U.S. Department of State notice of November 5, 2025, the start date for the DV‑2027 registration period and the date DV‑2027 results become available through the Entrant Status Check will be announced on travel.state.gov as soon as practicable. These changes do not affect the immigrant visa application window for selected DV‑2027 entrants, which remains October 1, 2026, through September 30, 2027.
For other US photo services, try our dedicated tools: US Passport Photo Maker, US Visa Photo Tool, Green Card Photo Maker, and Digital Passport Photo Maker.

[{"q":"What Is the Correct DV Lottery Photo Size, and How Do I Resize My Photo to It?","a":"

The correct DV lottery photo size is 600×600 to 1200x1200 pixels, square format, saved as a JPEG up to 240 KB. To resize your photo to these dimensions without distorting proportions, upload your selfie to the PhotoGov’s DV Lottery Photo Tool. It automatically scales your image to 600×600 pixels, crops it to the correct framing, head size, and positioning ( 50–69% of the frame height), and delivers a file within the required size range. No manual resizing or guesswork with manual photo editing is required from you.

"},{"q":"What Is the Best Online Tool to Check DV Lottery Photo Requirements?","a":"

The best online DV Lottery photo checker is one that validates every official requirement in a single automated step: pixel dimensions (600×600 to 1200x1200-pixel range), head-to-photo height ratio (50–69%), plain white/off-white background, JPEG format, and file size up to 240 KB.

PhotoGov runs all of these checks automatically after processing your selfie, flagging any parameter that falls outside the U.S. Department of State specification before you download a final photo. If you want a human expert to review the result, you can add the optional Human Verification service.

"},{"q":"How Do I Crop My DV Lottery Photo to the Right Dimensions?","a":"

Cropping a DV Lottery photo to the exact 600×600 to 1200x1200-pixel square requires more than just cutting the image — the crop must also place the head correctly so the face fills 50–69% of the photo height, with the crown of the head positioned just below the top edge and clear space above.

PhotoGov handles this automatically: it detects your face, calculates the biometric crop zone, and centers your head within the square frame.

"},{"q":"How Do I Verify That My DV Lottery Photo Qualifies Before Submitting?","a":"

To verify a DV lottery photo before submission, check it against every official requirement published by the U.S. Department of State: size (600×600 to 1200x1200 pixels), head height ratio (50–69%), plain white or off-white background, no glasses, neutral expression, JPEG format, sRGB color profile, and file size under 240 KB.

Doing this manually is error-prone — a single out-of-spec parameter is enough for the system to flag or reject your entry photo. PhotoGov runs an automated compliance check immediately after processing, so you receive a verified, entry-ready digital photo. For extra certainty, our Human Verification service provides a specialist review before download.

"},{"q":"Which DV Lottery Photo Editor Produces Reliable Compliance-Aligned Results?","a":"

No online service can legally guarantee that your photo will be accepted by the U.S. Department of State’s automated system when you submit your DV Lottery entry. What a reliable DV Lottery photo editor can do is automatically apply all published technical requirements and validate the output before delivery. This includes correct dimensions between 600×600 and 1200×1200 pixels, a head size ratio of 50–69%, a plain white or off-white background, JPEG format, and a file size of up to 240 KB in the required sRGB color space. A trustworthy tool will not alter your facial features or expression, focusing instead on technical compliance such as cropping, color profile, and file-size optimization.

"},{"q":"What Tool Automatically Validates the Background in a DV Lottery Photo?","a":"

PhotoGov automatically checks your original background against the plain white/off-white requirement. Our background detection algorithm works across a wide range of original environments — light walls, neutral surfaces, and even moderately textured backgrounds. The tool checks the image for any residual color fringe or shadow that could cause a compliance failure, and flags issues before you download. The final photo produced with our DV Lottery photo editor has a plain background free from patterns, gradients, objects, or shadows, as required by the U.S. Department of State.

"},{"q":"How Do I Fix a Rejected DV Lottery Photo and Resubmit?","a":"

You cannot fix and resubmit a rejected DV Lottery photo within the same DV Lottery entry: if your photo (and entry) is rejected by the official system, that submission cannot be corrected or resubmitted. What you can do is prepare a fully compliant photo before you submit your next eligible DV Lottery entry in a future registration period. To do this, start by identifying typical issues such as wrong dimensions, incorrect head ratio, colored or patterned background, file size above the limit, or visible glasses.

Upload your original image — or take a new selfie — to the PhotoGov’s DV Lottery Photo Tool. It automatically applies all current technical requirements of the U.S. Department of State, including correct 600x600 to 1200x1200 pixel dimensions, head size 50-69% of the frame, plain white or off‑white background, JPEG format, sRGB color profile, and file size within the 240 KB limit.

For best results, retake your photo against a plain white or light-colored wall, ensure your face is evenly lit and centered in the frame, remove glasses, and keep a neutral expression. If the original photo has fundamental issues such as motion blur, harsh shadows, or low resolution, taking a new selfie is the only reliable way to prepare a DV‑compliant photo before your single DV Lottery submission.

"},{"q":"What Are the Most Common Reasons DV Lottery Photos Are Rejected?","a":"

The most frequent reasons DV Lottery photos are rejected include:

Incorrect image dimensions (any size other than the required 600×600 to 1200x1200 pixels).

Head height outside the required 50–69% of the image’s total height.

A background that is not plain white or off‑white (for example, colored, patterned, or textured).

Shadows visible on the background or on the applicant’s face.

Glasses worn by the subject

(glasses have been prohibited in DV photos since 2016)

.

A photo that has been digitally altered, filtered, or heavily retouched in a way that changes appearance.

File size over 240 KB, not a JPEG, non-sRGB color profile.

Poor technical quality, such as low resolution, blur, noise, compression artifacts, or pixelation.

Use this as a checklist or refer to our full DV Lottery Photo Guide before submitting your entry.

"},{"q":"Is There a Free DV Lottery Photo Tool That Validates Official Specifications?","a":"

Yes — PhotoGov offers a free DV lottery photo tool that validates your photo against the official US Department of State specifications at no charge (in countries outside the U.S., UK, and Canada where affordable fees apply). Upload your selfie, select the DV Lottery template, and the tool applies and checks every required parameter: 600 × 600 to 1,200 x 1,200-pixel range, 50–69% of the frame head size, white/off-white background, JPEG format, and file size up to 240 KB. The validated digital file is available for immediate download. An optional Human Verification service is available for an additional fee if you want a compliance specialist to review the photo before you submit.

"},{"q":"How Do I Center My Face Correctly for the DV Lottery Photo?","a":"

Correct face centering for a DV Lottery photo means that your head is positioned horizontally in the middle of the 600×600 to 1200x1200 pixel frame, with your face looking straight at the camera and without any tilt or rotation. The top of your head should be just below the upper edge of the image, and your chin should be clearly above the lower edge, so that your head occupies 50–69% of the overall photo height.

"},{"q":"How Do I Adjust the Head Size Ratio in My DV Lottery Photo?","a":"

The DV lottery head size rule requires your face — measured from the bottom of the chin to the top of the head (including hair) — to occupy between 50% and 69% of the total photo height, which translates to approximately 300–414 pixels in the 600×600 px frame. If your head is too small (face too far from the camera) or too large (face too close), the proportions fall out of spec. A reliable DV Lottery photo editor measures the head ratio automatically and adjusts the crop to bring it within the valid range. If the original photo cannot produce a compliant crop — for example, because the selfie was taken from too far away — the tool will ask you to upload a closer shot.

"},{"q":"How Do I Export My DV Lottery Photo in the Required JPEG Format and File Size?","a":"

The US Department of State requires the DV lottery photo to be a JPEG file up to 240 KB. PhotoGov produces a JPEG output automatically, with compression calibrated to stay within the valid file size range while preserving enough image detail to meet the minimum quality standard. You do not need to adjust export settings manually. After download, the file is ready to attach directly to dvlottery.state.gov during the entry window. If you need a printable version — for example, for a physical visa appointment later in the process — PhotoGov can also generate a formatted print sheet.

"},{"q":"Does the PhotoGov DV Lottery Photo Tool Work for the DV-2027 Entry Period?","a":"

Yes. PhotoGov applies the current US Department of State photo specifications, which have remained consistent across recent DV Lottery cycles. The underlying DV lottery photo template is reviewed by our compliance team every eight weeks to capture any changes to the official requirements. As of August 10, 2026, the U.S. Department of State has not announced the DV-2027 registration dates. For the DV-2027 entry period, when it’s open by the U.S. Department of State, PhotoGov will reflect the specifications in force at that time. If you are preparing your entry in advance, check the official dvlottery.state.gov portal to confirm the entry window dates and any updated photo guidance before submitting.

"},{"q":"Is Your DV Photo Checker Free?","a":"

Yes. The PhotoGov DV Photo checker is free in all countries outside the U.S., UK, and Canada. Upload your portrait, and let the tool apply the required size and crop, and download your submission-ready digital file, or bundle our add-on services, such as Human Verification or casual-to-formal clothes adjustment, available at checkout for an additional fee.

"},{"q":"Can I Use the DV Lottery Photo Tool on My Phone?","a":"

Yes. Our DV Lottery photo checker 2027 runs entirely in your mobile browser — Chrome, Safari, or Firefox on iOS and Android. No app to download, no account to register. Tap upload, take a selfie, or choose an existing photo from your gallery, and the tool returns a DV-ready JPEG you can save directly to your phone. Practical for preparing a DV-2027 entry photo from home, no desktop required.

"},{"q":"What File Will I Receive After Processing It With Your DV Photo Editor?","a":"

A single JPEG file within the 600×600-1200x1200-pixel range, in sRGB, up to 240 KB, with a plain white/off-white background — the exact format required for DV lottery entries at dvlottery.state.gov. The final file is ready to attach directly to your DV entry: no resizing, no recompression, no format conversion on your side.

"},{"q":"Can I Submit More Than One Entry to Increase My Chances?","a":"

No. The US Department of State permits only one DV entry per person per fiscal year. Submitting more than one — whether under your own name or by being listed twice — disqualifies all your entries. The DV system uses biometric matching on your photo to detect duplicates, which is one of the reasons photo quality matters.

"},{"q":"Do I Need a Separate Photo for Each Family Member?","a":"

Yes. Every spouse and every child under 21 listed on your DV entry must have their own, compliant photo. The DV system rejects entries with missing or duplicated family-member photos. PhotoGov can produce a DV photo for each family member from an individually uploaded selfie.

"},{"q":"Is My Personal Data and Photo Safe When I Use an Online DV Lottery Photo Tool?","a":"

Yes. PhotoGov handles your uploaded image and any personal information solely for the purpose of producing your DV lottery photo. Your data is processed on secure servers in a private session and is not shared with third parties, government agencies, or external AI services. In line with our data retention policy, uploaded images are deleted after processing is complete — they are not stored, indexed, or used for any other purpose. PhotoGov does not sell or monetize user data in any form. For the complete details of how your data is managed, see our Privacy Policy.

"}]

What’s a Visa Photo, Anyway?

A visa photo is more than just a picture — it’s your official image in a government system. Countries like Algeria use it for identity verification, immigration, and security. If your photo doesn’t meet the exact specifications, your application may be rejected or delayed.
That’s why PhotoGov exists — to make the process stress-free and accurate.
Tips & Recommendations
Always take the photo in good lighting.
Avoid using filters or editing apps — they can distort your image.
Keep your camera lens clean for sharpness.
If you wear glasses, make sure there’s no glare.
Take a few shots to choose the best one before uploading.
Detailed Photo Rules (Size, Dress Code, Colors)
Size: Must be exactly 35x45 mm
Dress code: No uniforms or white tops
Colors: Light background, dark clothes preferred
Expression: No smiling, neutral face

Validity & Appearance Changes

Photos for Algeria visa applications should be recent — taken within the last 6 months. If your appearance has changed significantly (e.g., beard, hairstyle, weight loss/gain), you should take a new photo to avoid rejection.
Always use a fresh image to stay safe.

children.innerHtml: Egypt Visa Photo Online For Free - 2025

Create your 2x2 inch (51x51 mm) Egypt visa photo from home using your smartphone. No need to visit a studio or worry about embassy rules — just take a selfie, upload it to PhotoGov, and get a high-quality photo that meets all official requirements. Whether you're applying for a tourist, business, or student visa, your photo will be perfectly sized, background-corrected, and ready to print or upload in minutes.
Auto-crop the photo to fit the Egypt visa size (free online tool)
Full document requirements for photos
How to get a photo - tutorial
Get photo for: Egypt visa 2x2 inch, 51x51 mm
How It Works – 3 Easy Steps
Take a selfie on your phone — neutral expression, light background.
Upload your photo to PhotoGov.net — we automatically adjust size, background, and lighting.
Download your final image — ready to print or send online for Egypt visa application.
It’s fast, easy, and saves you the stress of retaking photos or guessing embassy requirements.
How the App Works
PhotoGov instantly transforms your selfie into an officially compliant 2x2 inch Egypt visa photo. Our AI takes care of everything technical:
Crops your image to exactly 51x51 mm (2x2 inch)
Adjusts your head position and image sharpness
Cleans or replaces the background
Ensures lighting and contrast meet embassy guidelines
Delivers files for both digital and print use
No experience needed — just take a clear photo and we’ll handle the rest.
Why Choose PhotoGov
Guaranteed Compliance
Fully matches Egypt’s official visa photo requirements
Background Removal
Smart cropping, sizing, and background removal
No studio needed
Works with any smartphone
No specialized skills required
Final photo ready in under 2 minutes
Quick Tip: How to Take a Great Photo at Home
Stand in front of a white or light wall with soft, natural light
Keep your phone at eye level — don’t tilt your head
Wear dark clothes to contrast with the background
Don’t smile — a neutral expression is required
Make sure your whole face is visible, including ears
Once uploaded, we’ll do all the technical work for you.
*Data from government agencies
Egypt Visa Photo Requirements
Technical Specifications
Photo size
51 mm × 51 mm (2 x 2 inches)
Head height
Between 25–35 mm
Top of head to top edge
3–5 mm
Resolution
Minimum 600 dpi
File format
JPEG for digital, high-quality photo paper for print
Background
Plain white or light gray
Online submission
Accepted by Egypt e-Visa systems and consulates
Expression
Neutral, no smiling
Eyes
Open, clearly visible
Glasses
Not allowed
Accessories
No large jewelry or headwear (except religious)
Lighting
Even light with no shadows
What’s a Visa Photo?

It’s your official ID image for immigration and embassy records. For Egypt, this photo must meet biometric and visual standards. A small mistake — wrong size, smile, poor lighting — can result in delays or rejection.
With PhotoGov, you don’t need to worry about these rules. We make sure your photo passes every time.
Tips & Recommendations
Clean your phone lens before taking the photo
Don’t use filters — they may alter your features
Keep your face centered and body still
Take a few shots so you can choose the best one
Use indirect light to avoid shadows on your face
Full Rules – Size, Dress Code, Colors
Size: Exactly 2x2 inches (51x51 mm)
Dress code: No uniforms, no white or bright tops
Expression: Neutral, mouth closed
Accessories: Avoid anything that covers your face
Hair & makeup: Natural, clean appearance
Background: Plain white or very light gray only
Common Mistakes to Avoid
Using passport-size photos instead of 2x2 inch
Smiling or raising eyebrows
Wearing glasses or hats
Blurry or low-resolution images
Busy or colorful backgrounds
Shadows on the face or wall
PhotoGov helps you avoid all of these with built-in checks and corrections.
Features of PhotoGov
Our online passport photo tool offers several features to help you create the perfect photo:
Crop
Auto-crops to exact 2x2 inch size
Resize
Instantly scales image to meet embassy standards
Background removal
Replaces or corrects background to solid white/light gray
Auto-adjustment
Fixes lighting, sharpness, contrast, and alignment
Photo Validity & Appearance Changes
Your photo must be recent — taken within the last 6 months. If your appearance has changed significantly (haircut, beard, major weight change), it’s best to take a new one to avoid problems.
Frequently Asked Questions

children.innerHtml: Photo Requirements
Technical requirements if you are going to process the photo yourself through Photoshop or other services:
Facial expression
Neutral – no smiling or raised eyebrows
Eyes
Open, clearly visible, looking at the camera
Glasses
Not allowed
Head coverings
Only for religious reasons – face must be fully visible
Hair & face
Hair must not obscure the face
Accessories
No large jewelry, hats, or visible headphones
Clothing
No white tops; avoid uniforms
Shadows & lighting
No shadows on face or background; evenly lit
What’s a Visa Photo?

It’s more than a headshot — it’s your biometric identity for international travel. Egyptian authorities use this image to verify who you are. If your photo doesn’t match the embassy’s requirements, your visa can be delayed or even denied.
PhotoGov takes that risk away — you get a verified photo without the guesswork.
Tips & Recommendations
Clean your phone camera before taking a shot
Don’t use filters or smoothing apps
Make sure your shoulders are visible
Avoid busy backgrounds and patterned walls
Try a few times — our app shows you which one works best
Full Rules – Size, Dress Code, Colors
Size: Must be exactly 40x60 mm
Clothing: Wear something that contrasts with the background (not white)
Expression: Neutral, no smiling
Glasses: Not allowed
Headgear: Only for religious purposes
Background: White or light gray, no shadows or textures
Common Mistakes to Avoid
Using a wrong size (like passport size instead of 40x60 mm)
Smiling or tilting your head
Wearing white clothes or accessories that blend in
Shadows on the wall or your face
Low-resolution or blurry images
Using a selfie app that alters facial features
With PhotoGov, we prevent all of these automatically
Photo Validity & Appearance Changes
Your Egypt visa photo must be recent, usually taken within the last 6 months. If your appearance has changed significantly (new beard, haircut, weight change), it’s safest to upload a new photo.
Features of PhotoGov
Our online passport photo tool offers several features to help you create the perfect photo:
Crop
Our in-built cropping feature allows you to trim new visa photos and ensure that they don’t have uneven edges. This allows you to neaten up your picture and ensure it’s the proper size for your visa.
Resize

You can also resize your picture as needed through PhotoGov, meaning that the end result will be a perfectly proportioned image that will fit just right into your visa. Additionally, you don’t need to worry about stretching or squishing the image and ruining the quality.
Background removal
If you can’t find a neutral background against which you can take a satisfactory picture, don’t worry; we have a background removal tool that can help you achieve the same results.
Auto-adjustment
With the click of a button, you can have our auto-adjustment tool immediately optimize your image to meet brightness, color, and contrast standards.

children.innerHtml: How to Create the Perfect Spain Visa Photo: A Step-By-Step Guide
Pick the Document Type
– Select “Spain Visa Photo” from the list of options provided on our website.
Take Your Photo
– Use a high-quality camera or smartphone, standing 1.5-2 meters from the camera.
Submit Your Photo
– Upload your image to our platform, ensuring it meets format and background requirements.
Optimize the Image
– Use our tools to crop and enhance your image to fit the 26x32mm specifications.
Save and Submit
– Download the final image or print it for submission.
Professional Advice for Perfect Results
Lighting Setup – Use natural daylight or evenly distributed artificial light to avoid shadows.
Background Preparation – Ensure the backdrop is a solid, light color with no patterns.
Stable Camera Positioning – Use a tripod or steady surface to prevent blurring.
Posture and Alignment – Sit or stand tall, keeping your shoulders even and facing the camera directly.
Avoid Common Photo Mistakes
Reflections in Glasses – If possible, remove glasses or adjust lighting to eliminate reflections.
Wrong Size – Verify the dimensions and resolution using our platform’s resizing tools.
Inconsistent Background – Ensure the background is plain and meets official standards.
Uneven Lighting – Adjust your lighting setup to ensure even illumination on your face and background. Additional Compliance Aspects
Face Visibility – Ensure all facial features are visible, with hair pulled away from the eyes.
Focus and Sharpness – The image should be clear, with no blurring or pixelation.
Proportional Sizing – The face should occupy 70-80% of the photo height.
File Validation – Use our tools to check the file size and resolution before submission.
Submission Guidelines
For physical submissions: Print your photo on high-quality matte or glossy paper in exactly 26x32mm dimensions.
For digital applications: Ensure your photo meets the required file size and format before uploading.

Ethiopia Passport Photo — Dimensions and Guidelines
Before printing, ensure that your photo is formatted according to the specific guidelines. Here are some important aspects to consider:
Technical Specifications for Self-Processing:
Dimensions
The photo must strictly adhere to the 30x40 mm size requirement. Any deviation will lead to rejection, necessitating a retake of the photograph.
Color
The photo should be in color and taken against a neutral white or off-white background. This ensures clarity and avoids distractions. Avoid digital enhancements, such as color balance adjustments.
Resolution and File Size

The photo should be of high quality with a minimum resolution of 600 DPI. Ideally, aim for a resolution between 600 and 1200 DPI. The file size should range between 1 MB and 15 MB to ensure smooth processing.
Attire and Dress Code

When taking your Ethiopian passport photo, adhere to the following guidelines: 
 •	Clothing: Wear normal, everyday attire. 
 •	Avoid: Uniforms, camouflage clothing, head coverings, and eyeglasses (unless required for religious reasons).
Image Quality and Background

•	Make sure your photo is clear and focused without any blur, noise or pixelation. 
 •	Use a background without any shadows for your photo.

PhotoGov and the European Commission Standards for Schengen Visa Photos

The Schengen visa photo rules are defined by the European Commission — Migration and Home Affairs and the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Document 9303 biometric standard. We track these requirements continuously, review each country’s guidance by hand, and keep our automatic template up to date. The final photo you download from PhotoGov complies with all current official specifications of Schengen consulates and visa centers.

A Schengen visa photo produced with our visa photo-making tool is a 35 × 45 mm biometric image with a white background, cropped and framed according to the ICAO requirements, with your head centered and within the required 32–36 mm range. Our Schengen visa photo tool changes only the size, the crop, and the background of the image — it never reshapes or alters your facial features. Your final photo can be downloaded as a JPEG for online submissions or a printable PDF sheet for printouts and in-person applications.

If you want a second opinion before you apply, add the Human Verification service. A senior PhotoGov compliance specialist checks your photo against the latest Schengen visa rules and either approves it or recommends a re-upload. This is the option most worth using when your appointment is already booked, when a previous photo was refused, or when you are applying for a child whose appearance changes quickly.
For other European document photos, see our dedicated tools: German Visa Photo Tool, French Passport Photo Tool, Spanish Visa Photo Tool, and Italian Visa Photo Tool.

children.innerHtml: What is a UK Driving Licence Photo?
The photo the DVLA requires for full and provisional UK driving licences, and for renewing your photocard.
Built by PhotoGov to the DVLA and GOV.UK rules — 35 × 45 mm, correct head height, plain light background — and ready to submit.
Use it either way: upload it to the online DVLA service, or print it for a postal (D1) application.
Your Final UK Driving Licence Photo from PhotoGov

PhotoGov automatically applies all key technical requirements to your original photo. The final image is ready for submission and doesn’t require any adjustments from you. Below are the key technical parameters of your final UK driving licence photo from PhotoGov.

children.innerHtml: If your photo is rejected due to technical issues on PhotoGov’s side, we provide a free retake or a full refund.
PhotoGov: Compliance-Aligned Output for UK Driving Licence Photos

PhotoGov follows the official driving licence photo specifications published by the DVLA on GOV.UK and the photo standards applied by HM Passport Office. These guidelines form the basis of our processing rules, and the compliance team keeps them updated as new revisions come into force. Our summary of official UK passport photo requirements covers the digital and printed formats for passport applications.

Every file produced by the platform reflects the technical elements expected from an official UK driving licence photo: the correct 35 × 45 mm dimensions, head height, lighting, and a face ratio aligned with DVLA identification systems. The tool prepares the final image without altering facial features or cosmetic editing and delivers a ready-to-print or digital file within seconds.
A visa application follows a different route, and our UK visa photo requirements page covers the photo for that document.

For time-sensitive driving licence applications, PhotoGov offers the Human Verification service. In this mode, our senior compliance specialist manually reviews your picture against the latest DVLA and GOV.UK driving licence photo requirements before you submit it.

Frequently Asked Questions

attributes.model:
[{"q":"How to Take a UK Driving Licence Photo Using a Phone?","a":"

Find a plain, light grey or cream wall and stand near a window \u2014 the daylight must evenly illuminate your face. Hold the phone at eye level, look straight at the lens, keep a neutral expression with your mouth closed, and your shoulders square in the frame. Upload the sharpest shot to PhotoGov and choose the UK driving licence format \u2014 the tool converts it into the 35 \u00d7 45 mm frame, 70-80% head height, and background, producing a submission-ready file in a digital or printable format.<\/p>"},{"q":"How to Resize a Photo to the UK Driving Licence Size?","a":"

You can crop a photo by hand on your phone or laptop, but an online driving licence photo maker is more reliable: it fits the image to the official 35 \u00d7 45 mm size and the DVLA head-height band, not just the crop. PhotoGov also offers extras such as Human Verification or a casual-to-formal clothing change for a smarter result.<\/p>"},{"q":"Why Should I Make My Driving Licence Photo at Home?","a":"

It is quick, cheap, and convenient \u2014 all you do is take a selfie and upload it, and PhotoGov handles the sizing, cropping, and background. You skip the studio trip, and you can add a formal-attire change to lower the risk of rejection.<\/p>"},{"q":"How Do I Convert My Picture into the 35 \u00d7 45 mm Size?","a":"

Upload your picture to the PhotoGov driving licence photo converter and pick the UK format. The tool rescales and re-crops it to the official 35 \u00d7 45 mm dimensions and adjusts the background to match DVLA and GOV.UK rules.<\/p>"},{"q":"Can I Print My Driving Licence Photo After Editing?","a":"

Yes. Your final file comes print-ready, so you can print it at a copy shop, on a home printer, or through an online print service for a postal (D1) application. PhotoGov also gives you a printable PDF sheet.<\/p>"},{"q":"Can I Use the Same Photo for My Driving Licence and My UK Passport?","a":"

No. We don\u2019t recommend using the same photo for different document types, as it can lead to delays and rejections. Though the size of a UK passport and driving licence photo is the same, the requirements for a passport photo digital submission require a specific file. Use our UK Passport Photo Tool<\/a> if you specifically need a passport photo.<\/p>"},{"q":"Where Can I Find a Free UK Driving Licence Photo Checker Online?","a":"

PhotoGov has a built-in checker that reviews your driving licence photo for size, head height, background, and lighting against the DVLA and GOV.UK rules, and flags anything that needs a retake \u2014 just upload your selfie to check it free. For added certainty, Human Verification puts a senior specialist on a manual review.<\/p>"},{"q":"Do I Need a New Photo to Renew My Driving Licence?","a":"

Yes. The DVLA requires you to update the photo on your photocard licence every 10 years, and the photo must be a recent, true likeness of you. You can apply online and upload a new photo, or apply by post with a printed photo. PhotoGov prepares a 35 \u00d7 45 mm file ready for either route.<\/p>"},{"q":"Can I Wear Glasses or a Head Covering in My Driving Licence Photo?","a":"

You can wear glasses as long as your eyes are clearly visible, with no glare or tinted lenses. Everyday hats are not allowed, but head coverings worn for religious or medical reasons are accepted, provided they do not hide your facial features.<\/p>"},{"q":"Will My File Meet the File-Size Requirements for the Online DVLA Application?","a":"

Yes. PhotoGov outputs a high-resolution JPG\/JPEG built for the online DVLA service, which accepts the 35 \u00d7 45 mm format, plus a printable PDF for postal (D1) submissions. The file follows DVLA and GOV.UK requirements: final acceptance always rests with the issuing authority.<\/p>"},{"q":"Is Human Verification Available for My Driving Licence Photo?","a":"

Yes. Choose Human Verification at checkout, and a senior PhotoGov specialist checks your finished driving licence photo against the latest DVLA and GOV.UK rules. If it meets every requirement, it is approved; if anything looks off, you are invited to re-upload.<\/p>"},{"q":"What Happens If My Driving Licence Photo Gets Rejected?","a":"

If the fault is technical on our side, we refund you or provide a free retake. If the original selfie is the problem \u2014 lighting, head position, or expression \u2014 you will need to take and upload a new one. Adding Human Verification before you submit minimises the chance of a rejection.<\/p>"},{"q":"Is My Personal Data and Photo Safe With PhotoGov?","a":"

Yes. We treat your personal data and images with great care. PhotoGov uses your information solely to generate an official ID photo and deletes it from our servers once the process is complete. We never share your data with third parties or external AI services. If you have any questions, you can always contact our Customer Support<\/a> team or read more details in our Privacy Policy<\/a>.<\/p>"},{"q":"Is There an Official Government Driving Licence Photo Tool?","a":"

No. The DVLA publishes the photo rules and sample images on GOV.UK, but does not run its own photo maker. PhotoGov builds your photo to those official specifications and adds a simpler interface, plus options like Human Verification and a formal-attire change.<\/p>"}]

children.innerHtml: Your UK Passport Online Photo for Free

You need to send in a passport photo that passes certain government criteria in order to apply for a UK passport.  The photo is a key aspect of your application, and if it doesn’t fulfill the essential requirements, it can cause delays or even rejection of your passport request.    You don't have to go to a professional photo booth or studio to get the perfect UK passport photo. You can do it right from your phone with PhotoGov.net.

Why the photo on your UK passport is important

You need to use the photo for your UK passport to prove who you are and for biometric reasons. It has to follow precise rules about size, background color, head position, and face expression. Your application could be delayed or turned down if the photo doesn't satisfy these standards.
But don't worry! You may be sure that PhotoGov.net will automatically review and change your photo to suit the exact UK Passport requirements, making the procedure easy and stress-free.

Creating the correct photo for your UK passport has never been easier.   Don't worry about waiting in line or going to photo booths.
Take a Selfie:

How to take your own UK Passport online photo

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect passport photo yourself:
1. Take a picture of yourself

Open up the PhotoGov.net photo service and take your picture. Make sure you’re not wearing any headcovers or glasses, do not wear a uniform, and keep your expression neutral. Ensure that the area is well-lit and that you are standing against a neutral background.

children.innerHtml: Common Mistakes to Avoid
Taking a UK passport photo may seem easy, but there are typical blunders that can make the process take longer or get you turned down
Things you should not do are:
Wrong background: The background must be simple white or light grey, with no patterns or shadows
The picture must be exactly 35 mm x 45 mm in size
Bad lighting: Make sure your face is evenly lit and doesn't have any dark areas or shadows
Facial expression: Keep a neutral expression, with your mouth closed and eyes open
Glare on glasses: If you wear glasses, ensure sure there isn't any glare or reflection that gets in the way of your vision
With PhotoGov, we automatically rectify these typical problems for you, so your photo will always be compliant

Crop

Changes the size of your photo so that it fits the official UK passport size
Background removal
This takes away any distracting background and replaces it with a solid, conforming color
Auto-adjustment
Automatically changes the brightness, sharpness, and contrast of your picture to make sure it looks clear and professional
How to take UK Passport online photos for babies and kids

When taking pictures of babies and children for passport, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.

children.innerHtml: Our platform is built to meet His Majesty's Passport Office passport photo rules. However, the final acceptance of your photo is always at the full discretion of HM Passport Office.
PhotoGov and HM Passport Office Standards for ID Photos

PhotoGov adheres to the official photo rules issued by His Majesty’s Passport Office, as well as the biometric guidelines of the ICAO Doc 9303. These rules are regularly monitored and updated by our team. The PhotoGov technical crew adjusts the settings in the photo-making software whenever standards change to keep every template up to date.

For UK passports, the images produced by the UK passport photo checker online free tool are tailored to the 35 × 45 mm format with a 29-34 mm head size, centered in the frame, and a plain light‑coloured background with soft, even lighting. The photo is adjusted only in terms of size, crop, and background — the applicant’s facial features are not altered in any way. The final file is prepared for printing or digital submission in just a few seconds.

For users requiring additional reassurance that their photo meets all formal criteria, we offer the Human Verification service. In this mode, our senior compliance specialist manually reviews your picture against the latest HM Passport Office requirements before you submit it. This option is particularly suitable for time‑sensitive applications or situations where a rejection would cause significant inconvenience.
For other U.K. ID photos, see our dedicated tools: UK Visa Photo Tool, UK Driving Licence Photo Tool.

children.innerHtml: Greece Passport Photo - 40mm x 60mm

A properly oriented passport photo is essential for a hassle-free application process. Greek officials impose stringent requirements of 40mm x 60mm as only images that adhere to these standards will pass, specifically biometric standards, and this will mitigate rejections. Adjustments to these standards can lead to processing hindrances or outright refusal to accept the application. PhotoGov makes it easy, offering compliant passport photos in a few simple steps.
Auto-crop the photo to fit the Greece passport size (free online tool)
Full document requirements for photos
How to get a photo - tutorial
Get photo for: Greece Passport 40x60 mm (4x6 cm)
Appearance Standards
Facial Expression – Neutral (open eyes & closed mouth)
Head Position Head Centered 70-80% in frame
Clothes — No uniforms; no light-colored outfits that meld into the scenery
No Hands or Props – No other person's hands or any other objects, supports or accessories should be visible.
How to Take the Perfect Greek Passport Photo
Choose a Bright Area — Make sure it is evenly lit without strong shadows.
Use Plain Background – White wall or backdrop required.
Position them Correctly – Make sure your head is directly in the middle and facing the camera.
Upload to PhotoGov – our system automatically adjusts size, brightness, and background.
Terms of Service - Download + Print - 100% compliant Greek passport photo instantly.
Guidelines and size requiements for a Greece passport

For successful Greece passport applications, it's vital to follow Greece passport photo requirements. Key criteria include a recent photo (taken within the last month) sized 40x60mm, a light and plain background, a neutral expression, and an unobstructed, full-face view, background color - rgb(238,238,238);. Refrain from wearing glasses, headgear, or casting shadows, except for religious reasons. Abiding by these Greece passport photo requirements helps ensure a smooth application process.

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect passport photo yourself:
1. Take a picture of yourself

Open up the PhotoGov.net photo service and take your picture. Make sure you’re not wearing any headcovers or glasses, do not wear a uniform, and keep your expression neutral. Ensure that the area is well-lit and that you are standing against a neutral background.

Common Errors That Result in Rejections
Fix Shadows on Face or Background – Make sure you have soft, even lighting.
Wrong background – avoid colors or patterns
Head Tilted or Off-Center – Keep your head straight and centered.
Glare from Glasses – Remove the glasses or angle the camera to avoid reflection.
Additional Compliance Tips
No Digital Retouching Your Review photos should include your natural features.
Visible Full Face – No Hats, Scarves or Head Coverings (Except For Religious Or Medical)
Be Sharp — No blurred or pixelated images.
Neutral Lighting – No color filters or artificial tones.
Single Picture Verification with PhotoGov - Our system guarantees that your picture follows all Greek passport requirements.
How to take Greece Passport photos for babies and kids

When taking pictures of babies and children for passport, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.
PhotoGov Features
Our online passport photo tool offers several features to help you create the perfect photo:
Crop

Our in-built cropping feature allows you to trim new passport photos and ensure that they don’t have uneven edges. This allows you to neaten up your picture and ensure it’s the proper size for your passport.
Resize

You can also resize your picture as needed through PhotoGov, meaning that the end result will be a perfectly proportioned image that will fit just right into your passport. Additionally, you don’t need to worry about stretching or squishing the image and ruining the quality.
Background removal
If you can’t find a neutral background against which you can take a satisfactory picture, don’t worry; we have a background removal tool that can help you achieve the same results.
Auto-adjustment
With the click of a button, you can have our auto-adjustment tool immediately optimize your image to meet brightness, color, and contrast standards.

Photo ID - Passport, national ID card or similar official document
Application Forms – Check the right form has been completed, depending on the type of application.
Payment Confirmation – The application fees for Greek passport are subject to payment before application submission

children.innerHtml: Hong Kong Passport Photo Requirements

Hong Kong passport photo requirements are set by the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government (HKSAR), and are based on the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) biometric standards. Both Hong Kong passport and visa photos adhere to the same standards.

For a successful application, a photograph must exactly adhere to the HK government regulations. This is where PhotoGov comes in handy: simply upload your portrait to our platform, and it will automatically adjust it to meet the following HKSAR guidelines:
Number of Photos
One digital photo is required for online submissions with the application form, and one original photograph scanned or in print quality — for in-person submissions.
Recency
A photograph must be taken within the past six months of the HK passport application and exactly reflect the applicant's current looks.
HK Passport Photo Size

The original photo, or processed by a scanner must follow the official Hong Kong passport photo requirements and have the size of 40x50 mm (1.57x1.97 in), with the distance from the head crown to the chin 32-36 mm (1.26x1.42 in). The smallest acceptable dimension for a digital photograph for online applications —  1,200x1,600 px.
Colour

he HK passport photo must be submitted in colour, exactly reflecting the applicant's natural skin tone and hair colour. Overly dark or light photographs aren't acceptable. Applicants must avoid heavy make up or any personalisation that alters facial features.
Background
A plain white background is required for a Hong Kong passport photo. It mustn't have any shadows, glare, textures, patterns, or foreign objects.
Lighting
Soft, distorted lighting is required for HK passport photos. The image must show clear facial features without shadows, glare, or flash reflection.
Positioning and Framing

The applicant's full frontal face, squared to the camera, and looking directly into it, is required for printed or digital photographs. The HK passport photo must be free of any frames or decorative elements.
Facial Expression
Neutral facial expression with no smiling, laughing, or frowning is required for any HK identity document. The applicant's eyes must be open and mouth closed.
Attire, Head Coverings, and Accessories

Formal or everyday attire is suitable for an HK passport photo. Refrain from wearing overly light coloured clothing as it will blend with the white background. Military attire can't be worn in ID photos. The applicant can wear a head dress only for religious or medical purposes. In case of the latter, a signed letter from the doctor must be submitted along with an application form. Accessories that obstruct facial features or the hairline aren't allowed.
Glasses
Glasses are allowed in a HK passport size photo, provided that the frame does not cover the eyes or have any glare from flash reflections.
Digital Quality
Photos taken with a digital camera or smartphone must be submitted in an acceptable file format — JPEG, GIF, or TIF, with a maximum image size of 2 MB.

children.innerHtml: Taking a Hong Kong Passport-Size Photo at Home

Today, with tools like PhotoGov, you can take a fully compliant Hong Kong passport photo from the comfort of your home or office. No need to rush to a professional studio — all you need is a smartphone, good daylight, and our expert tips.
Find a well-lit spot by the window, ideally, with a white background (if you don't have it, you can hang a white sheet with a paper clip).
Keep your head centred, wearing everyday clothing with a plain neckline. Avoid accessories that cast shadows or obstruct your face.
Take a few headshots by holding a phone (front camera) about 40-50 cm (16-20 in) away from your face.
Select the best image and convert it into an HK passport-size photo with our free online tool.
How to Take a Baby's Hong Kong Passport Photo
Taking photos of your child follows similar steps but with minor differences. Once the image is captured, upload it to PhotoGov — and it will instantly transform it into a passport-size photo.
Setting
Uniform lighting from a natural source, plain background.
Position
A newborn may lie on a blanket; older children — sit or stand.
Expression
Neutral facial expression, no crying or laughing.
