children.innerHtml: HK Passport and Visa Application Process
Hong Kong Passport Applications
Passport applications are available online via the HKSAR website or by appointment at one of the Immigration Department offices. Follow the information provided to submit your application.
Hong Kong Visa Applications

Visa applications can be submitted online via the HKSAR Immigration Department website. Select your visa type, and fill out the online application. You can also apply for an HK visa with authorized visa service providers or at a consulate or embassy in your country of residency.
Check this list to confirm whether your nationality qualifies for a visa on arrival.
Hong Kong Passport Size Photo: 100% Compliance with the HKSAR Standards

PhotoGov uses intelligent image-processing technology to adjust your original photo to the latest requirements of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government (HKSAR). The system compares each file to the stored technical criteria — from size and proportions to background tone and lighting balance. These parameters are reviewed regularly by our internal compliance team, which tracks updates to official guidelines and verifies all changes manually.

Every photo produced through PhotoGov follows the professional standards accepted for HKSAR passports. The software automatically adjusts framing, contrast, and position, ensuring a natural look that meets biometric standards. You can also refine details such as clothing or background without affecting facial geometry.

For applicants who want an extra level of certainty, PhotoGov offers Human Verification — a manual check by a certified expert to confirm that your image meets every technical and visual condition before submission.
Frequently Asked Questions

attributes.model:
[{"q":"What are the Key HK Passport and Visa Photo Requirements?","a":"

The successfully uploaded photograph for an HK passport or visa must meet the following HKSAR requirements:

Print photo size 40×50 mm (1.57x1.97 in), head size 32-36 mm (1.26x1.42 in)

The photograph must include sufficient headroom above the crown, keeping the face centered and properly framed for identity verification

Digital photograph submitted in JPEG file size, 2 MB max (GIF or TIF image type is also allowed), minimum 1200x1600 pixels

White background, sharp, free from glare and shadows

Natural facial expression, looking directly into the camera.

These guidelines apply to every application submitted to the Immigration Department. Follow them exactly, as a substandard photograph — for example, one that appears too light, too dark, or is of incorrect size — cannot be used for processing for passport or visa purposes.

To save time and money, trust the photo-making process to PhotoGov: it will format your original portrait to the official specifications of Hong Kong authorities.

"},{"q":"Where Can I Print a Passport-Size Photo in Hong Kong?","a":"

You can print a passport photo at well-known chains such as Fotomax or Photobi HK that have branches across Hong Kong. To save time, use our online tool to create your passport photograph, download it in printable PDF format on a single sheet, and have it printed on the spot.

"},{"q":"How do I Resize a Photo to Passport Size?","a":"

By using online photo-making tools like PhotoGov. It's a modern, convenient option that allows you to save time and money and skip a visit to a studio. The whole process takes less than 30 seconds:

Take a selfie with your smartphone or tablet.

On the PhotoGov platform, choose a country and a document type.

Upload your photograph to our online photo-making tool. You don't have to worry that the successfully uploaded photograph meets the official requirements — our system takes care of it.

Wait for under a minute while the software converts your photo to meet the HKSAR requirements, cropping, resizing, centering, and adjusting the background.

Select additional options, such as clothing adjustment, priority processing, or human verification.

Download the image in high quality. It is ready for application to the Immigration headquarters, offices or online.

"},{"q":"How Many Photos are Needed For a Hong Kong Passport (1200x1600 Pixels) Photo Application?","a":"

You only need to submit one high quality photo that meets the official HKSAR specifications. Before application, make sure that your photo adheres to these standards: the best way to do so is to use the PhotoGov passport photo maker that automatically adjusts your original photo to the government guidelines for HK passport-size photos.

"},{"q":"What are the Prices For Hong Kong Passport Photos?","a":"

Photos taken at pharmacies, shipping centers or retail stores usually fall within the $15 range. Visiting a professional photographer may require a higher budget. But there is always a free option available right from the comfort of your home — the Hong Kong passport photo online free tool PhotoGov. Just upload your selfie, and our service will convert it into a passport-size photo for HK.

"},{"q":"How Can I Ensure My Hong Kong Passport Picture Meets Guidelines?","a":"

Carefully review the requirements outlined by the HKSAR that we’ve provided on this page. Use our HK passport photo online free tool to ensure that your image adheres to all hong kong passport photo requirements, including size, framing, head positioning, background and distance from the camera.

"},{"q":"What is The Best Way to Take a Photo for Work Authorization?","a":"

The best way is to use our HK passport photo online free tool, which will seamlessly create a work authorization photo in 30 seconds. First, click a selfie. Make sure the lighting is even, free of shadows. Choose a white background, keep a neutral expression, and capture a high-resolution image. Upload it to PhotoGov, and get an application-ready picture in printable or digital format.

"},{"q":"How Recent Should my Photo Be?","a":"

Your picture should be taken within the six months to accurately show your current appearance.

"},{"q":"Can I Use an App To Create The Photo?","a":"

Yes. Mobile applications and online platforms like PhotoGov are designed for making passport and visa photo size 40x50 mm, 100% compliant with the Hong Kong government official requirements.

"},{"q":"How Can I Get a Hong Kong Passport Size 40x50 mm Using Photogov?","a":"

Simply follow the on-screen instructions on the PhotoGov website. Take or upload a ready selfie to the platform, wait for about 30 seconds while the system processes your image to meet all document criteria, and download a digital or a printable file that is 100% compliant with the HKSAR requirements.

"}]

children.innerHtml: How to make your Ireland Passport Photo Online
Visit PhotoGov.net
Choose Ireland Passport Online (715x951 px) from the list of documents
Capture Your Selfie
Get a clear photo takens in daytime or with nice flash against a white wall or backdrop (you can use blanket)
Upload It
Our AI scales the size, frames your face just right and balances the background
Download Your File
Immediately receive a high-res image ready to upload on the Alianza DFA site
Tips for a Better Passport Photo at Home
Keep the face out of shadows with soft light without glare
Stare into the camera and keep a straight face
Do not wear white shirts that could disappear in the background
If you have long hair, pull it back and show your entire face. The focus is at around 1 meter from the wall
How to take your own Ireland Passport online photo

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect passport photo yourself:
1. Take a picture of yourself

Open up the PhotoGov.net photo service and take your picture. Make sure you’re not wearing any headcovers or glasses, do not wear a uniform, and keep your expression neutral. Ensure that the area is well-lit and that you are standing against a neutral background.

children.innerHtml: 3. Receive your Passport Photo
Finally, you can download your ID photo. These images can be printed off, or you can simply use them as digital photos.
Mistakes to Avoid and How to Fix Them
Bad resolution — should be 715x951 exactly
Glasses with glare or eyes not visible
Smiling or chatting in photo-clicking moment
Busy background or patterns
Not centering or too close to the edge of your head
With PhotoGov, these are either auto-corrected or alerted to before you download the final image
How to take Ireland Passport online photos for babies and kids

When taking pictures of babies and children for passport, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.

Expression: Neutral, mouth closed
Eyes: Open, visible, no red-eye
Headwear: Only for medical or religious purposes
Glasses: Strongly discouraged; no glare or frames covering eyes
Photo Age: Taken within the last 6 months
How to Pose for Your Ireland Passport Photo
Go to PhotoGov.net
Choose Ireland Passport – 35x45 mm in the list of documents
Capture a Photo
Simply snap a front-facing photo on your phone or camera in mild, even lighting
Upload It
Our AI will auto-crop, resize, center on your face and clean the background
Download the Final Image
Save your submission photo as a print quality file
How to take your own Ireland Passport offline photo

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect passport photo yourself:
1. Take a picture of yourself

Open up the PhotoGov.net photo service and take your picture. Make sure you’re not wearing any headcovers or glasses, do not wear a uniform, and keep your expression neutral. Ensure that the area is well-lit and that you are standing against a neutral background.

children.innerHtml: 3. Receive your Passport Photo
Finally, you can download your ID photo. These images can be printed off, or you can simply use them as digital photos.
Perfecting Your Passport Photo
Shoot near a window with natural light to avoid shadows. Face the camera directly at eye level
Steer clear of white tops, so your shoulders don’t disappear into the backdrop.
Avoid hair on your face and eyebrows.
Snap away — PhotoGov allows you to take as many pictures as you like, with no limit on retakes before you download
How to take Ireland Passport offline photos for babies and kids

When taking pictures of babies and children for passport, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.
Printing and Submitting Guide
Offline Passport Applications (from within Ireland)
You will need 2 identical printed photos to accompany your application
Best results are had by using glossy or matte photo paper
Ensure that both the prints are of the size 35x45 mm
Take them with you when submitting your paper application
Common Mistakes to Avoid
Smiling or looking fake
Background not equal or flat
Inadequate lighting resulting in circles of shadows
Bad crop (head tiny/huge)
PhotoGov smoothly resolves these problems, before you can download pictures

Edited photos — No filters, smoothing or editing allowed

When taking pictures of babies and children for visa, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.

Download the final photo file, ready for online submission or print it for in-person use

children.innerHtml: If your photo is rejected due to technical issues on PhotoGov’s side, we provide a free retake or a full refund.
PhotoGov and the RTO Driving Licence Photo Standards

Driving licence photo rules in India are set by the Regional Transport Offices under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways and applied through the Parivahan Sarathi portal. PhotoGov tracks these specifications and keeps its template updated, so every photo you download matches what the RTO accepts right now.
PAN applications go through a different department, and the Indian PAN card photo requirements describe the two prints that the form asks for.

A driving licence photo made with PhotoGov is 35 × 45 mm (420 × 525 pixels) with your head centred against a plain white background, saved as a JPEG within the Sarathi upload limit. The tool changes only the size, crop, and background — it never reshapes or smooths your face — and the file is ready in under a minute.

For a first application or a renewal, you cannot afford to get rejected. Add Human Verification: a senior PhotoGov specialist checks your driving licence photo against the latest RTO and Parivahan rules before you upload it.

Frequently Asked Questions

attributes.model:
[{"q": "What is the Driving Licence Photo Size for the RTO?", "a": "

The RTO and Parivahan require a 35 × 45 mm (3.5 × 4.5 cm) driving licence photo, which works out to 420 × 525 pixels at 300 DPI. PhotoGov outputs exactly this size, so you do not have to measure or crop anything yourself.

"}, {"q": "What is the Photo Size for the Parivahan Sarathi Online Application?", "a": "

For the online application on the Sarathi portal, the photo must be a JPEG at 35 × 45 mm (420 × 525 px) and compressed to a small file — usually around 20 KB for the driving licence upload. PhotoGov resizes and compresses the file for you so it is ready to upload right away.

"}, {"q": "How Do I Make an Indian Driving Licence Photo Online from My Mobile?", "a": "

Open PhotoGov in any mobile browser, click a fresh selfie or pick one from your gallery, and choose the driving licence format. The online tool sets the 35 × 45 mm size, centres your head, applies a plain white background, and saves an RTO-ready JPEG — no app to install.

"}, {"q": "How Do I Resize My Photo to 420 × 525 Pixels for Indian Driving Licence?", "a": "

Upload your photo to the PhotoGov driving licence photo converter and select the Indian DL format. The tool rescales and crops it to 420 × 525 pixels (35 × 45 mm) and fixes the background, so the dimensions match the RTO requirement precisely.

"}, {"q": "What Background is Required for an Indian Driving Licence Photo?", "a": "

The RTO requires a plain white background with no patterns, shadows, or coloured walls. PhotoGov removes your original background and replaces it with a clean white one automatically, so a selfie taken against any light surface still works.

"}, {"q": "How Do I Reduce My Indian Driving Licence Photo to Under 20 KB for Parivahan?", "a": "

PhotoGov compresses your final JPEG to the small file size the Sarathi portal expects — around 20 KB for the driving licence — without making the photo blurry. You download a file that uploads to Parivahan without a size error.

"}, {"q": "Can I Make an Indian Driving Licence Photo Online for Free?", "a": "

Yes. You can make your Indian driving licence photo online for free with PhotoGov. Upload your selfie, let the software adjust it to the RTO format, and download a submission-ready photo in under a minute, for free.

"}, {"q": "Can I Upload the Photo Directly to the Sarathi Portal?", "a": "

Yes. The file PhotoGov gives you is a JPEG at the correct 420 × 525-pixel format and within the Sarathi/Parivahan file-size limit, so you can upload it straight to your online driving licence application along with your signature.

"}, {"q": "Can I Use the Same Photo for My Driving Licence and Passport?", "a": "

It is better not to. A driving licence photo follows the RTO’s 35 × 45 mm and 420 × 525 px specification, while the Indian passport uses its own biometric format and file rules. Use the format that matches the document you are applying for to avoid a rejection. The Passport Seva photo requirements page sets out the format that applies when you apply for the passport itself.

"}, {"q": "Is There a Free Driving Licence Photo Checker Online?", "a": "

Yes. PhotoGov automatically checks your driving licence photo for size, head position, background, and lighting against the RTO and Parivahan guidelines, and flags anything that needs a retake. Add Human Verification for a manual review by a senior compliance specialist.

"}, {"q": "Is My Personal Data and Photo Safe With PhotoGov?", "a": "

Yes. We treat your personal data and images with great care. PhotoGov uses your information solely to generate your Indian driving licence photo and deletes it from our servers once the process is complete. We never share your data with third parties or external AI services. If you have any questions, you can always contact our Customer Support team or read more details in our Privacy Policy.

"}, {"q": "Is There an Official Government Driving Licence Photo Tool?", "a": "

No. The Parivahan Sarathi portal lets you upload a photo but does not provide a maker that sizes or compresses it for you. PhotoGov is built around the official RTO specifications and adds a simpler interface plus options like Human Verification and a formal-attire change.

"}]

children.innerHtml: Appearance Guidelines
Facial Expression
Neutral – mouth closed, no smiling or frowning
Eyes
Open and clearly visible
Head Position
Centered, facing forward
Face Coverage
Should occupy 70–80% of the photo’s height
Clothing
Avoid white tops; dark, solid colors preferred
Glasses
Not allowed unless medically necessary
Head Coverings
Allowed for religious or medical reasons, face must be fully visible
Lighting
Even lighting, no shadows or reflections on the face or background
How to Make Your India FRRO Photo
Select Document Type
Select “India FRRO Photo – 35x35 mm” from the list of document types on PhotoGov.net
Take Your Photo
Use a smart phone or digital camera, stand off 1.5–2 meters from a plain white/light colored wall
Upload Photo
Upload your image to PhotoGov. Please keep your face clearly visible with a neutral face
Auto-Resize & Optimize
PhotoGov will auto-crop your image to exactly that square size set at the top (35×35 mm), set to cleanout the background, then adjust brightness and sharpness
Download&Online submit
Download your final photo file and be done with online submission.
How to take your own India FRRO photo

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect visa photo yourself:
1. Take a picture of yourself

Open up the PhotoGov.net photo service and take your picture. Make sure you’re not wearing any headcovers or glasses, do not wear a uniform, and keep your expression neutral. Ensure that the area is well-lit and that you are standing against a neutral background.

children.innerHtml: 3. Receive your Passport Photo
Finally, you can download your ID photo. These images can be printed off, or you can simply use them as digital photos.
Emptiness of Your FRRO PhotoBest Practices
Lighting: Shoot in natural or soft artificial light to eliminate shadows on face and background
Background – Stand against plain white or light-colored wall. Do not let the background have patterns/textures
Positioning: Face must be centered with the Camera as you put on a mask Your face is going to occupy 70–80% of the photo height
Attire: Avoid white tops and choose dark solid colors

children.innerHtml: Common Mistakes to Avoid
Using the wrong size photo (e.g., passport size instead of 35x35 mm)
Wearing glasses or head coverings that obscure your face (unless medically or religiously required)
Using blurry, low-resolution, or overexposed images
Background with shadows or patterns
Smiling or tilting the head
PhotoGov will automatically detect and correct these issues during photo processing
Submission & Printing Format Guide
Print on – Print your photo on professional quality glossy or matte photo paper and set it exactly 35x35 mm (3.5x3.5 cm) for physical submission
Digital Submission: Upload your photograph in the FRRO online application portal or consulate system. Check if that meets file size and resolution guidelines
How to take India FRRO photos for babies and kids

When taking pictures of babies and children for visa, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.

children.innerHtml: Make Your India PAN Card Photo Online for Free — Ready in 30 Seconds

Applying for a PAN in India? Upload a clear portrait to PhotoGov, and our PAN card photo maker will crop and resize it to 35 × 45 mm (3.5 × 4.5 cm), the photo space shown on the current PAN application form for individuals. Download a digital image or printable layout in about 30 seconds. It works on iPhone, Android, and any browser — no app or editing skills required.
No studio · No app · 30 seconds

attributes.model: {"src":"https://photogov.fsn1.your-objectstorage.com/photogov/admin/upload/906c34c5-df46-4f3b-93fa-892ad830bbf6.svg","alt":"not affiliated","title":"not affiliated"}

children.innerHtml: PhotoGov is an independent photo-preparation service. We are not affiliated with the Income Tax Department, Protean, or UTIITSL. We prepare the applicant’s photograph only; we do not create PAN cards, submit applications, verify PAN details, or influence the official decision.
Make Your PAN Card Photo Online Now

Upload a recent portrait from your phone or camera, and our PAN card photo maker creates a vertical 35 × 45 mm image for the current individual PAN application form. The tool crops the picture, centres the head, and prepares a plain white background. Download a JPEG or printable PDF. Use this profile only when your PAN route asks you to supply photographs; Instant e-PAN through Aadhaar does not require a photo upload.

children.innerHtml: If you need assistance, don't hesitate to contact our Support team, which is always there to help.
How Our Free India PAN Card Photo Maker Works

Our free India PAN card photo maker checks the source image and applies the correct crop, head position, background, dimensions, and file settings. It does not retouch facial features or add beauty filters. Add optional Human Verification if you want an expert review, then download your finished PAN application photo as a digital or printable file.

children.innerHtml: What Is an India PAN Card Photo?
A recent colour portrait used for an individual PAN application in India.
For applications filed from 1 April 2026, Form No. 93 shows a photo space 4.5 cm high by 3.5 cm wide — 35 × 45 mm in standard width-by-height order.
Prepared as a digital image or printable layout for the PAN application route that asks you to supply photographs.
Your Final India PAN Card Photo from PhotoGov

PhotoGov applies the current 35 × 45 mm PAN photo dimensions, vertical crop, head positioning, plain background, and output settings to a suitable source portrait. The finished file is ready to download and does not require manual resizing. Below are the key technical parameters of your final India PAN card photo.

For the complete capture and form rules, see our India PAN Card Photo Requirements Guide. An Indian passport photo uses the same 35 x 45 mm portrait, described in the new Indian passport photo requirements guide.

PhotoGov and India PAN Photo Standards

For new PAN applications filed on or after 1 April 2026, the Income Tax Department directs applicants to the new forms under the Income Tax Rules, 2026. Form No. 93 for an Indian citizen shows two spaces for a recent colour photograph, each 4.5 cm high by 3.5 cm wide. In standard width-by-height order, that is 35 × 45 mm. The form also indicates that a signature or left thumb impression crosses one of the two printed photographs. Add it only after printing and attaching the photo; it should not be built into the image file.
PhotoGov creates the 35 × 45 mm portrait and checks the crop, head position, background, lighting, sharpness, and facial visibility before generating the file.

Select Human Verification at checkout, and a PhotoGov compliance specialist will manually review the source and prepared image against the current profile. The reviewer can recommend a retake and confirm the technical output, while final acceptance remains with the authority processing the PAN application.

Frequently Asked Questions

attributes.model:
[{"q":"Can I Make an India PAN Card Photo Online for Free?","a":"

Yes. Upload a suitable portrait, choose the India PAN photo profile, and download the finished image. PhotoGov is free in India; Human Verification and other extras are optional.

"},{"q":"How Do I Take a PAN Card Photo at Home?","a":"

Ask another person to photograph you at eye level in even daylight. Look straight at the camera, keep a natural expression, turn off filters and portrait effects, and leave space around the head and shoulders for the vertical crop.

"},{"q":"What Is the Current PAN Card Photo Size in India?","a":"

For a new individual application filed from 1 April 2026, Form No. 93 shows each photograph as 4.5 cm high by 3.5 cm wide. Written in standard width-by-height order, the current India PAN card photo size is 35 × 45 mm.

"},{"q":"Does PhotoGov Include a PAN Card Photo Checker?","a":"

Yes. The checker reviews the dimensions, crop, head position, background, lighting, sharpness, and facial visibility. If the source is too small, blurred, or tightly cropped, PhotoGov asks for a better image. Human Verification adds a manual review.

"},{"q":"Is the PAN Card Photo Size Still 35 × 25 mm?","a":"

That was the size published for the previous Form 49A/49AA route. New PAN applications filed on or after 1 April 2026 use the new forms, and Form No. 93 shows 4.5 × 3.5 cm, or 35 × 45 mm in width-by-height order. If an older application was already pending on 31 March 2026, follow the form issued for that case.

"},{"q":"Is a Passport Size Photo for PAN Card the Same as a Regular Passport Photo?","a":"

Not automatically. “Passport size” is not one universal measurement. For a current individual PAN application, use the 35 × 45 mm PAN photo profile instead of choosing a generic passport photo size.

"},{"q":"How Many Photos Do I Need for a PAN Application?","a":"

The current Form No. 93 for an individual Indian citizen contains two spaces for recent colour photographs. Follow the instructions for your exact application route if you are using another form.

"},{"q":"Do I Sign Across the PAN Application Photo?","a":"

Form No. 93 indicates that a signature or left thumb impression should cross one of the two photographs. Prepare and print the clean photo first, then follow the form’s placement instructions; do not add the signature digitally.

"},{"q":"Do I Need a Photo for Instant e-PAN?","a":"

No. The Income Tax Department says the Aadhaar e-KYC Instant e-PAN route does not require a scanned photo or signature upload. Use this tool only for a PAN route that asks you to provide photographs.

"},{"q":"Can I Print the PAN Card Photo at Home?","a":"

Yes. Download the printable layout and print at 100% or “actual size” on photo paper. Do not use “fit to page,” because it can change the 35 × 45 mm dimensions. A photo lab can also print the file.

"},{"q":"Can I Use the PAN Card Photo Maker on My Phone?","a":"

Yes. The PAN card photo maker works in modern browsers on iPhone, Android, Mac, and Windows. Upload the original camera image and download the finished file without installing an app.

"},{"q":"What Should I Do If My PAN Card Photo Is Rejected?","a":"

Read the rejection message first. For blur, lighting, pose, or facial-visibility problems, take a new photo. For dimensions, crop, or file-format errors, contact PhotoGov Support with the exact message. PhotoGov provides a free retake or refund when its processing caused the issue.

"},{"q":"Is My Photo and Personal Data Safe With PhotoGov?","a":"

Yes. PhotoGov handles uploads under its Security and Privacy policies. The Privacy Policy explains what data is collected, how it is used, and how long it is retained.

"},{"q":"Can PhotoGov Create or Edit a PAN Card?","a":"

No. PhotoGov is a PAN card photo maker, not a PAN card maker or editor. It cannot create, reproduce, edit, print, or download a PAN card, and it cannot retrieve a photograph or personal details from a PAN number.

"}]

children.innerHtml: Fails to Remember
Here are a few common errors to look out for when you are preparing your India passport photo:
Background: No pattern, texture or shadow on background background should be plain white or light grey
Incorrect profile size: The size of your photo should be exactly 35x35 mm
No lighting: Your face should be evenly light, and no shadows or dark areas
Facial Expression: You must have a neutral look, closed mouth and eyes open
Contact lens: If you wear glasses, please make sure there are no glare reflections
It automatically corrects all said mistakes in PhotoGov and you can guarantee that your picture is legit every time

How to take your own India passport photo
Before you shoot, the MEA passport photo guide 2026 sets out the current size, background, and upload rules for Passport Seva.

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect passport photo yourself:
1. Take a picture of yourself

Open up the PhotoGov.net photo service and take your picture. Make sure you’re not wearing any headcovers or glasses, do not wear a uniform, and keep your expression neutral. Ensure that the area is well-lit and that you are standing against a neutral background.

How to take India passport photos for babies and kids

When taking pictures of babies and children for passport, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.

PhotoGov: Meeting Passport Seva Standards for Indian Passport Photos

PhotoGov is an Indian passport photo maker designed to convert a regular selfie into a ready-to-submit passport-size photo. The tool automatically applies the official Passport Seva photo specifications: 35 × 45 mm dimensions, pure white background, centered crop with the face occupying 80–85% of the frame, and biometric-grade resolution. All photos produced with PhotoGov meet international biometric standards described in the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) Document 9303. The final acceptance remains at the full discretion of the issuing authority.

To ensure compliance with official standards, our internal Indian passport-size photo template is regularly updated. Our compliance team manually reviews all requirements every eight weeks. If your application is urgent, you can add the Human Verification service. In this case, our senior compliance specialist manually reviews the photo you plan to submit and provides expert feedback on whether it meets current Passport Seva standards.

"},{"q":"How do I upload the finished photo to OCI Services?","a":"

"},{"q":"Does PhotoGov Submit My OCI Application?","a":"

"},{"q":"What If the OCI Portal Rejects my Photo?","a":"

"},{"q":"Is My OCI Photo Uploaded to the Government Portal Automatically?","a":"

"},{"q":"Is PhotoGov an official OCI service?","a":"

No. PhotoGov is an independent OCI photo service and is not affiliated with the Government of India, Ministry of Home Affairs of India, or any other government agency. Check our Independence disclaimer for more information.

"}]

Simply upload your recent selfie, choose OCI Card Photo as your document type, and let the tool automatically resize your original image to the 200x200 to 900x900-pixel OCI picture. Download your ready OCI photo as a JPEG for online upload."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Can I Make an OCI Photo Online for Free?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes. Use a reliable online OCI photo maker that uses your original selfie as a source photo and creates an OCI photo online for free. Choose the OCI photo service based on positive customer reviews and high Google ratings."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"What Does the OCI Photo Editor Do?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"It converts a suitable portrait into the OCI upload format by setting the square crop, face position, pixel dimensions, JPEG/JPG format, and 200 KB file-size limit. It does not retouch the applicant or edit the OCI application."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Can I Resize an OCI Photo Online for Free From my Phone?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes. The PhotoGov free OCI photo resize tool works in Safari, Chrome, and other modern mobile browsers. You can use PhotoGov as an OCI photo checker: the tool has a built-in OCI photo template and checks your original photo against all parameters, including the square crop, face position, dimensions, format, and file size, preparing a correct, application-ready OCI picture."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Can I Convert a Photo to OCI Size Online for Free?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes. Upload a selfie to PhotoGov, and select India as your country and OCI photo as your document type. PhotoGov will create an OCI-size photo online for free — 200 × 200 to 900 × 900 pixels, JPEG under 200 KB that you can download in under 30 seconds."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Does This OCI Photo Tool Resize an OCI Signature Image?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"No. This page prepares the applicant’s OCI picture only. The OCI signature image has its own upload field and technical settings, so do not combine it with the photo or use the portrait tool to resize it."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"How Do I Take an OCI Photo at Home?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"You can take an OCI photo at home in a few simple steps:Take a selfie in sufficient daylight. Official guidelines must also be followed, or your photo can lead to a hold or rejection in your application. But phew! Importance of Your India Registration of Birth Photo

Your photo for Indian birth registration is an important part of your formal papers and has to be in a specific size, resolution and technical specifications. The authorities use the photo for identification, so it must fulfil their parameters. If the photo fails to meet required specifications size or quality, then there is a high likelihood of your application getting delayed. Other Indian documents set their own rules, and the Indian PAN card photo guide describes the two prints a PAN application needs.
With PhotoGov.net, we make sure your photos are automatically sized correctly to perfectly meet all the required norms and get rid of the need of corrections all by yourself.

How to take your own India registration of birth photo

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect registration of birth photo yourself:

Background Incorrect: Background is plain white or light grey.

How to take India registration of birth photos for babies and kids

When taking pictures of babies and children for registration of birth, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.

Tips for Capturing Passport Photos of Babies and Kids

If you're photographing ones consider laying a sheet on the floor for newborns or positioning older babies in front of a white backdrop. It's essential to capture their face well seen, lit and there are no obstructions in the shot.

Auto Adjustment
Enhance your photos brightness and contrast with one click.
Crop and Resize
Adjust the size and crop your photo effortlessly to meet standards.
Where to Get Your Photo Printed
Pharmacies and Drug Stores.
Walgreens, CVS as well as Rite Aid provide passport photo services typically priced around $15.
Shipping Centers.
You can also avail similar services, at UPS and FedEx locations.
Post Offices.
Many post offices offer passport photo services at competitive rates.
Retail Stores.
Check out passport photo booths at different retail outlets.

children.innerHtml: India Visa Photo – 190x190 px Format for VFS Global Submissions

When applying for an Indian visa through VFS Global, one of the most important steps is submitting a 190x190 pixel digital photo. It’s a small but critical part of your application — and one that can lead to rejections if not done right. With PhotoGov, you don’t have to guess. Our platform automatically adjusts your selfie to meet India’s visa photo standards: size, background, clarity, and format — all in one go. Whether you're applying for a tourist, business, or e-visa, your photo will be ready for instant upload to the VFS system. The passport route uses a different file, covered in the guide on how to make an Indian passport photo.

children.innerHtml: Steps to Create Your India Visa Photo (190x190 px)
Follow these simple steps to create a fully compliant digital photo for your Indian visa application via VFS Global:
Select the Document Type.
Choose "India Visa (190x190 px)" from our list of supported formats on PhotoGov.
Capture the Photo.
Use a high-resolution smartphone or camera. Stand 1.5–2 meters from the lens, keep your head straight, and ensure even lighting.
Upload Your Photo.
Submit your image to our platform. Make sure the background is plain and your expression is neutral.
Optimize and Edit.
Our system will automatically crop, resize, and enhance your photo to fit the 190x190 pixel format with correct resolution and framing.
Download and Submit.
Save the optimized digital file and upload it directly to the VFS Global portal during your visa application.
Appearance Requirements
Expression
Neutral – no smiling or frowning
Eyes
Open, clearly visible, no red-eye or glare
Head position
Centered and facing forward
Head coverings
Allowed only for religious reasons, must not obscure the face
Hair & face visibility
Hair should not cover the eyes, ears should be partially visible
Glasses
Not allowed
Clothing
Avoid white tops; contrast with background is important
Accessories
No hats, headphones, or flashy jewelry
Lighting
Even, natural lighting – no shadows or reflections
How to Take an India Visa Photo from Home
PhotoGov is built to help you take your India visa photo at home — just follow these simple steps:
Environment
Choose a light-colored or white wall as a background
Use indirect daylight (near a window) or soft indoor lighting
Make sure the wall is free of patterns, shadows, or textures
Camera Setup
Use the rear camera of your phone for better image quality
Set the phone at eye level — arm’s length or tripod
Look straight into the camera; keep your head straight and shoulders level
Personal Appearance
Wear a dark shirt to contrast with the background
Keep hair away from the eyes
Remove glasses or accessories
Maintain a calm, neutral expression
Upload your selfie to PhotoGov and we’ll instantly convert it into a 190x190 px JPEG, with perfect brightness, alignment, and framing.
Common Mistakes to Avoid
Submitting a non-square photo (e.g., 4:3 or 3:2 ratio)
Low-resolution or blurry images
Visible background shadows or patterns
Wearing white tops that blend into the background
Smiling, tilting head, or uneven lighting
Glasses, filters, or editing apps that distort your face
PhotoGov prevents all of these with automated compliance checks.
PhotoGov Features
Our online passport photo tool offers several features to help you create the perfect photo:
Crop
Converts any image to perfect 190x190 px
Resize
Ensures exact pixel and DPI resolution for online use
Background removal
Applies plain white background automatically
Auto-adjustment
Fixes lighting, head position, and contrast

Do you require a biometric photo for your Italian ID card (Carta d’Identità)? You can use PhotoGov to create a 35x45 mm (1.4x1.8 inch) photo of the required format from your smartphone in a few seconds. Snap one selfie, and we will crop, resize, and format your passport photo to the correct specifications issued by the Italian government — ready to be printed or used online.

Our online passport photo tool offers several features to help you create the perfect photo:

You can also resize your picture as needed through PhotoGov, meaning that the end result will be a perfectly proportioned image that will fit just right into your Italy ID Card Photo

Brightness and Contrast
Properly balanced, there is no overexposed glare at any level of magnification

Hats

Face Apperance
Picture of entire face is required
How to Take an Italy ID Card Photo
Choose your document
Go to PhotoGov. net and choose Italy ID card – 35x45 mm
Take a photo
Provide a front facing photograph against a light coloured wall with a smartphone or camera,Head straight, and both open your eyes and mouth
Upload your selfie
PhotoGov is going to automatically crop, scale and sharpen your photo
Download the final version
Receive a digital and printable file that complies with all of Italy’s ID photo rules
How to Take the Ideal Picture
Light: Natural light or soft artificial light to prevent any shadows
Camera distance: Using your device’s front camera and someone to take the photo, stand 1-1.5m away
Background: One with white/light/ empty wall is preferred. Avoid textures and objects
Position: You can sit or stand. Look directly at the camera
How to take your own Italy ID card photo

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect employment authorization photo yourself:
1. Take a picture of yourself

Open up the PhotoGov.net photo service and take your picture. Make sure you’re not wearing any headcovers or glasses, do not wear a uniform, and keep your expression neutral. Ensure that the area is well-lit and that you are standing against a neutral background.

Finally, you can download your ID photo. These images can be printed off, or you can simply use them as digital photos.
Printing and Submission
Print: Print on High quality and use Gloss photo paper or Matte photo paper
Photo size: Please make sure that the photo you upload is printed as 35x45 mm (3.5x4. 5 cm)
Submission: One printed photo for in person applications. If CIE’s request is online, submit the digital file
How to take Italy ID card photos for babies and kids

When taking pictures of babies and children for employment authorization, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.
Disscussion Issues And How To Aboid Them
Wrong size – The photo must measure 35 45 mm. Use auto-resize on PhotoGov
Dim or non-uniform lighting – Ensure lighting is even on your face and on your background
Reflections in glasses – Remove your glasses or angle them to prevent glare
Facial expression – Keep your face tolerant and relaxed
Improper background — Steer clear from colored, busy, or patterned backgrounds. Try our all-in-one deletion tool

Appearance Requirements
Expression
Neutral – no smile, no frown
Eyes
Open and clearly visible
Head position
Centered, straight, not tilted
Glasses
Not allowed
Head coverings
Only for religious reasons – must not obscure the face
Clothing, Accessories
No white or light tops – contrast with background required. No hats, jewelry, or headphones
Lighting
Even, without shadows on the face or background
How to Take a Visa Photo at Home
Lighting: Use natural daylight near a window or soft indoor lights. Avoid direct sun or shadows.
Background: Stand against a plain white or light wall. Our system will fix minor imperfections.
Framing: Keep the camera at eye level. Your face should take up about 70% of the photo.
Posture: Sit or stand straight, look directly at the camera, relax your face.
Once done — upload the photo to PhotoGov and let us handle the technical side.
Common Errors to Avoid
Sending a passport-size photo rather than 35x45 mm
Wearing white clothes that merge into the background
Grinning or head tilting
Bad focus, shadows, or glasses
Ignoring either tight or too loose cropping around your face
PhotoGov automatically checks and fixes all these problems

You need to send in a photo that meets the requirements in order to get a Japan APEC Business Travel Card.  The official size for the photo on the Japan APEC Business Travel Card is 35x45 mm (3.5x4.5 cm).  If you don't follow the specified rules, your application may be delayed or turned down.   We make it easy to take a picture for your Japan APEC Business Travel Card that meets all the rules at PhotoGov.  Send us a selfie or a high-quality photo, and we'll resize, crop, and optimize it to fit Japan's official standards. You can then send it in online or in person.

children.innerHtml: Step-by-step guide to making your Japan APEC Business Travel Card photo
Choose the Type of Document
On PhotoGov.net, pick "Japan APEC Business Travel Card – 35x45 mm" from the list of document types
Take a Picture
Use a smartphone or a camera with a lot of pixels.  You should be 1.5 to 2 meters away from a white or light-colored background. Make sure the lighting is consistent and soft, with no shadows
Put the picture up
Put your picture on PhotoGov.  Make sure your face is plainly visible with a neutral look and even lighting
Resize and Optimize Automatically
PhotoGov will automatically crop your picture to 35x45 mm, clear up the background, and change the brightness and sharpness
Get it and send it in
You can either print your final photo file for usage in person or submit it online
How to Take the Best Photo for Your Japan APEC Business Travel Card
Lighting: To avoid shadows or too much light, use soft, uniform light. Daylight from the sun is best
Background: Stand with your back to a wall that is white or light-colored. Stay away from patterns or things that will distract you
Positioning: Keep your head straight and in the middle. Your face should take up roughly 70–80% of the height of the picture
Clothes: Wear clothes that are black and solid. Don't wear white or shiny tops
How to take your own Japan APEC Business Travel Card photo

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect employment authorization photo yourself:
1. Take a picture of yourself

Open up the PhotoGov.net photo service and take your picture. Make sure you’re not wearing any headcovers or glasses, do not wear a uniform, and keep your expression neutral. Ensure that the area is well-lit and that you are standing against a neutral background.

children.innerHtml: 3. Receive your Passport Photo
Finally, you can download your ID photo. These images can be printed off, or you can simply use them as digital photos.
Things You Shouldn't Do
Using the improper size (such a passport size instead of 35x45 mm)
Putting on glasses or other things that hide your face
Using pictures that are grainy or low-resolution
Background with patterns or shadows
Smiling or leaning your head to the side
During photo processing, PhotoGov will automatically find and fix these problems
How to take Japan APEC Business Travel Card photos for babies and kids

When taking pictures of babies and children for employment authorization, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.
More tips for being compliant
No Retouching: Don't use filters or editing that changes the way your face looks
Sharpness — Make sure the picture is crisp and doesn't have any pixelation or blurring
Face Coverage: Your face should make up 70–80% of the height of the picture
File Size and Format: JPEG or PNG, and the file size must be less than 1 MB for digital submission
Instructions for submitting and printing
For in-person submission: Use high-quality matte or glossy photo paper to print your picture in the exact dimensions of 35x45 mm
To send it digitally, upload your picture to the Japan consulate or visa application page. Make sure the file size and resolution are correct

children.innerHtml: Photo for the Japanese Language Proficiency Test (JLPT) - 2025

One important thing you need to do when you apply for the Japanese Language Proficiency Test (JLPT) is send in a photo that meets the requirements.  For digital submissions, the official size for the JLPT photo is 3x4 cm (360x480 pixels).  If you don't follow the rules, your application could be delayed or turned down.   We make it easier to take a compliant JLPT photo at PhotoGov.  You can upload your selfie or a high-quality photo, and we will resize, crop, and optimize it to match the official requirements so that you can send it in digitally or print it off.

children.innerHtml: *Data from government agencies
Rules for how to look
Requirement for Aspect
Expression on the face
Neutral: mouth closed, no smile or frown
Eyes
Wide open, plainly visible, and looking right at the camera
Position of the Head
Centered and looking straight ahead
Covering the Face
Should take up 70–80% of the height of the picture
Clothes
Don't wear white tops; dark, solid hues are better
Glasses
Not allowed unless it's for medical reasons
Coverings for the head Face
Must be fully visible
Lighting
The face and background should be evenly lit, with no shadows or reflections
How to Make Your JLPT Picture: A Step-by-Step Guide
Choose the Type of Document
On PhotoGov.net, look for the selection of document types and choose "JLPT Photo – 3x4 cm (360x480 px)"
Take a Picture
Use a good smartphone or digital camera.  Stay 1.5 to 2 meters away from a white or light-colored background.  Make sure the lighting is gentle and even
Put your picture up
Send your picture to PhotoGov.  Use good lighting and a neutral expression to make sure your face is easy to see
Resize and optimize automatically
PhotoGov will cut your photo down to 3x4 cm (360x480 px), clear up the background, and make it sharper, brighter, and more contrasty
Get it and send it in
You can either print the final photo file to use in person or download it and submit it
Best Ways to Take Your JLPT Photo
Use natural light or mild artificial light to avoid shadows or too much brightness
Background: Stand in front of a wall that is simple white or light-colored. Make sure there aren't any patterns or things that could distract you in the backdrop
Positioning: Make sure your face is in the middle of the frame and looking straight at the camera. Your face should take up around 70–80% of the height of the photo
Clothes: Wear dark, solid-colored clothes that stand out against the background. Don't wear white tops
How to take your own Japanese language proficiency test photo

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect language proficiency test photo yourself:
1. Take a picture of yourself

Open up the PhotoGov.net photo service and take your picture. Make sure you’re not wearing any headcovers or glasses, do not wear a uniform, and keep your expression neutral. Ensure that the area is well-lit and that you are standing against a neutral background.

children.innerHtml: 3. Receive your Passport Photo
Finally, you can download your ID photo. These images can be printed off, or you can simply use them as digital photos.
Common Mistakes to Avoid
Using the wrong size, like a passport size instead of 3x4 cm (360x480 px)
Putting on glasses or other things that cover your face
Using pictures that are grainy or low-res
A background containing patterns, shadows, or objects
Smiling or moving your head
During photo processing, PhotoGov will automatically find and fix these problems
How to take Japanese language proficiency test photos for babies and kids

When taking pictures of babies and children for language proficiency test, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.
More tips for following the rules
No Retouching: Don't use filters or digital changes that change the way your face looks
Sharpness: Make sure the picture is crisp and not pixelated or blurry
Face Coverage: Your face should take up 70–80% of the height of the picture
File Size and Type: JPEG or PNG, and less than 1 MB for digital submission
Guidelines for Submitting and Printing
For Physical Submission: Make sure your photo is the right size by printing it on high-quality matte or glossy photo paper that is 3x4 cm (30x40 mm)
For Digital Submission: Upload your photo to the JLPT application site or consular system. Make sure it fits the requirements for file size and resolution

children.innerHtml: Japan Passport Photo Requirements

Japan passport photo requirements are determined by the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) and are based on the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Document 9303 biometric specifications. To avoid passport application rejections, the submitted pictures must fully meet these guidelines. But worry not, PhotoGov automatically matches your portrait to 100% of official standards, delivering a ready-for-the-application official passport photo. Below is the comprehensive list of all requirements.
Number of Photos
One photo is required for both in-person and online submissions.
Recency
The photograph must be taken within the last six months and clearly reflect the applicant's current appearance.
Photo Size
The Japan Passport Photo Size is 35x45 mm, with a head size from 32 to 36 mm from the crown to the chin.
Color
Only colored photos are accepted.
Background
A plain white background, free from any patterns or textures, is required for a Japan passport photo.
Lighting
Professional distorted lighting that naturally presents the applicant's skin tone and hair color is required. The photo must be free from any shadows, reflections, or glare.
Positioning and Framing
The applicant's face and shoulders must be squared to the frame, facing forward. No tilting is allowed on passport photos.
Facial Expression

Only natural facial expressions are accepted in Japanese passport photos. No smiling, frowning, or any other overly strong expressions are allowed — they can result in delays or application rejection.
Attire, Head Coverings, and Accessories

Wear normal clothes for your Japan passport photo. Avoid white, overly bright items, large logos, or any accessories that may obstruct your facial features. No hats or headwear are allowed on official ID pictures, unless worn for religious or medical reasons. Remove face mask or any accessories that may obscure your facial features or prevent a clear view of your eyes, nose, and mouth.
Glasses

Formally, the MOFA of Japan doesn't restrict glasses in passport photos. However, it strongly advises refraining from wearing them, if possible. If there are glasses in the image, there should be no glare, flash reflections on the lenses, and the frames must not cover the eyes — they have to be fully visible. Tinted eyeglasses, even the medical ones, are not allowed. The same applies to sunglasses or any colored glasses.
Print Quality
Professionally printed photos on either matte or glossy paper are accepted.
Digital Quality

The Japanese passport photo must be a sharp, colour image at 600 dpi or higher, with no blur or visible pixels. Recommended digital size is at least 827 × 1062 pixels, saved in JPEG format without filters or digital alterations.

Passport Photo Near Me: The Most Convenient Locations in Japan

In Japan, it is easy to get passport photos thanks to the wide availability of photo booths, photo studios, and online tools. You can choose the option that best fits your schedule and budget — whether you are at a train station, in a convenience store, or at home with a smartphone.
Photo Booths

Self-service photo booths are installed in many train stations, convenience stores, and shopping centres across Japan. They offer preset templates for Japanese passports and ID photos, and prints are usually ready in a few minutes at a low cost.
Photo Studios and Camera Shops

Professional photo studios and large camera stores such as Yodobashi Camera or Bic Camera provide passport photo services with staff who know MOFA requirements. This option is more expensive than a booth but offers controlled lighting and expert guidance.
Convenience Stores and Printing Kiosks

Some convenience stores and in-store kiosks allow you to print ID photos from a smartphone app or USB drive using predefined passport formats. This is practical if you already have a compliant digital photo and only need prints.
Online Photo Tools

Online services like PhotoGov help you create a Japanese passport photo that meets MOFA specifications from anywhere in the world. You save time, money, and skip a visit to a photo studio. All you need to do is upload a selfie, and the system adjusts size and composition to meet 100% of official standards. In under 30 seconds, you're ready to download a digital file or a print-ready PDF page.

children.innerHtml: How to Take a Japanese Passport Photo at Home

Today, with convenient online services like PhotoGov available 24/7, from anywhere in the world, you don't need to leave your home to make a professional passport picture. A simple setup and a phone — is pretty much all you need. Just follow the practical tips below, and our platform will take care of the rest.
Select a well-lit spot in your house: the natural light from the window is best. Ideally, if it has a plain background.
Use a tripod to place your digital camera or smartphone at a distance of about 1–2 meters (roughly 3–7 feet) from your face.
In case you're taking a selfie with your iPhone's front camera, you must hold it approximately 20 inches away from your face.
Turn off the portrait mode to avoid blur and distortion in the photo. Set a timer.
Take a few images, select the best one, and upload it to the PhotoGov platform.
Wait about 30 seconds for the software to convert your selfie into a fully compliant passport photo.
Select additional services such as business clothing matching or expert verification.
Download the fully compliant image in digital or printable format.
Taking Baby's Photo for a Japanese Passport

A professional photographer or a studio visit with a newborn or a toddler can be challenging. PhotoGov allows you to take your child's passport photo from the comfort of your home. Use our expert tips to take the best picture, and let us handle the rest.
Setting
Uniform lighting from a natural source, plain background.
Position
A newborn may lie on a blanket; older children — sit or stand.
Expression
Neutral facial expression, no crying or laughing.
Frame
No toys, parents’ hands, or other objects in the frame.

children.innerHtml: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) of Japan sets the Japan visa photo requirements, which follow the biometric photo rules defined by the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Document 9303. Only photos adhering to these specifications are eligible for applications. But don't worry — our Japan visa photo editor applies all the rules listed below automatically, including the required size, crop, framing, head positioning, and background. All you need to do is upload a well-made selfie.
Number of Photos
Two photos are required with Japanese visa applications.
Recency
The photo must be taken within the past 6 months to accurately reflect the applicant's appearance.
Photo Size

Passport photo size is required with Japanese visa applications — depending on a particular consulate, the accepted sizes are 45x45 mm (1.77 × 1.77 inches), 35x45 mm (1.38 × 1.77 inches), or 2x2 inches (5.08 × 5.08 cm). The head must take 70-80% of the image and measure between 32 and 36 mm (1.26-1.42 inches).
Color
Japan photo must be submitted in color only.
Background

A plain white background is required with Japanese visa applications. It must be evenly lit and free from patterns, textures, and shadows. Some consulates allow a blue background, but it's better to submit a photo with a white background, according to the MOFA standard, to avoid rejections.
Lighting
Only professional, good lighting is required for a Japan visa picture. It mustn't cast shadows on the applicant's face or background, and naturally reflect the skin tones and hair color.
Positioning and Framing
The applicant must be facing forward, with the face fully visible and square to the camera. Avoid tilting or moving when a Japan visa photo is being taken.
Facial Expression
An applicant must maintain a neutral facial expression with eyes open and mouth closed. Smiling, showing teeth, or any exaggerated expressions aren't permitted in a photo for Japanese visa.
Attire, Head Coverings, and Accessories

Wear conservative clothing in darker colors. Avoid too formal or bright clothes with large lettering or symbols. Military or camouflage wear isn't allowed on a Japanese visa photo. Headwear isn't allowed, unless worn daily for religious or medical reasons. In this case, it shouldn't obstruct facial features.
Glasses

Glasses are discouraged on Japan visa photos. Keep them off to increase the chance of approval, but if you must wear glasses for medical reasons, provide a signed certificate from your medical provider proving the reason for wearing glasses. Sunglasses, tinted glasses (even for medical reasons), and colored lenses aren't allowed on Japanese visa photos.
Print Quality
Only photos printed on matte photographic paper are accepted. Photos printed on regular paper on home printers aren't accepted.
Digital Quality
High resolution of at least 300 DPI, sharp focus, no visible pixels or noise. File format — JPEG or PNG, recommended file size — 240 kBytes.
What is Japan Visa Photo Dresscode?

Following the cultural values of Japan, respect the traditions and wear formal, conservative clothing in your Japanese visa picture. Dress in darker colors, and give preference to collared clothing. Avoid open shoulders and accessories like scarves that cover your neck or parts of the face. Modest jewelry, like small earrings and necklaces, is allowed, but any jewelry or piercing accessories that obstruct the face must be taken off. Military wear, camouflage, is prohibited on Japanese visa photos.

children.innerHtml: How to Take a Japan Visa Photo at Home

With the convenient online Japan visa photo tool PhotoGov, you can skip the hassle and expense of visiting a photo studio. Simply follow the steps below, take a selfie at home, upload it to our platform, and receive a visa-compliant Japanese photo in under a minute.
Find a good spot for taking your Japan visa photo. Ensure that the area is well-lit and that you are standing against a neutral background — a wall by a window works best.

Dress properly. Put on formal clothing in darker colors. Head coverings may be worn only for religious and medical reasons. Take off your glasses. Keep your facial expression neutral, eyes open, and mouth closed, and look directly into the camera.

Set up the camera or the smartphone. If you have a tripod, it's best to use it, setting your digital camera or the phone's camera on timer. In this case, use the back camera and stand about 2 metres (6.56 feet) from the camera. If taking a selfie, you can use the front camera, holding it about 40–50 cm (16–20 inches) away from your face.

Upload and convert photo to Japan visa size for free. Browse PhotoGov and use our Japan visa photo tool to convert your selfie into a 100% compliant with official requirements, visa-ready photo. Download a digital photo for online submissions or a printable PDF file for in-person applications at a Japan embassy or consulate.
How to Take Japan Visa Photos of Babies and Kids

When photographing babies or young children for a Japanese visa, the general photo requirements remain the same — proper clothing, good lighting, and high image quality. However, officials tend to be more flexible about maintaining a perfectly neutral expression in children’s photos. Follow our tips to create a suitable picture of your child at home, and trust the PhotoGov to turn it into an application-ready visa image of the required photo size and properties.
Setting
Uniform lighting from a natural source, plain background.
Position
A newborn may lie on a blanket; older children — sit or stand.
Expression
Neutral facial expression, no crying or laughing.
Frame
No toys, parents’ hands, or other objects in the frame.
PhotoGov: 100% Japanese Visa Photo Compliance

PhotoGov formats your portrait according to the official specifications issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan and the biometric standards defined in ICAO Document 9303. The system calibrates background color, adjusts head position and facial proportions, balances exposure, and applies the exact layout and size used for Japanese visa photographs. Every technical element — from the distance between key facial points to overall brightness and contrast — is aligned with the standards applied when Japanese visa photos are reviewed.

For applicants who prefer an additional layer of assurance, PhotoGov offers Human Verification. Our top compliance specialist manually examines your image, checking alignment, lighting, head size, background uniformity, and biometric accuracy before the final file is approved. This extra step gives you confidence that your photo meets the standards used by Japanese diplomatic missions when assessing visa applications.
Frequently Asked Questions

[{"q":"What is Japan Tourist Visa Photo Size?","a":"

The official Japan tourist visa photo size is 45x45 mm (1.77 × 1.77 inches). However, some consulates require a 35x45 mm (1.38 × 1.77 inches), or a 2x2 inches (5.08 × 5.08 cm) size. Always double-check the required size before your application to avoid rejections.

"},{"q":"What is Japan Visa Photo Size in cm?","a":"

4.5-4.5 cm is the size required by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan. However, some embassies and consulates may request a 3.5x4.5 cm or a 5.08 × 5.08 cm size as the preferred ones. Double-check with your local Japanese consulate in advance.

"},{"q":"Is Japan Visa Photo Size 2x2 Inches Acceptable?","a":"

Yes, a 2x2 inches is widely accepted as the Japan visa picture size by consulates in the United States and some other countries, for example, India. However, it is not the common size — most of the consulates accept 45x45 mm (1.77 × 1.77 inches), required by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan. 35x45 mm (1.38 × 1.77 inches) is also accepted, depending on the country.

"},{"q":"Where Can I Check a Sample Japan Visa Picture?","a":"

You can check a sample Japan visa picture (or a detailed list of photo specifications) at the website of your local Japanese consulate. Google \"Japanese consulate near me,\" and visit the relevant page. For example, if you're in Mumbai, check the Mumbai Consulate's page. The sample picture listed on this page adheres to all 2026 official standards, too.

"},{"q":"Is it Okay to Smile in My Japan Visa Photo?","a":"

No. You cannot smile in your Japan visa picture. Your facial expression must be neutral, with the mouth closed and the eyes open.

"},{"q":"Is it Okay to Use a Selfie for My Visa photo?","a":"

Yes. But only if it's taken correctly, and then converted into a Japan visa size photo by a professional Japan visa photo editor:

Firstly, take a correct selfie. Using the back camera or having someone else take the photo is better as it results in a better picture.

Secondly, use PhotoGov to convert your selfie into Japan visa photo online for free. Upload the selfie to our platform, wait for about 30 seconds, and receive a digital or a printable file, ready to be approved.

Do not include a simple selfie (taken on your phone) with your application! This is a very common reason for a rejection. Use professional services like PhotoGov to adjust your selfie to a compliant image.

"},{"q":"Is it Appropriate to Wear Jewelry or Makeup in My Visa Picture?","a":"

Yes, but only if they don't interfere with your natural appearance in any way. The reflective makeup that can cast shadows or cause glare isn't allowed. Jewelry must be modest and small in size. Any accessories that obstruct your facial features, neck, or ears aren't allowed. Piercing accessories that obstruct your facial parts must be removed.

"},{"q":"What is the Best Way to Print the Japan Visa Picture?","a":"

Use the PhotoGov service to convert your selfie into a printable Japan visa photo. Choose a PDF printable file upon checkout, and print your photos on high-quality matte photographic paper. Note that photos printed at home on regular paper aren't accepted.

"},{"q":"What if I Wear a Headscarf for Religious Reasons?","a":"

No problem. Head coverings worn for religious reasons are allowed on biometric photos. However, make sure that they don't cover up your face from chin to forehead, or obstruct your facial features.

"}]

Applying for a Cambodia visa needs a lot of attention to detail, especially when it comes to your visa photo. A single deviation from the official guidelines can lead to delays or outright rejection of your application. Our professional service caters to providing perfect 35mm x 45mm (1 3/8" x 1 3/4") visa photos that are consistent with the strict requirements set by Cambodia. With the very latest technology and expert guidance, we guarantee that your photo is technically compliant and looks natural. From precise measurements to pixel perfect editing, Photogov takes care of each and every detail to help you save time and stress.

Cambodia Visa Photo Requirements

Cambodia’s visa authorities have very strict requirements on what can and cannot be submitted. This is because failure to meet these standards may result in application rejection. The following are the non-negotiable criteria for your visa photo -
Exact Dimensions
Aspect Ratio  - 1 -1.29 (height to width).
Tolerance  - Any size or framing that is more or less 1mm will be rejected.
Background
Color  - The background of the photo should be plain and light in color, preferably white or off-white.
Uniformity  - There should be no patterns, textures, shadows, or other objects in the background.
Purpose  - So that your face is the only thing in the frame.
Resolution & Image Quality
Minimum Resolution  - 300 DPI for a sharp and clear image.
Focus  - No blurring, pixelation, or graininess.
Lighting  - The amount of light should be evenly distributed to avoid any shadow on the face or background.
File Format & Size (Digital Submissions)
Accepted Formats  - JPEG, PNG, or BMP.
File Size  - The size of the file should be between 10KB and 500KB to meet the requirements of online submission.
Compression  - Avoid using compression that results in artifacts while maintaining clarity.
Subject Appearance
Facial Expression

- 
 
 
The face should have no facial expression and the eyes should be wide open with the mouth closed, no smiling or frowning.
Head Position -
Centered in the frame.
It covers 70-80% of the photo’s height (forehead to chin).

Face directly facing the camera, shoulders level.
  
 Clothing -
No uniforms, or very casual clothes that can be merged with the background are allowed to be worn.

Religious or medical headwear is also allowed but it should not cover the face.
  
 Accessories -
No glasses (only if required medically and with a doctor’s note).
No hats, headphones, or any other jewelry that might be distracting.
Our Professional Process - Precision at Every Step
We use the latest technology and the knowledge of specialists to provide the photos that are compatible with the specifications of Cambodia. Here’s how we ensure perfection -
Initial Consultation
Lighting Setup
- We show you how to take the photo with gentle and diffused light (natural or artificial) to avoid shadows.
Background Preparation
- Professional background in order to avoid gradients.
Posture Guidance
- Information on where to place the head, the shoulders, and the eyes.
Precision Capture
Equipment
- High-resolution DSLR cameras mounted on tripods for stability.
Multiple Shots
- 10-15 images are taken to choose the best frame.
Compliance Check
- Real-time verification of the dimensions and framing.
Expert Editing
Cropping & Resizing
- To 35mm x 45mm with millimeter accuracy.
Background Correction
- To eliminate shadows, patterns, or any other distortions.
Color Balancing
- Adjust the brightness, contrast, and the skin tone.
Retouching
- Some touches only; for instance, removing stray hairs without altering your natural appearance.
Quality Assurance
Manual Review -
Technicians check for compliance with the standards set by Cambodia.
Tips for Taking Your Photo at Home
This section will help you avoid common mistakes when taking a photo at home for your application -
Lighting
Natural Light - Shoot near a large window on a cloudy day.
Artificial Light - Two softbox lights are used at 45degree angles to avoid shadows.
Avoid - Bright sunlight, flash, or direct light behind the subject.
Camera Setup
Stability - Blurring is eliminated with the use of a tripod.
Distance - Stand 1.5–2 meters from the camera.
Framing - Your head should fill 70-80% of the frame.
Background
Material - A plain white wall or a wrinklefree sheet should be used.
Check for Shadows - Place the lights in a manner that there are no shadows on the backdrop.
Appearance
Clothing - The best to wear is a collared shirt, in a color that is not the background color (for instance, navy blue when submitting a white background).
Expression - Try to relax your face, look directly into the camera, and keep your mouth closed.
Accessories - Glasses, hats, or jewellery are not to be worn except for religious or medical reasons.
Editing Tools
Free Software - Basic cropping and resizing can be done using tools like GIMP or Canva.
Common Mistakes & How to Avoid Them
Even slight mistakes can lead to the photo being rejected. Be careful with these tips -
Incorrect dimensions - Use a ruler or our online template to check if it is 35mm x 45mm.
Shadows on the background - Rearrange the lights or use a brighter background.
Blurry image - Clean the camera lens, make sure the device is steady, and ensure proper focus.
Wrong facial expression - Practice a neutral face in front of a mirror before taking the photo.
Overediting - Only tweak the size, brightness, and contrast of the photo.
