How to take your own South Korea Alien Registration photo

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect employment authorization photo yourself:
1. Take a picture of yourself

Open up the PhotoGov.net photo service and take your picture. Make sure you’re not wearing any headcovers or glasses, do not wear a uniform, and keep your expression neutral. Ensure that the area is well-lit and that you are standing against a neutral background.

Finally, you can download your ID photo. These images can be printed off, or you can simply use them as digital photos.
Best Practices for Your South Korea ARC Photo
To reduce shadows, use gentle artificial lighting or natural light.
Your background should be solid white or light grey free of patterns.
Positioning: Your head should be straight and centered; your face should fill roughly 70–80% of the height of the picture.
For contrast with the backdrop, wear dark, solid-color apparel.
For correct framing, skip selfies and either use a tripod or have someone to photograph you.
Common Errors to Avoid
Using wrong size images (e.g., 2x2 inches instead of 3x4 cm)
Grinning or tilting your head
Wearing glasses or unapproved headgear
Uneven illumination, reflections, or shadows
Photos that are low-quality or overexposed
Selfies shot too near or with distortion
PhotoGov fixes these mistakes automatically in photo processing.
How to take South Korea Alien Registration photos for babies and kids

When taking pictures of babies and children for employment authorization, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.
South Korea Alien Registration Photo-Making Tips
Body-camera distance

A employment authorization photo must include the individual’s upper body, with their head and hair being fully visible for ease of identification. To achieve this, place your camera around 5-7 feet (1.5-2 meters) away. We recommend taking a few pictures at varying distances to find one that works.
Posture

While a employment authorization picture is only a headshot, your posture still plays an important role in the final product. Be sure to stand as straight as possible while also remaining relaxed. Look straight ahead into the camera, allowing it to have as clear a view of your face as possible.
Lighting

Your photograph should be well-lit and free of shadows. This is important as it helps to make sure your features can be made out clearly. Try to ensure that you have an equal amount of light from either side, as well as in front and behind you.
Submission & Printing Policies
For In-Person Submission: Print your photo on premium matte or glossy photo paper at the precise 3x4 cm dimensions.
Before submitting via the Immigration Service portal, make sure the file is JPEG or PNG format and under 1 MB.

children.innerHtml: South Korea K-ETA Photo Maker

Applying for the South Korea K-ETA (Korea Electronic Travel Authorization) requires a suitable photo. The South Korean government wants a 3.5x4.5 cm (35x45 mm) shot that satisfies certain technical and aesthetic criteria. Any variation from these criteria could result in processing delays or application denial.

      PhotoGov helps you produce a K-ETA photo that exactly fits South Korea's criteria. Whether digitally or printed, upload a selfie or photo and we will automatically resize, crop, and improve it to satisfy the required requirements for simple submission.

Guidelines for Appearance
Technical requirements if you are going to process the photo yourself through Photoshop or other services:
Face Expression
Neutral: no smiling or frowning
Head Location
Straight and looking forward, centered in the picture
Face Coverage
Should cover 70–80% of the height of the photo
Spectacles
Not permitted unless medically required
Head Covers
Should not hide facial features; allowed only for religious or medical reasons
Clothing
Dark, solid-colored clothes advised; stay away from white tops.
Step-by-Step Instructions for Making Your South Korea K-ETA Photo
Choose the Document Type
Select "South Korea K-ETA Photo - 3.5x4.5 cm" from PhotoGov.net.
Snap Your Picture
A digital camera or your phone will do.  Stand 1.5–2 meters from a plain white or light-colored backdrop.  Make sure there are no shadows and consistent illumination.
Send the Picture
Send your photo to PhotoGov.  Ensure your face is well-lit and expression neutral.
Resize & Optimize Automatically
The photo is automatically resized to 3.5x4.5 cm, background cleaned, and brightness and sharpness changed by our platform.
Download and Send
Prepare your file for online submission or print it for in-person use.
Best Practices for Your K-ETA Photo from South Korea
Avoid severe shadows by using gentle, natural light or indirect artificial illumination.
Stand against a solid white or light-colored wall. Stay away from background distractions.
Make sure your head is facing straight ahead and in the middle. The height of the picture should be mostly 70–80% your face.
Wear dark, solid hues. Steer clear of tops in white or vivid hues.
How to take your own South Korea K-ETA photo

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect K-ETA photo yourself:
1. Take a picture of yourself

Open up the PhotoGov.net photo service and take your picture. Make sure you’re not wearing any headcovers or glasses, do not wear a uniform, and keep your expression neutral. Ensure that the area is well-lit and that you are standing against a neutral background.

children.innerHtml: 3. Receive your Passport Photo
Finally, you can download your ID photo. These images can be printed off, or you can simply use them as digital photos.
Common Errors to Avoid
Using a passport photo instead of the necessary 3.5x4.5 cm (35x45 millimeter) size
Wearing head coverings or eyewear that block the face unless for religious or medical reasons.
Background with shadows, patterns, or objects
Underexposure or overexposure of the photograph
Not facing the camera straight on or tilting
PhotoGov guarantees your photo is compliant by automatically finding and fixing these problems.
Extra Compliance Advice
Avoid digital changes to facial characteristics
Make sure the picture is clear, not pixelated or blurry
The face should take up 70–80% of the height of the picture
Digital submission: JPEG or PNG, under 1 MB
Submission & Printing Policies
For In-Person Submission: Print your photo on high-quality matte or glossy photo paper in the precise 3.5x4.5 centimeter size.
Upload the photo to the K-ETA web system for digital submission. Make sure the file is under the size restrictions and in JPEG or PNG format.

One of the most crucial things you need to do when you apply for a South Korea Registration Card is to send in the right photo.  To be accepted, this photo must fulfill very strict standards. Even tiny faults can cause your application to be delayed or turned down.   But don't worry!  You may quickly take the perfect picture for your South Korea Registration Card using just your phone with PhotoGov.net.  You don't need a professional photo studio or photo booth.

What your South Korea registration card photo means

Your South Korea registration card photo is more than just a normal headshot. It's an official part of your ID and is utilized by the government.  The authorities need the photo to be a certain size, have a certain backdrop, and be of a certain quality.  Your application can be delayed or turned down if your photo doesn't fulfill the official requirements.
You don't have to worry about checking and fixing your photo yourself because PhotoGov.net does it for you and makes sure it meets all of South Korea's severe requirements.

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect employment authorization photo yourself:

children.innerHtml: Things You Shouldn't Do
Here are some frequent problems that could cause your application for a South Korea registration card to be delayed or turned down:
Wrong background: The background must be a solid white or light gray color with no patterns or shadows
Your photo must be exactly 35x45 mm; the size is wrong
Bad lighting: Don't let shadows or dark spots hide your face or surroundings
You need to have a neutral face, not a smile or frown
If you wear glasses, ensure sure there isn't any glare or reflection on them

children.innerHtml: Can i take my employment authorization picture at home?
So long as you’re willing to put in the effort to take a good photograph, there’s nothing stopping you from taking your employment authorization picture at home. Simply follow these steps:
Observe the proper dress code.
Ensure your area is well-lit.
Take the picture up against a neutral background.
Important Parts of PhotoGov
This is why PhotoGov is the easiest and most reliable way to get a picture of your South Korea Registration Card:
Crop
This tool will automatically crop your photo to the right size of 35x45 mm
Resize
Changes the size of the picture to match the official size for your South Korean registration card photo
Background removal
This takes away any distracting background and replaces it with a color that is acceptable (white or light gray)
Auto-adjustment
Changes the brightness, sharpness, and contrast to make sure the picture is clear
How to take South Korea registration card photos for babies and kids

When taking pictures of babies and children for employment authorization, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.

children.innerHtml: How to Take a Perfect South Korean Passport Photo at Home
Opt for Even Face Illumination
– No harsh shadows on the face or background.
Use a Plain White Wall
– A white or beige wall is ideal.
Keep a Straight Posture
– Direct your face to the camera with a blank expression.
Upload to PhotoGov
– Our AI will automatically crop, adjust lighting, and remove background.
Download & Print
– Print your South Korean passport photo online in just a few seconds.
Top Tips for Avoiding Common Photo Rejections
Shadows on Face or Background – Ensure proper lighting.
Wrong Background – Backgrounds must be white or light-colored.
Head Tilted or Not Aligned – Keep your head straight and level.
Glare from Glasses – Remove glasses or slightly tilt your head to avoid reflections.
More Photo Compliance Tips
No Digital Edits – No photo retouching or artificial edits.
Cover Whole Face – Hair should be pulled back so it does not cover the eyes or forehead.
No Color Adjustments or Filters – Preserve natural skin tones.
Guidelines for Submission & Printing
Digital Applications – Ensure the correct file type and size before uploading.
Physical Applications – Your passport photo should be printed on matte or glossy paper.
Further Guidance on South Korean Passport Applications
Make sure you also have the following before submitting your South Korean passport photo:
Identification Documents – Previous passport, national ID, or birth certificate.
Two Application Forms – Ensure all the information is accurate and up to date.
Application Fees – Payment of passport application fees is required in most cases before processing.
South Korean Passport Photo Printing Locations
CVS, Walgreens, Walmart – Print your passport photo at major photo centers.
PhotoGov Digital Download – A high-resolution passport photo that is ready for submission.

Lighting

Best Practices for Your South Korean Visa Photo
Lighting: Soft artificial light or natural light from a window. Steer clear of intense sunshine.
Stand against a basic white or light-colored wall. Steer clear of any background patterns or distractions.
Keep your head in the middle of the picture. Your face have occupies 70-80% of the picture.
Avoid white tops and choose solid black clothes to offset the light backdrop.

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect visa photo yourself:

To make sure your photo meets all Myanmar visa requirements, follow these steps:
Choose a well-lit environment

Glare on Glasses – Remove glasses or adjust the angle to reduce reflections.
Face Too Close or Too Far – Ensure that the face fits properly within the frame.
Additional Compliance Tips
No Digital Edits – Do not retouch or alter facial features.
Natural Lighting Only – Avoid colored lights that distort skin tones.
Face Must Be Clear – Hair should not cover your hairline or eyes.
Clarity and Focus – Ensure the image is sharp and free from blurriness.
Submission and Printing Instructions

More for Visitors Applying for a Myanmar Visa

Passport – It should be valid for at least the next six months from your date of arrival.
Visa Application Form – Fill up a Myanmar visa application form with appropriate data.
Travel Itinerary – Flight bookings, hotel reservations, or a letter of invitation from a host in Myanmar.
Payment Confirmation – Proof of visa application fee payment.
Where Can You Submit a Myanmar Visa Application?
Different nationalities have different methods for obtaining Myanmar visas:
e-Visa on Arrival – You can apply for this visa online through the Myanmar eVisa portal if you are a citizen of certain eligible countries.
Embassy or Consulate Application – Required for applicants not eligible for the eVisa system due to nationality.
Visa on Arrival – In rare instances, usually for business people, government officials, and their relatives.

The eVISA system accepts only the correct file type and size, which is the most common reason uploads fail. To make sure your Malaysia visa application goes smoothly it's important to follow the photo guidelines. These essential requirements are as follows. A Malaysian passport uses the same 35 x 50 mm format, and our Malaysia passport photo requirements guide sets out the rest of its rules.
Before printing, ensure your photo meets the proper specifications:
Photo Freshness
The picture must be recent taken within the month.
Dimensions
The photo should measure 35x50mm.
Background
Opt for a light colored background, better the white one.
Facial Expression
Maintain a neutral expression with a clear full-face view.
Accessories
Refrain from wearing glasses, headwear or anything that may cause shadows unless for religious purposes.
Size
The photo must strictly be 35x50mm. Any deviation will result in the rejection of the photo, requiring it to be retaken.
Color

The photo must be in color, with a neutral white or off-white background to facilitate easy identification. The image should be clear, free of distractions, and not digitally enhanced (e.g., no color adjustments).

For infants and kids follow these suggestions:
Newborns. Lay a sheet on the ground and place the baby on it.
Babies. Sit them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet. If necessary, support their head with a hand behind the sheet making sure no one else is visible in the frame.

children.innerHtml: Amazing Dutch Passport Photos: 35 mm x 45 mm

If you apply for a Dutch passport, a correctly formatted photo is mandatory. The Dutch Government has strict 35mm x 45mm photo specifications to ensure biometric accuracy. Not up to standards get you delays or rejection. PhotoGov is a solution that will create passport photos quickly and easily along with full compliance.
Auto-crop the photo to fit the Netherlands employment authorization size (free online tool)
Full document requirements for photos
How to get a photo - tutorial
Get photo for: Dutch ID card 35x45 mm (3.5x4.5 cm)
Why Should You Use PhotoGov for Your Dutch Passport Photo?
Guaranteed Strict Compliance
Your photo meets Dutch passport requirements.
Auto-Sizing Functionality
Automatically crops your image to the size of 35mm x 45mm.
Background Perfection
Guarantees a consistent, white or light background.
High-Resolution Optimization
Balances brightness, contrast and sharpness.
Print and Digital
Optimized for online or physical passport applications.
Fast Processing
Get a  perfectly compliant passport photo in minutes.
*Data from government agencies
Technical & Size Requirements
Photo Size
35mm x 45mm
Aspect Ratio
Background
Solid white, light gray, no shadows, or no patterns
Resolution
At least 600 DPI
Accepted File Types
JPEG or PNG
File Size
Between 50 KB and 10 MB
Facial & Positioning Rules
Neutral Expression - Both eyes opened, mouth closed.
Degree of Fingers - On a 45-degree line with thumb tip pointing towards the camera.
How to Take a Dutch Passport Photo at Home
Have Adequate Lighting
– Use fully fledged lightings to get rid of darkness.
Simple White or Light Grey Backdrop
- Best is a smooth wall.
Stand Straight
— Directly engage with the camera with a neutral face.
PhotoGov Upload
— Our system auto-validates and optimizes your photo.
Download & Print
– Get Your 100% Gov. Approved Dutch Passport Photo Instantly!
Common Reasons for Photo Rejections
Inadequate Lighting – Shadows on the face or background are grounds for rejection.
Wrong Background - Background must be white or light gray only.
Left/Right Head Tilt or Misalignment - The head positioning needs to be straight and centered.
Glare From Glasses - Remove the glasses or angle them so that they do not reflect the light.
Pro Compliance Tips
No Image Retouching – No manipulation of facial features.
No Scarves or Masks (Unless Medically Needed) – Make sure your whole face is visible.
No Crop, Blurry Pictures – Only high-quality photos accepted.
No Filter or Color Correction – Keep raw skin tones.
Instructions for Printing & Digital Submission
For Online Applications – Before uploading, please ensure the appropriate file format and resolution.
For Physical Passport Submissions – Print the photo on a matte or glossy paper.
Required Documents for Dutch Passport Application
Also, make sure you have the following before submitting your Dutch passport photo:
A Valid ID – National ID, a previous passport or recognized document.
Notarized Copies of the Completed Application Forms – Verify that you attached everything.
Payment Proof – Payment for the Dutch passport is required before processing.
How to Print Your Dutch Passport Photo?
Retail Locations – Print your photo at CVS, Walgreens, or Walmart.
PhotoGov Digital Copy – High-resolution digital passport photo ready to submit.

children.innerHtml: New Zealand  NZETA Photo: 540x720 px Online

Are you going to New Zealand with a New Zealand Electronic Travel Authority (NZETA)?  Uploading a digital photo that meets the requirements is one of the most important parts of your application.  The government of New Zealand has stringent rules about how to send in photos, and not following them could cause delays or rejections.   This article will show you exactly how to shoot a suitable NZETA photo (540x720 pixels) using your phone and get it ready using PhotoGov, a sophisticated program that makes sure your photo fits all government requirements.
Auto-crop the photo to fit the New Zealand visa size (free online tool)

How to get a photo - tutorial
Get photo for: New Zealand NZETA 540x720 px
What is NZETA?

Visa-exempt nationals must have the NZETA (New Zealand Electronic Travel Authority) before they can travel. Travelers must fill out an online application, which involves sending in a digital photo that meets the requirements for a passport. This picture needs to match biometric criteria, which are similar to those for a passport photo but with distinct sizes and formats.
How to Use Your Phone to Take a Valid NZETA Photo
Use the back camera for a higher resolution
To avoid shadows, stand close to a natural light source.
Use a light-colored background that isn't too busy (white, cream, or light gray).
Don't show any emotion; keep your mouth closed and your eyes open.
No glasses, filters, or tilting your head

New Zealand NZETA Photo — Size and Requirements

Make sure to check how your photo will appear when printed to get the result. Save your photo in the format as instructed. It's important to understand the specifications, for passport and visa photos. Here are some common requirements:
Technical requirements if you are going to process the photo yourself through Photoshop or other services:
Size
In the New Zealand, a photo for visa photo must be 540x720 px in size. Photographs that deviate from these requirements will not be considered and will have to be retaken by the applicant.
Color

New Zealand NZETA photos must be taken in color to help officials identify you. Furthermore, the picture should be taken against a neutral background, white or off-white in color. This helps to ensure that the photograph is clear and that it stands out as it should, without any distractions. You should not digitally enhance your photograph; this includes adjusting the color balance.
Resolution and file size (in KB or MB)

It’s important that your New Zealand NZETA photograph is high-quality and clear, as this will make it easier for border officials to make it out and compare it to you. To that end, you should ensure that you use a resolution of no less than 1 DPI (dots per inch). Ideally, you should use a resolution of at least 1200 DPI, but between 1 and 1200 should be fine. Just remember, the clearer and more satisfactory your picture, the less likely your application is to be rejected; aim for a file size of between 1 MB and 15 MB.
Attire, clothing, dress code

When you take a picture for a Kenya visa, there is a particular dress code you must adhere to. The main points of this dress code are that you must:
Wear normal, everyday clothes.
Avoid wearing uniforms or camouflage clothing.
Avoid head coverings or headgear.

Avoid eyeglasses, including both sunglasses and spectacles.

If you adhere to these simple instructions and ensure that your picture is well-lit and of a high quality, your photograph should be satisfactory.
Image definition parameters

It’s essential that the photo quality is satisfactory. Ensure your picture is clear and properly focused, free of blur or noise. You should also make sure that it isn’t visibly pixelated and that it has been printed onto either matte or glossy photographic paper, as opposed to plain printer paper.
Background, contrast, and shadows

An New Zealand NZETA picture must have both sufficient detail and high contrast. So, to ensure that your photograph is suitable, be sure to take it against a plain, neutral background, either white or off-white in color. This is important, as it helps you stand out in the picture. Additionally, be careful that there is no shadow in the photo, particularly any obscuring the face.
How to take your own New Zealand NZETA photo

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect visa photo yourself:
1. Take a picture of yourself

Open up the PhotoGov.net photo service and take your picture. Make sure you’re not wearing any headcovers or glasses, do not wear a uniform, and keep your expression neutral. Ensure that the area is well-lit and that you are standing against a neutral background.

Next, upload your image and process it through our site.

Finally, you can download your ID photo. These images can be printed off, or you can simply use them as digital photos.
Things You Shouldn't Do
Sending a 2x2 inch or passport - size photo instead of a 540x720 px photo
Putting on glasses or headgear that covers the face
Using patterns, shadows, or colored backgrounds
Photos that have been retouched or filtered
Taking the picture using a low-quality front camera
PhotoGov automatically finds and fixes these problems, making sure that everything is 100% compliant
How to take New Zealand NZETA photos for babies and kids

When taking pictures of babies and children for visa, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.
Why should you use PhotoGov for your NZETA photos?
Exact sizing and formatting
You don't have to guess to meet the 540x720 pixel requirement
Designed for smartphones
Works with selfies and automatically improves the quality of the picture
Affordable
Less expensive than studios or services in person
Instant delivery
Get your NZETA photo in a matter of seconds
Easy to use
No need to cut or edit by hand

children.innerHtml: New Zealand Passport Photo: 900x1200 px Pic Online

You need to send in a photo that meets strict biometric standards when you apply for a New Zealand passport.  It's more vital than ever to send in a photo that fits the required 900x1200 pixel resolution now that submissions are digital. If you don't, you could face delays or even rejection.   We'll show you how to take a passport photo for New Zealand that meets official standards using only your phone in this article.  You can get the right size, lighting, and formatting for your photos without going to a photo studio with programs like PhotoGov.net.
Auto-crop the photo to fit the New Zealand passport size (free online tool)
Full document requirements for photos
How to get a photo - tutorial
Get photo for: New Zealand Passport Online 900x1200 px
How to Take a Picture for Your New Zealand Passport
Use your phone (ideally the back camera) to take a picture in front of a basic light background
Go to PhotoGov.net and choose "New Zealand Passport 900x1200 px" to upload it
Our program will automatically crop, resize, and change the photo to meet official standards
Download the optimized image so you may print it or send it in online
How to take your own New Zealand Passport Online photo

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect passport photo yourself:
1. Take a picture of yourself

Open up the PhotoGov.net photo service and take your picture. Make sure you’re not wearing any headcovers or glasses, do not wear a uniform, and keep your expression neutral. Ensure that the area is well-lit and that you are standing against a neutral background.

children.innerHtml: What makes New Zealand's rules different?

New Zealand has accepted digital submissions, which is different from many other countries that only accept printed passport images. This means that your photo must meet pixel-based standards (900x1200 px) and not just size limitations like 35x45 mm.
The head should take up 70% to 80% of the frame, and the lighting should be natural, with no harsh shadows or color casts. It is against the rules to use filters from phone apps.
How to Take a Compliant Picture at Home
For higher resolution, use the back camera on your phone
Stand in front of a window to get gentle, natural light.  Don't use lights above your head
Make sure your eyes are level and your face is centered in the frame
Wear basic clothes that stand out against the light background
Don't smile or open your mouth; just keep your face neutral
After you take your picture, upload it to PhotoGov.net. Our AI technology will:
Cut your picture down to 900 by 1200 pixels
Put your head in the middle
If necessary, change the backdrop to a solid light gray
Make sure the file size is less than 500 KB
Create a digital version that may be sent online

children.innerHtml: How to take New Zealand Passport Online photos for babies and kids

When taking pictures of babies and children for passport, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.
Why should you use PhotoGov?
Guaranteed Compliance
Following New Zealand's DIA picture rules exactly
Auto-Sizing Functionality
Automatic cropping and changing the background
No need to go to a photo studio
PEG image in digital form that is ready to be sent
Full Compliance
No extra fees, no need to make an appointment
No specialized skills required
You don't need any specialized skills or knowledge to use our online passport photo service.
Mistakes that happen a lot and how to avoid them
Wrong size: sending in pictures that are 600x800 or 2x2 inches instead of 900x1200 px
Filters or retouching — this will automatically have your application turned down
Bad lighting — shadows or an inconsistent tone on the face
Smiling or tilting your head will both make your images non-biometric
Wearing glasses, especially ones with clear lenses, might induce glare
With PhotoGov, you don't have to worry about these problems because it has automated inspections and compliance tools

children.innerHtml: 35x45mm New Zealand Passport Photo

A New Zealand passport photo will adhere to the strict requirements set out by their National Passport Agency and is a key component of the application process. Not complying with the stringent government guidelines may lead to delays or rejections. Photogov’s sophisticated online technology guarantees that your passport photo fulfills all official specifications so that you can present a perfect photo without any trouble.
Auto-crop the photo to fit the New Zealand passport size (free online tool)
Full document requirements for photos
How to get a photo - tutorial
Get photo for: New Zealand Passport Offline
Avoid These Common Mistakes
Avoid Shadows in Background – Stand a little away from the wall to prevent shadows.
Overexposure or Underexposure – Ensure lighting is balanced to avoid excessive brightness or darkness.
Glare on Glasses – If you wear glasses, take them off or slightly tilt your head to reduce glare.
Head Wrong Size – Check that your head is positioned correctly within the frame.
How to Take a Perfect New Zealand Passport Photo
Select a Well-Lit Setting – Utilize natural daylight or artificial lighting to minimize shadows.
Use a Good Quality Camera – A smartphone with a great camera or a professional digital camera gives the best results.
Keep the Correct Placement – Stand 1.5 to 2 meters away for proper framing
Upload Your Image – Our system will resize, adjust background, and pixelate automatically.
Download & Submit – A digitally approved file ready for passport submission

children.innerHtml: How to take your own New Zealand Passport Offline photo

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect passport photo yourself:
1. Take a picture of yourself

Open up the PhotoGov.net photo service and take your picture. Make sure you’re not wearing any headcovers or glasses, do not wear a uniform, and keep your expression neutral. Ensure that the area is well-lit and that you are standing against a neutral background.

children.innerHtml: 3. Receive your Passport Photo
Finally, you can download your ID photo. These images can be printed off, or you can simply use them as digital photos.
Additional Compliance Tips
No Digital Edits – Do not retouch or change facial features.
Natural Light Only – Avoid colored lighting that alters skin tone.
Face Fully Visible – No hair covering the eyes or forehead.
Focus & Sharpness – Ensure the image is sharp and free of pixelation.
Print and Submit Directorates
Digital Applications – Check the pixel size, file format (JPEG, PNG, PDF), and resolution before uploading.
For Physical Applications – Print your photograph on high-quality matte or glossy paper.
Check Your Government Compliance – Our system helps confirm your photo meets government requirements before submission!
How to take a New Zealand Passport Offline photo using a phone
So long as your smartphone has a good quality camera, you can certainly use it to take a picture for your passport. With that being said, however, selfies are not acceptable, so follow these steps:
Ask someone to take your picture for you.
Position them 5-7 feet away so that only your upper body is in the shot.
Alternatively, use a tripod set up between 5-7 feet away. Move it as necessary to get the perfect picture.
How to take New Zealand Passport Offline photos for babies and kids

When taking pictures of babies and children for passport, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.
PhotoGov Features
Our online passport photo tool offers several features to help you create the perfect photo:
Crop

Our in-built cropping feature allows you to trim new passport photos and ensure that they don’t have uneven edges. This allows you to neaten up your picture and ensure it’s the proper size for your passport.
Resize

You can also resize your picture as needed through PhotoGov, meaning that the end result will be a perfectly proportioned image that will fit just right into your passport. Additionally, you don’t need to worry about stretching or squishing the image and ruining the quality.
Background removal
If you can’t find a neutral background against which you can take a satisfactory picture, don’t worry; we have a background removal tool that can help you achieve the same results.
Auto-adjustment
With the click of a button, you can have our auto-adjustment tool immediately optimize your image to meet brightness, color, and contrast standards.
How can i convert my photo to passport size?

While you can convert the size of pictures using a variety of methods, the best option is to use our passport photo tool - PhotoGov. That way, you can rest assured you’ll have a high-quality, properly sized end product, one that isn’t distorted or blurred by stretching or compressing.
I already have a digital passport photo. How do i print it?

If you have a digital photograph, unfortunately, you won’t just be able to print it out on printer paper. You specifically need a high-quality print on either matte or glossy photo paper. You can either achieve this by visiting any photo service or by using our tool to print your image off at home.
Where to get a passport photo
Pharmacies and drug stores
Well-known medicinal retail brands, namely Walgreens, CVS, and Rite Aid, proffer immediate passport photo solutions in-store. Do anticipate a charge, with most services priced around the $15 mark.
Shipping centers

Shipping giants like UPS, FedEx, and adjacent shipping facilities also cater to passport photo needs, mirroring the services of typical drugstores. At a going rate of around $15, it stands as a worthy alternative if you're considering external providers for your passport imagery.
Post offices and other passport acceptance agents

It's customary for post offices and agencies of a similar function to be equipped for passport applications, which includes offering photographic sessions. Maintaining the price consistency as observed earlier, you can typically expect a fee around the $15 ballpark.
Retail stores

Retail venues frequently host areas meant for passport photo shoots, assuring quality pictures in line with norms. Even though each establishment might set its own rate, you can usually anticipate a decent pricing range.

children.innerHtml: Appearance Standards
Facial Expression
Neutral; Eyes - Both Open but Mouth is Closed.
Head Position
Centered, 70-80% of the frame
Clothing
No uniforms or too-casual attire. Stick to solid colors
Other Accessories
Glasses must be removed unless medically necessary. No head gear unless for religious or medical reasons
How to Generate an Online Visa Photo for New Zealand
Pick the Perfect Environment
– Find a bright room that has a solid white or light wall.
Use a Good Quality Camera
– Use a high-resolution digital camera or smartphone.
Stand 1.5 to 2 m from the camera
– Ensure proper lighting.
Upload Your Photo
– The system automatically adjusts size, background, and image quality.
Buy Now - Download & Submit –
Get a Digital File(s) that are in full compliance with your online visa application.
Common Errors to Avoid
Shadows in the Background – Step back from the wall a bit to avoid dark patches.
Overexposure or Underexposure – Lighting should be balanced to prevent too much brightness or darkness.
Reflections on Glasses – Take off your glasses or adjust your body position.
Compliance: More Tips
No Digital Edits – No retouching or modifying facial features.
Natural Lighting – Don’t use colored lights that alter skin tones.
Facial Visibility – Ensure your face and eyes are not covered by hair.
Well-defined and Focused – The image should be sharp with no blurriness.
Guidelines for Printing and Submission
Digital Submissions – Check file format, file size, and resolution before uploading.
Frequently Asked Questions

children.innerHtml: Make Your New Zealand Visa Photo Online for Free — Ready in 30 Seconds

Applying for a New Zealand visa? Make your New Zealand visa photo online for free with PhotoGov. Upload a photo taken on your phone, and our NZ visa photo editor will crop and resize it for an Immigration Online application or prepare a printable 35 × 45 mm version for a paper form. It works on iPhone, Android, and any browser and takes about 30 seconds — no app or editing skills required.
No studio · No app · 30 seconds

children.innerHtml: What Is a New Zealand Visa Photo?
A biometric photo for a New Zealand visa application through Immigration New Zealand.
Prepared as a 3:4 JPG or JPEG for an Immigration Online application.
Downloadable as a digital JPEG for online submissions or a printable PDF when the visa application must be submitted on paper.
Your Final New Zealand Visa Photo from PhotoGov

PhotoGov automatically applies all official Immigration New Zealand standards to your original photo. The final image is ready for submission and doesn't require any adjustments from you. Below are the key technical parameters of your final NZ visa photo from PhotoGov.
For a full overview of official standards, please see our New Zealand Visa Photo Requirements Guide.

children.innerHtml: If your photo is rejected due to technical issues on PhotoGov's side, we provide a free retake or a full refund.
PhotoGov and Immigration New Zealand Standards for Visa Photos

PhotoGov maintains a dedicated template for New Zealand visa photos, built around Immigration New Zealand's published specifications and kept aligned with them for both application routes. Select "Immigration Online" or "paper application" in the tool, and PhotoGov applies the correct technical profile automatically — the right pixel dimensions and file-size range for a digital upload, or the correct 35 × 45 mm layout for a printed photo — so you don't need to track the exact numbers yourself.

Every template also reflects INZ's requirement for a natural, unaltered portrait: PhotoGov crops and resizes a suitable source photo without AI enhancement, filters, beautification, background replacement, facial retouching, object removal, or changes to colour, brightness, contrast, or sharpness. If the source image has unsuitable lighting, focus, pose, or background, the fix is a new photo, not digital editing.

Optional Human Verification adds a manual review of the source and prepared file by a PhotoGov compliance specialist, checking it against the current INZ template before you download it — though final acceptance always remains at the discretion of Immigration New Zealand.

Frequently Asked Questions

attributes.model:
[{"q":"Can I Get My New Zealand Visa Photo Online for Free?","a":"

Yes. Upload a suitable photo to PhotoGov and choose “New Zealand” → “Visa Photo.” The New Zealand photo editor will crop and resize your original portrait for digital upload or printing. The service is free outside the U.S., U.K., and Canada where affordable pricing applies.

"},{"q":"How Do I Take a New Zealand Visa Photo at Home?","a":"

Ask another person to take the picture — the result will be more reliable. Stand about 0.5 metres in front of a plain, light-coloured background and position the camera about 1.5 metres away at eye level. Use even light, look directly at the camera with a neutral expression, and turn off filters and portrait effects. Upload the best photo to an online NZ passport photo editor, and download a ready file in a printable or digital format.

"},{"q":"Can I Edit a New Zealand Visa Photo Online for Free?","a":"

Yes, with the help of an NZ visa photo editor. Upload a good-quality headshot taken in daylight, looking directly into the camera with a neutral expression, with head and shoulders square in the shot against a light plain background. The online NZ photo checker will analyze your original photo and adjust it to the NZ visa photo specs, producing a file for a digital or in-person submission.

"},{"q":"Does PhotoGov Include a New Zealand Visa Photo Checker?","a":"

Yes. PhotoGov is an online platform with a built-in template for the NZ visa photo. It checks the source and prepared file for dimensions, head framing, file format, and other settings, and then automatically adjusts your original headshot to these specs. Optional Human Verification adds a manual review by a senior compliance specialist that checks your final photo and provides compliance feedback. Please note that the final acceptance is always at the discretion of Immigration New Zealand.

"},{"q":"How Do I Make the Correct New Zealand Visa Photo Size Online?","a":"

To convert a photo to New Zealand visa size, upload the original image to an online New Zealand Visa maker such as PhotoGov. For an online application, it prepares a correct 3:4 JPG file within the 512 KB–3 MB range; for a paper application, it prepares a printable PDF file with 35 × 45 mm images. No manual cropping or additional editing is required.

"},{"q":"Will My Photo Work for NZeTA and Online Visa Applications?","a":"

No. NZeTA and online visa applications follow related portrait-quality rules but use different application flows. The official NZeTA mobile app may capture the photo directly. Select the exact New Zealand visa or NZeTA profile you are applying for instead of assuming one file is interchangeable.

"},{"q":"Does the Online Visa Photo Tool Work for a Child or Baby New Zealand Visa Photo?","a":"

Yes. The child must be alone in the picture, with no adult, hand, toy, or pacifier visible. Use a clear, natural source photo. If the image cannot meet the rules without removing something digitally, take a new picture.

"},{"q":"Can I Print My New Zealand Visa Photo for a Paper Application?","a":"

Yes. Select the paper visa format to receive a printable PDF file with 35 × 45 mm photos. Print it on professional photo paper at home or at a copy shop.

"},{"q":"How Does Human Verification Fit an NZ Visa Timeline?","a":"

Human Verification can help ensure that the photo you’re planning to submit with your application matches all key specifications for your visa type. Add this service at checkout, and our senior compliance specialist will manually review your photo and provide feedback on its compliance. If the reviewer identifies a problem, a retake will be recommended. Please keep in mind that none of the online visa photo-making tools can guarantee acceptance — it is at the full discretion of Immigration New Zealand.

"},{"q":"What Happens If Immigration New Zealand Rejects My Photo?","a":"

Check the exact INZ error first, and act accordingly. If it concerns lighting, background, focus, pose, or facial visibility, retake and upload a new photo. Don’t edit an old one! If it concerns technical file errors, save the file in the required format and re-upload. If the photo has been produced with PhotoGov and rejected, contact our Support team with the message describing the problem, and we will come back to you with a solution.

"},{"q":"Can I Use PhotoGov for a New Zealand Work Visa Photo?","a":"

Yes. You can use PhotoGov’s New Zealand visa photo maker for a visitor, student, or work visa. Simply upload a good-quality original headshot to the photo-making tool, and it will adjust it to all NZ visa photo specs. Download an application-ready photo in the required digital JPEG or printable PDF format.

"},{"q":"What Devices and Browsers Does Your NZ Visa Photo Maker Work On?","a":"

Any modern mobile or desktop browser — Safari, Chrome, Edge, Firefox — on iPhone, Android, Mac, or Windows. No app download or account required.

"},{"q":"Is My Photo and Personal Data Safe With PhotoGov?","a":"

Yes. PhotoGov handles uploaded information under its current Security and Privacy policies. The Privacy Policy explains what data is collected, how it is used, when it may be disclosed, and how long it is retained.

"},{"q":"Is PhotoGov Part of Immigration New Zealand?","a":"

No. PhotoGov is an independent photo-preparation service. It does not submit, assess, approve, or issue a New Zealand visa or NZeTA. Immigration New Zealand makes the final decision.

"}]

PhotoGov creates a 350 × 467-pixel Pakistan ID photo — crops the original image, centres the head, prepares a plain white background and exports as a JPEG for a digital upload.

The 350 × 467 photo checker reviews the dimensions, framing, background, lighting, sharpness, and facial visibility before the file is generated. NADRA’s PakID guidance describes live photo capture for identity-document applications, and some CNIC processes may require a photograph at a NADRA Registration Centre. children.innerHtml: PhotoGov provides photo-making services only. It does not create or edit a CNIC, access NADRA records, retrieve a photo by CNIC number, or submit an application. Final acceptance is determined solely by the issuing authority.
Frequently Asked Questions

attributes.model:
[{"q":"Can I Make a 350x467 Photo Online for Free?","a":"

Yes, you can make a 350x467 photo online for free. Upload a clear portrait to PhotoGov, choose Pakistan as your country and 350 × 467 document format, and download the finished JPG without installing an app. Human Verification and other optional extras are charged only if you select them.

"},{"q":"How Do I Take a Suitable 350 × 467 Photo at Home?","a":"

Ask another person to take the picture or use a tripod for a good result. Use the rear, not the selfie camera. Stand in even daylight, look directly at the camera with a neutral expression and turn off filters or portrait effects. Leave space around the head and shoulders — PhotoGov will apply the final 350 × 467 crop and white background.

"},{"q":"How Do I Convert an Image to CNIC Photo Size?","a":"

Upload the original full-resolution image to PhotoGov and choose the 350 × 467 format requested by the application. The tool detects the face, crops the image to portrait orientation, centres the head, prepares the white background, and creates the final JPG. No manual cropping or CNIC editor is required.

"},{"q":"Does PhotoGov Include a 350 × 467 Photo Checker?","a":"

Yes. The automated checker reviews the pixel dimensions, portrait crop, head position, background, lighting, sharpness, and facial visibility. If the source can be used, PhotoGov prepares the file automatically; if it is too small, blurred, or distorted, you will need to upload a better photo. Human Verification adds a manual check by a compliance specialist.

"},{"q":"What Does 350 × 467 Photo Size Mean?","a":"

350 × 467 describes the image dimensions: 350 pixels wide and 467 pixels high. PhotoGov applies that exact canvas, keeps the portrait centred and proportional, and exports the result as a JPG. The dimensions do not define the file size, so check any separate KB limit shown in the application form.

"},{"q":"What If the Form Says “Image Dimensions Must Be Greater Than 350x467”?","a":"

Start with the original full-resolution camera photo. The source must be larger than the final canvas so it can be cropped down cleanly. A screenshot, messaging-app copy or image already reduced to 350 × 467 pixels may not contain enough detail and can trigger this error.

"},{"q":"Can PhotoGov Make a 350x467 Photo Size 240 KB – 5 MB File?","a":"

Yes. PhotoGov creates the required 350 × 467 pixel dimensions in a file size of 240 KB - 5 MB range. You receive an application-ready digital photo within the official dimension and size limits.

"},{"q":"Can I Use a 350 × 467 Photo for CNIC, NICOP or POC?","a":"

Only when the exact application screen asks you to upload a 350 × 467 image. NADRA’s PakID app can capture a live photo, and some CNIC processes may require photography at a NADRA Registration Centre. Follow the instructions shown for the document and application route you are using.

"},{"q":"Can I Use a Selfie for a 350 × 467 Photo?","a":"

A close arm’s-length selfie can distort the face and make the head look too large. For the best result, ask someone else to take the picture, or use the rear camera with a timer and place the phone at eye level. Keep the camera straight and turn off portrait mode, filters, and beauty settings.

"},{"q":"What Does Human Verification Check?","a":"

A PhotoGov compliance specialist checks the 350 × 467 dimensions, head position, background, lighting, sharpness, and facial visibility, then confirms the file is ready or asks you to upload a better source photo. This adds a human review but does not replace the official application check.

"},{"q":"What Should I Do If the 350 × 467 Photo Is Rejected?","a":"

Read the error message first. If it concerns blur, lighting, pose, or facial visibility, take a new source photo. If it concerns the pixel dimensions, crop or JPG file, contact PhotoGov Support and include the exact message. If the problem was caused by PhotoGov’s processing, we provide a free retake or refund under the applicable terms.

"},{"q":"What Devices and Browsers Does the 350 × 467 Photo Resizer Support?","a":"

The resizer works in modern mobile and desktop browsers, including Safari, Chrome, Edge and Firefox, on iPhone, Android, Mac and Windows. Upload the original camera image rather than a screenshot or a version compressed by a messaging app.

"},{"q":"Is My Photo and Personal Data Safe With PhotoGov?","a":"

Yes. PhotoGov handles uploaded information under its current Security and Privacy policies. The Privacy Policy explains what data is collected, how it is used, when it may be disclosed, and how long it is retained.

"},{"q":"Is PhotoGov Part of NADRA or the Government of Pakistan?","a":"

No. PhotoGov is an independent photo-preparation service. It does not issue, renew, print, or verify a CNIC, NICOP, or POC and has no access to NADRA records. It only prepares the photo file; the official service handling the application makes the final decision.

"}]

children.innerHtml: Appearance Standards
Expression
Neutral (Eyes Open and Mouth Closed)
Head Position
Centered, 70-80% of the frame
Clothing
No white clothes that blend with the background
Accessories
Glasses are not recommended; head coverings are permitted for religious or medical purposes but may not obscure facial features
How to Take a Perfect Portugal Passport Photo
Use a Good, Well-Lit Background – Even Light, No Shadows.
Use a Good Quality Camera – A phone or professional camera is fine.
Maintain Positioning – Stand 1.5 to 2 meters away from the camera.
Send Us Your Picture – We will crop, resize, and place the background.
Download and Submit – Get Your Portugal Compliant Passport Photo Print.
Mistakes That Result in Most of the Rejections
Shadows on Face or Background – Stay further away from the wall and use softer lighting.
Overexposed / Underexposed – Adjust exposure settings for clarity and accuracy.
Glare on Glasses – If wearing glasses, take them off or change their position to minimize reflections.
Additional Compliance Tips
No Digital Retouching – Do not edit or alter facial features.
All of Your Face Should Be Visible – No hair covering the eyes or forehead.
Maintain Sharpness – No blurriness, high resolution.
Use Only Natural Light – Avoid colored lights that distort natural skin tones.
Submission and Printing Instructions
For Digital Applications – Confirm file format, size, and resolution before submission.
For Physical Uses – Print on premium matte or glossy paper.
General Information for Applicants to Portugal Passport
It’s not only about a compliant photo when applying for a Portugal passport. Ensure you also have:
Valid ID Documents – A national ID or previous passport.
Proof of Citizenship – Birth certificate or naturalization documents.
Completed Application Form(s) – Ensure accuracy and timeliness of information.
Fee Receipt Payment Information – Proof of passport processing fee.
Double-Check Your Documents – Make sure you have everything required for submission.
Apply for a Portugal Passport – Where?
Portuguese nationality holders may apply for a passport via the following directives:
Government Offices – Passport application centers throughout Portugal.
Obreira Portuguesa – Portuguese Consulate (when applying from abroad).

To make sure your photo meets all the requirements check how it will look when printed and save it in the recommended format. Understanding the specifics, for passport and visa photos is important. Here are some typical guidelines.
Technical Guidelines
Size
In Qatar a passport photo should be 38x48 mm. Any variation may lead to rejection requiring a picture.
Color

The photo should be in color for identification. It must be taken against a background blue, to ensure clarity and focus solely on the image without distractions. Avoid any enhancements like adjusting color balance.
Resolution and File Size

Your photo needs to be clear and high quality to aid border officials in identification. Maintain a resolution of 300 DPI. While ideally preferred at 600 DPI, anything between 300 and 600 DPI is acceptable. Keep the file size between 1 MB and 15 MB to prevent rejection.
Dress Code Recommendations

Wear everyday attire.
Try not to wear uniforms or clothing that blends in.
Only wear head coverings or headgear for special reasons.
Avoid wearing glasses, including sunglasses and prescription glasses.
By following these guidelines and making sure your photo is well lit and of quality you'll end up with a picture.
Photo Quality Criteria

Make sure the image is clear properly focused and doesn't have any blurriness or noise.
Steer clear of any artifacts or pixelation.
Print the photo, on matte or glossy photo paper not printer paper.
Background, Contrast and Shadows

For documents the photo should be detailed with contrast. Here's how to ensure it meets the criteria.
Use a light blue background without distractions.
The background should make you stand out in the picture.
Make sure there are no shadows cast on your face during the photo shoot.
By adhering to these recommendations your photograph will meet the standards, for an application process.

children.innerHtml: Professional Russian Visa Photo Service: The 1 3/8" by 1 3/4" Solution

Are you in the process of applying for your Russian visa and in need of a photo that meets the specific and precise official requirements? Our professional service offers only perfect size 35mm x 45mm (1 3/8" x 1 3/4") visa photos. With the help of our professional advice and high-tech equipment, you can be sure that your photograph will be in the correct technical format and will show your real self. PhotoGov simplifies the whole process of measurement and editing to the highest level of quality to leave you with time to worry about other matters.
Auto-crop the photo to fit the Russian Federation visa size (free online tool)
Full document requirements for photos
How to get a photo - tutorial
Get photo for: Russia Visa 35x45 mm (3.5x4.5 cm)
Understanding the Requirements
In order for a Russian visa photo to be considered as valid, it must fulfill the following conditions:
Exact Dimensions
The photo must be
35mm x 45mm
in size. This is very precise, and any deviation may lead to the photo being rejected.
Background
The photo background should be
light and without patterns, textures, or shadows
– ideally, it should be white. This helps to avoid competition with other objects in the picture, including shadows
Resolution
The image quality should be high, with at least
300 DPI resolution
suggested for better picture quality.
File Format & Size
When submitting digitally, the following file formats are acceptable:  JPEG, PNG, or BMP.
There is a limitation on the file size, and any photo submitted should be within the allowed limits.
Appearance Guidelines
The subject should have a  neutral expression,  with eyes open and mouth closed.
The head should be  positioned in the center of the frame and should cover the part of the frame as laid down by the official rules.
Our Professional Process
Initial Setup

• We first help you to identify the most appropriate setting for your photo.
  • The lighting should be mild and non-direct, such as using indoor lighting with moderate incandescent bulbs or during cloudy day conditions to avoid cast shadows and reflections.
Precision Capture

<ul>
<li>Our professional photographers, who work in pairs, use high-quality cameras fitted with stabilizers to take several photos to increase the chances of getting the best output.
<li> All the shots are taken with the right measurements of 35mm x 45mm and will show your real features.
<ul>
Expert Editing

• Our state-of-the-art software carries out very precise cutting and alteration.
  • Adjustments to brightness, contrast, and color are done in a way that the background remains uniformly light, and the face looks natural.
Quality Assurance

<ul>
<li> Each image is checked one more time before being released for use.
<li> Our technicians also check the dimensions, background tone, and overall compatibility with the Russian visa photo standards.
<li> This strict inspection minimizes the chances of being asked to submit new pictures and increases your chances of getting your visa without any problems.
Tips for Taking the Perfect Portrait
There are several rules that one should follow when taking the photo at home to make the process go smoothly:
Lighting is Paramount

It is better to position yourself where the light is soft and even.
The best source of natural light is near a window but on a cloudy day, and the best artificial source of light will not have severe shadows or glare.
Stabilize Your Camera
No matter if you are using a digital camera or a smartphone, it is important to place your device on a tripod or support it on a stable surface to avoid blurring caused by movement.
Maintain a Neutral Expression

Look into the camera with a calm and genuine expression.
Do not pose, smile, or make any other facial expressions that are not consistent with the requirements of the state department.
Background Preparation

Make sure there is nothing in the background, and it is a uniform light color.
Any kind of blemish, whether it is small dirt on the wall or a shadow, can negatively impact the quality of your photo.
Minimize Editing

It is permitted to make some changes in the brightness and contrast levels, but it is prohibited to make alterations that would change your look.
We provide the service with minimal photo editing to make sure that the photo is real and meets the required standards.
Frequently Asked Questions

children.innerHtml: If your photo is rejected due to technical issues on PhotoGov's side, we provide a free retake or a full refund.
PhotoGov and Saudi e-Visa Photo Standards

Saudi Arabia's tourist e-visa is processed through visa.visitsaudi.com and requires a compact 200 × 200 pixel digital photo rather than a printed passport-style photo — a detail that surprises many first-time applicants used to larger passport photo files.

The strict file-size ceiling (5–100 KB) is the most common technical rejection cause, since a full-resolution phone photo is typically several megabytes. Requirements also call for a plain white or light background, no head covering except for religious or medical reasons, and glasses removed unless medically necessary. PhotoGov compresses and formats your photo precisely within the accepted range without degrading facial clarity and never alters your facial features.

Our Human Verification service is especially useful ahead of Umrah and time-sensitive business travel, when a rejected e-visa photo can delay an already-booked trip.
For other Saudi Arabia document photos, see our dedicated tools: Saudi Arabia Visa Photo Tool (2×2 inch), Saudi Arabia ID Card Photo Tool, Saudi Arabia Work Permit Photo Tool.

children.innerHtml: Saudi Arabia ID Card - Digital & Print Use

Applying for a Saudi national ID card (Iqama or Saudi citizen ID) requires a biometric photo that precisely meets the standard 4x6 cm (40x60 mm) criteria.  Errors in size, background, or appearance could cause delays or rejections at civil affairs agencies or Jawazat.   With only a selfie, PhotoGov.net helps you generate a completely compliant Saudi Arabia ID card photo.  Our system guarantees ideal size, background, and resolution, so saving you time and avoiding mistakes.  All done online, you'll get a high-quality printable version and a ready-to-upload digital file.
Auto-crop the photo to fit the Saudi Arabia employment authorization size (free online tool)
Full document requirements for photos
How to get a photo - tutorial
Get photo for: Saudi Arabia ID card 4x6 cm
Best Practices for Photographing a Saudi ID Card
Natural daylight is ideal; avoid shadows on your face.
Stand against a light wall or curtain.
Stand tall, face centered and straight.
Avoid editing techniques that alter your face.
Wear medium or dark solid clothes to offset the backdrop.
Step-by-Step Instructions for Making Your Saudi ID Photo
Follow these steps to create a completely compliant ID card photo using PhotoGov:
Select the Document Type
From our supported list, choose "Saudi Arabia ID Card - 4x6 cm."
Snap Your Picture
Your phone or camera will do.  Under natural light, stand 1.5–2 meters from a white wall.
Send the Picture
Send your photo to PhotoGov.  Ensure your face is well-lit and your expression is neutral.
Revise and Maximize
Our tool will improve quality, clean the background, and crop the picture to the 4x6 centimeter size.
Download and Send in
Print it for offline use or download your digital file for online use right away.
Requirements for Saudi Arabia ID card photos

Your ID photo has to fit certain criteria in size, arrangement, quality, and attractiveness if it is to be accepted for Saudi national identity. These policies apply to residents seeking Iqama or Muqeem cards as well as Saudi nationals. Travelers applying online submit a different file: the Saudi Arabia eVisa photo rules give its size, background, and file size.

Standards of Appearance
Articulation Neutral
relaxed face, closed mouth, no smile
Sight Completely
open, apparent, no red-eye
Head Location
Straight and centered
Coverage of Face
Should cover 70–80% of the height of the picture
Eyewear
Not permitted (take out even transparent lenses)
Head Covers
Permitted solely for religious purposes; face has to stay totally exposed
Ears and Hair
Hair should not hide face characteristics; ears may stay seen
How to take your own Saudi Arabia ID card photo

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect employment authorization photo yourself:
1. Take a picture of yourself

Open up the PhotoGov.net photo service and take your picture. Make sure you’re not wearing any headcovers or glasses, do not wear a uniform, and keep your expression neutral. Ensure that the area is well-lit and that you are standing against a neutral background.

children.innerHtml: 3. Receive your Passport Photo
Finally, you can download your ID photo. These images can be printed off, or you can simply use them as digital photos.
Typical Errors
Causing Rejection Sending the incorrect size — for example, passport size or 2x2 inch rather than 4x6 cm.
Grinning or tilting your head
Wearing white clothing that blends with the backdrop
Relying on overexposed, pixelated, low-resolution photographs
Wearing headgear or glasses not allowed per policy
Background not plain or shadows seen behind you
PhotoGov's compliance tool will automatically find and fix these problems.
PhotoGov Features
Our online passport photo tool offers several features to help you create the perfect photo:
Crop

Our in-built cropping feature allows you to trim new employment authorization photos and ensure that they don’t have uneven edges. This allows you to neaten up your picture and ensure it’s the proper size for your employment authorization.
Resize

You can also resize your picture as needed through PhotoGov, meaning that the end result will be a perfectly proportioned image that will fit just right into your employment authorization. Additionally, you don’t need to worry about stretching or squishing the image and ruining the quality.
Background removal
If you can’t find a neutral background against which you can take a satisfactory picture, don’t worry; we have a background removal tool that can help you achieve the same results.
Auto-adjustment
With the click of a button, you can have our auto-adjustment tool immediately optimize your image to meet brightness, color, and contrast standards.
Extra Compliance Advice
Do not digitally modify face characteristics
No blurring or pixelation; make sure sharpness and clarity.
Face should occupy at least 70% of the frame; check proportion.
Select the appropriate file size and format—JPEG/PNG, under 1 MB
Preview using PhotoGov validation tools before submission.
Printing and Submission Guidelines
For In-Person Use, cut to 4x6 cm and print your photo on high-quality glossy or matte photo paper.
Depending on your ID application type, upload the JPEG file via the Civil Affairs or Absher portals for digital submission.
How to take Saudi Arabia ID card photos for babies and kids

When taking pictures of babies and children for employment authorization, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.

children.innerHtml: Saudi Arabia Visa 2x2 Inches Photo Maker

When applying for a Saudi Arabia visa, one of the most crucial parts of your application is submitting the right photo. A photo that doesn’t meet the requirements — in terms of size, background, or clarity — can lead to unnecessary delays or rejections. <ul> <ul> With PhotoGov, creating a 2x2 inch (51x51 mm) Saudi visa photo is simple. No need to visit a photographer or worry about technical requirements. Just upload a selfie, and we will take care of the rest — ensuring the photo meets Saudi visa standards and is ready for online or print submission.
Auto-crop the photo to fit the Saudi Arabia visa size (free online tool)
Full document requirements for photos
How to get a photo - tutorial
Get photo for: Saudi Arabia visa 2x2 inches (51x51 mm)
Why Choose PhotoGov for Your Saudi Arabia Visa Photo?
Perfect Sizing
Automatically crops and resizes your photo to 2x2 inches (51x51 mm)
Background Removal
Guarantees a clear, white, or light background free of shadows or other diversions
Automatic Enhancement
Adjusts the brightness, sharpness, and contrast for a professional result
Digital and Print-Ready Formats
Obtain both digital-ready and printable files for simple submission
*Data from government agencies
Requirements for Saudi Arabia Visa Photos
Applications made through the tourist portal follow the Saudi Arabia eVisa photo rules instead, where the image is 200 x 200 pixels.
Your photo must meet rigorous criteria established by Saudi Arabia's embassy or consulate to guarantee its acceptance.  Here is a summary of the needed 2x2 inch (51x51 mm) photo rules:
Dimensions
2 x 2 inches (51 × 51 mm)
Resolution
Minimum 300 DPI
Format
JPEG, PNG
Digital submission
Usually less than 1 MB
Background Color
No patterns or shadows; plain white or light grey
Print-friendly
Indeed, for consulate/embassy submittal
How to Make Your Saudi Arabia Visa Photo
Follow these simple instructions to make sure your Saudi Arabia visa photo is properly sized and prepared for submission:

<b> Choose the Document Type <b>  
Select "Saudi Arabia Visa - 2x2 inch" from PhotoGov.net
Take the picture
Use either a camera or smartphone.  Maintain 1.5–2 meters from a white or light-colored wall
Send Your Picture
Make sure the picture is well-lit and clear.  Send it to us via our system for processing
Automatic Resize & Improve
To fit the 2x2 inch format, our system will automatically crop, resize, and enhance the image
Download and Send in
Once processed, the image can be printed for your Saudi visa application or downloaded as a digital file
Best Practices for Taking a Saudi Visa Picture
These tips can help you to make sure your photo satisfies Saudi embassy requirements:
Avoid shadows by using natural light or gentle interior lighting. Stand by a window.
Use a plain white or light-colored wall. Our system will fix minor flaws.
Hold the camera or phone at eye level and make sure your face occupies roughly 70–80% of the picture.
Wear dark, plain clothing to offset the light backdrop. Don't wear patterned or colorful clothing.
Steer clear of selfies; use a tripod or ask someone else to snap the picture to prevent angle distortion.

children.innerHtml: How to take your own Saudi Arabia visa photo

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect visa photo yourself:
1. Take a picture of yourself

Open up the PhotoGov.net photo service and take your picture. Make sure you’re not wearing any headcovers or glasses, do not wear a uniform, and keep your expression neutral. Ensure that the area is well-lit and that you are standing against a neutral background.

Next, upload your image and process it through our site.

children.innerHtml: 3. Receive your Passport Photo
Finally, you can download your ID photo. These images can be printed off, or you can simply use them as digital photos.
Mistakes Often Made to Avoid
When photographing for your Saudi Arabia visa, keep an eye out for these typical errors:
Using the incorrect size—ensure it is precisely 2x2 inches (51x51 mm).
Wearing white or reflective clothing that matches the background
Relying on low-quality images or selfies
Wearing glasses is not advised unless absolutely required.
Ignoring or turning your head.
Background or facial shadows
You need not be concerned about denials since PhotoGov will automatically address these problems.
How to take Saudi Arabia visa photos for babies and kids

When taking pictures of babies and children for visa, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.

children.innerHtml: Saudi Arabia Work Permit Photo – 4x6 cm

When applying for a Saudi Arabia work permit, one of the first things you'll need is a compliant photo. The Saudi government requires a 4x6 cm (40x60 mm) photo for work permits and other official documents. Getting this right is crucial — even small mistakes can delay your application.  With PhotoGov, you can create a 4x6 cm photo that meets all the official specifications — quickly and easily using your smartphone or camera. Whether you need a digital file or a physical print, we’ve got you covered.

Photo Requirements for Saudi Arabia Work Permit

To ensure your photo meets Saudi Arabia’s official requirements, here are the key specifications you need to follow. Not following these guidelines could lead to delays or rejection of your application. An eVisa is submitted online in a smaller digital format, and our Saudi eVisa photo rules page lists the pixel size and file limits.

Size

Resolution

Image Format

File Size

Printable
Yes – required for in-person applications

children.innerHtml: How to Create Your Saudi Arabia Work Permit Photo
Follow these simple steps to create a compliant photo using PhotoGov:
Select Document Type
Choose "Saudi Arabia Work Permit – 4x6 cm" on PhotoGov.net
Capture the Photo
Use a high-resolution camera or smartphone. Stand 1.5–2 meters away from the camera in a well-lit environment
Upload Your Photo
Upload the image to our platform. Ensure the background is plain and your lighting is even
Auto Edit and Enhance
We’ll crop the image to the correct size, adjust the background, and enhance lighting and sharpness
Download and Submit
Download your ready-to-use digital file, or print it for physical submission
Best Practices for Taking a Saudi Arabia Work Permit Photo
Lighting: Use natural or soft artificial light. Avoid harsh direct light or shadows on your face
Background: Use a plain white or light-colored wall. Avoid busy or patterned backgrounds
Framing: Ensure your face is centered and takes up about 70-80% of the photo height
Camera Setup: Use a tripod or stable surface to avoid blurry images
Clothing: Avoid bright or white clothing; dark, solid colors work best for contrast
How to take your own Saudi Arabia work permit photo

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect work permit photo yourself:
1. Take a picture of yourself

Open up the PhotoGov.net photo service and take your picture. Make sure you’re not wearing any headcovers or glasses, do not wear a uniform, and keep your expression neutral. Ensure that the area is well-lit and that you are standing against a neutral background.

children.innerHtml: Our service is built to meet all current Singapore visa photo rules. However, the final acceptance of your photo is always at the full discretion of the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority Singapore (ICA).
PhotoGov and the ICA Rules for Visa Photos

PhotoGov is an online service that helps you produce an application-ready Singapore visa photo that meets all current ICA photo standards — 35x45 mm size, plain white background, correct crop and alignment, and all essential biometric parameters. In accordance with strict ICAO biometric standards for machine-readable documents, we never digitally enhance or alter your facial features. The passport itself follows the ICA standard described in our Singapore passport photo requirements guide.

The official ICA visa photo template is regularly reviewed and updated by the PhotoGov’s compliance team to stay aligned with the latest guidelines of Singapore authorities. Please note that final acceptance of your photo remains at the discretion of the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority.
For applications requiring the highest level of precision, you can choose Human Verification — a detailed manual review performed by an experienced compliance expert before submission.
For other Singapore document services, see our dedicated pages: Singapore Passport Photo Tool.
