It is very important to take your picture correctly for it to be successfully converted into a Singapore visa photo size with a free online tool. Use these 7 tips to create an acceptable picture:

Find a well-lit spot in your house. Take a photo against a plain wall (preferably white) during daytime

Make sure your head and shoulders are square and exactly in the middle of the shot

Turn off portrait mode, flash, and filters

Keep a neutral expression: don’t smile, frown. Keep your mouth closed, and eyes open.

Take a few shots and upload the best one to an online Singapore visa photo maker

Wait until your image is converted into the official Singapore visa photo size

Instantly download an ICA-compliant, application-ready, Singapore visa photo.

It adjusts your photo to the correct size, head position, white background, and other characteristics, producing an official visa photo that is ready for immediate submission.

Yes. The PhotoGov online Singapore visa photo maker allows you to preview and adjust your final photo before purchase. If you’re unhappy with the result, retake your photo and download it once you are satisfied with the result.

"},{"q":"What Features Should I Look For in a Singapore Visa Photo Maker to Ensure My Application Is Not Rejected?","a":"

You can choose a reliable Singapore visa photo maker based on these essential parameters:

The tool must offer technical compliance with the ICA Singapore visa photo standards

The interface must be intuitive and glitch-free: you must be able to upload your photo in seconds

The processing mustn’t take longer than 1 minute

Two formats must be available for download: digital and printable

The service must offer reliable Customer support in case you have questions or technical issues

The platform must follow a comprehensive privacy policy, not use your data other than for photo processing, and not forward it to any third parties.

"},{"q":"Does PhotoGov Offer Human Verification for My Singapore Visa Photo?","a":"

children.innerHtml: Typical Errors to Avoid
While it may seem easy to shoot the appropriate picture, tiny errors could lead to rejection or delays.  Here are few typical errors to be on lookout for:
The background should be plain white or light gray, with no patterns or shadows.
Your picture has to be precisely 35x45 mm.
Bad lighting: Stay away from dark spots and shadows in the picture.
Facial expression: You want a neutral expression, neither a grin nor a frown.
Wearing glasses: Ensure your spectacles show no reflection or glare.
PhotoGov guarantees your photo is legal by automatically correcting these frequent errors for you.

Auto-adjustment

How to take Singapore visa offline photos for babies and kids

When taking pictures of babies and children for visa, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.

children.innerHtml: Getting the Ideal Thailand Visa on Arrival

children.innerHtml: Mistakes Often Made
Many people make minor errors while snapping their visa photos, which can lead to rejections or delays.  Here are few typical problems to be on the lookout for:
Wrong background: Dark, busy, or colorful backgrounds will create issues. Keep to white or light grey
Incorrect measurements: The photo has to be precisely 40x60 mm
Thai visa photos call for a neutral face, hence keep your mouth closed and refrain from smiling
Glasses with glare: If you wear glasses, make sure there’s no glare or reflection, and your eyes are clearly visible

Thinking of getting a Thai visa?  Your application is not complete without a compatible photo whether it is a tourist, business, or education visa.  The most frequent cause for rejection?  Wrong pictures.  Using only a selfie from your phone, PhotoGov.net helps you produce a flawless Thailand visa photo. children.innerHtml: Typical Errors to Avoid
These typical mistakes to avoid when getting ready for a Thailand visa photo:
Backgrounds that are busy or patterned
Grinning or fake facial expressions
Low-quality cellphone selfies taken in shadowy or bad lighting
Wrong pixel resolution or size
Wearing uniforms, caps, or tinted glasses
PhotoGov helps you to prevent these issues. Before sending the last file, our computerized system checks every image to guarantee complete compliance.
How to take Thailand Visa online photos for babies and kids

When taking pictures of babies and children for visa, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.

children.innerHtml: Free 2x2 Inch Thailand Visa Photo (from the US)

A conforming 2x2 inch (5.08x5.08 centimeter) photo will be one of the first requirements if you are seeking a Thailand visa from the United States.  This photo has to follow the Thai consulate's particular guidelines otherwise it can slow down your application. <ul><ul>  PhotoGov helps you to design the ideal Thailand visa photo in only a few easy steps.  Send us a selfie or a high-quality photo, and we'll resize, crop, and optimize it to satisfy the official Thailand visa photo criteria—ready for digital submission or printing.

children.innerHtml: Creating Your Thailand Visa Photo: A Step-by-Step Guide
Choose Document Type
From our document selection on PhotoGov.net, select "Thailand Visa - 2x2 inch"
Snap Your Picture
Opt for digital camera or high-resolution smartphone camera.  Stand 1.5-2 meters from a plain white or light-colored backdrop
Send Your Picture
Send your picture for processing.  Make sure your face is completely visible and the lighting consistent
Resize & Optimize Automatically
PhotoGov automatically corrects the background, resizes the picture to 2x2 inches, and improves the quality
Download & Send
For physical submission, print the file; for digital submission, download it
Best Practices for Your Thailand Visa Picture
Avoid severe shadows by using mild artificial lighting or natural daylight
Ensure the background is a solid white or light-colored surface
Your face should occupy roughly 70-80% of the picture. Maintain eye level with the camera
Wear dark, solid-colored clothing. Steer clear of very reflective or white tops
Selfie Advice: Have someone else take the picture or use a tripod
Common Errors to Avoid
Using a passport-size photo instead of 2x2 inches (5.08x5.08 cm)
Wearing caps or glasses that hide your face
Background with patterns or shadows
Taking selfies at odd angles
Images under or overexposed
PhotoGov guarantees that these errors are immediately found and fixed.
Extra Compliance Advice:
Avoid digital change or editing of facial features under No Retouching
Sharpness—Make sure the picture is not pixelated or blurry
Your face should take 70-80% of the height of the picture
For digital submission, JPEG or PNG with file size under 1 MB
How to take your own Thailand Visa photo

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect visa photo yourself:
1. Take a picture of yourself

Open up the PhotoGov.net photo service and take your picture. Make sure you’re not wearing any headcovers or glasses, do not wear a uniform, and keep your expression neutral. Ensure that the area is well-lit and that you are standing against a neutral background.

Applying for a Turkish passport is somewhat complicated, hence you need pay great attention to your picture. One departure from the official policies might cause delays or outright rejection of your application. Our professional service provides 60mm x 50mm passport images guaranteed to satisfy all Turkish official criteria. Using the very newest PhotoGov technologies and professional advice, we guarantee that your picture appears natural and is technically accurate. Regarding size and pixel manipulation, we address every element to enable you to save time and effort. This page will go over Turkish passport photo criteria so you may get ready with the correct paperwork for your application. children.innerHtml: Common Mistakes & How to Avoid Them
Small errors can lead to rejection. Keep these tips in mind:
Incorrect dimensions Use a ruler or our online template to verify that your photo is 60mm x 50mm
Shadows on the background Adjust the lighting or choose a brighter background
Blurry image Clean the camera lens, use a tripod, and ensure proper focus
Wrong facial expression Practice a neutral expression in front of a mirror before taking the photo
Overediting Limit your adjustments to brightness and contrast only
Steps to Make Turkey Passport Photos Online

If you’d like to make your own photo for a Turkey Passport, saving you the trouble of making an appointment with a professional photographer and turning up in person, there are a few important steps you’ll need to follow. We’ve broken them down for you below:
On PhotoGov.net, first choose what sort of document you are preparing a photograph for—i.e., a passport, visa, etc.
Next, take your photograph and upload it to our Turkey Passport photo maker. Make sure you follow the necessary guidelines for creating a biometric picture.
Refine your picture using our platform. PhotoGov.net automatically optimizes your photograph to help ensure it meets the necessary criteria, such as even lighting and image centering.
Download your image. You are now ready to use the digital file as you like.
Do-It-Yourself Tips – Taking a Compliant Photo at Home
Follow these guidelines to capture a photo that meets the official requirements.
1. Lighting
Natural Light Shoot near a large window on a cloudy day
Artificial Light Use two softbox lights placed at 45degree angles to avoid shadows
Avoid Strong sunlight, flash, glare, or back lighting
2. Camera Setup
Stability Use a tripod to prevent blurring
Distance Stand 1.5–2 meters away from the camera
Framing Ensure that your head occupies 70–80% of the frame
3. Background
Material A plain white wall or a wrinklefree sheet works best
Shadows Arrange lighting so that no shadows are cast on the backdrop
4. Appearance
Clothing Wear a collared shirt in a color that contrasts with the background (for example, navy blue against white)
Expression Maintain a neutral face; look directly into the camera and keep your mouth closed
Accessories Only wear glasses, hats, or jewelry if medically or religiously necessary
5. Editing Tools
Free Software Tools like GIMP or Canva can handle basic cropping and resizing
Avoid OverEditing Do not use filters, skin smoothing, or background replacement

children.innerHtml: Photo Requirements
Facial Expression
Neutral – no smiling, no frowning
Eyes
Open, clearly visible, no red-eye
Head Position
Centered in frame, straight, not tilted
Face Coverage
Should occupy 70–80% of the photo height
Head Coverings
Allowed only for religious/medical reasons; face must be fully visible
Glasses
Not allowed (remove all types)
How to Make a Turkey Visa Photo
Choose the Document Type
On PhotoGov.net, select “Turkey Visa – 50x60 mm”
Take Your Photo
Use your smartphone or digital camera. Stand in front of a plain wall, 1.5 to 2 meters from the camera
Upload the Photo
Make sure the lighting is soft and even. Your head should be straight, expression neutral
Crop, Resize & Edit
Our platform will automatically crop, size, enhance brightness, and correct the background
Download and Submit
Save your ready-to-use photo. You can print it or submit it online, depending on your consulate’s requirements
Tips for Taking Good Visa Photos
Lighting: Use indirect daylight or soft indoor lighting. Avoid overhead lights and harsh shadows.
Background: A white or light-colored wall is ideal. We will correct imperfections if needed.
Camera Setup: Use a tripod or ask someone to help. Keep the camera at eye level.
Posture: Sit or stand upright. Look directly into the camera with a relaxed, neutral expression.
Avoid Filters: Do not use beauty filters or apps — this can lead to rejections.
Avoiding Common Mistakes
Submitting the wrong size (e.g., passport-size instead of 50x60 mm)
Wearing white clothing on a white background
Blurry or underexposed images
Smiling or raising eyebrows
Using selfies with unnatural angles
Background shadows or visual distractions
Wearing glasses or accessories that cover part of the face
Our system automatically detects and corrects these issues during processing.
Guidelines for Printing and Online Submission
Printing: Use high-quality photo paper (glossy or matte). Ensure size is exactly 50x60 mm when printing.
Digital Submission: Upload the JPEG file provided by PhotoGov. Confirm file size and resolution on your consulate’s portal.
How to take your own Turkey Visa photo

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect visa photo yourself:
1. Take a picture of yourself

Open up the PhotoGov.net photo service and take your picture. Make sure you’re not wearing any headcovers or glasses, do not wear a uniform, and keep your expression neutral. Ensure that the area is well-lit and that you are standing against a neutral background.

Finally, you can download your ID photo. These images can be printed off, or you can simply use them as digital photos.
Common Errors to Avoid
Using the incorrect photo size, such as passport-size rather than 2x2 inches.
Donning caps or spectacles unless for medical or religious concerns.
Blurry, overexposed, or underexposed photographs
Background with patterns or shadows
Taking selfies in strange lighting or uncomfortable angles
PhotoGov automatically finds and fixes these problems during processing.
Guidelines for Submitting & Printing
Print your photo on high-quality photo paper (matte or glossy) in the precise 2x2 inch size.
For digital submission, make sure the digital file satisfies the embassy's criteria for file format and size.
Frequently Asked Questions

attributes.model:
[{"q":" A USA crew visa photo needs what size?","a":" The picture size has to be 2x2 inches (5.08x5.08 cm).
"},{"q":" May I use my phone to snap the picture?","a":" Certainly, provided you adhere to the rules and submit it to PhotoGov for automatic processing.
"},{"q":" May I wear spectacles in the picture?","a":" Not at all.  Unless they are medically required, glasses are not permitted.  Should you wear glasses, be sure there is no glare.
"},{"q":"How lately should my picture be?","a":" The picture should show your present look by being shot within the last six months.
"},{"q":" May I use my crew visa photo for other papers?","a":" Provided the requirements are satisfied, you may use the same image for additional papers.
"},{"q":" What happens if my photo is turned down?","a":" PhotoGov lets you change and reprocess the picture as often as required."}]

US Employment Authorization Photo — Size and Requirements
Ensure your photo looks accurate when printed. Save it in the specified format. It's crucial to understand the specifications for passport and visa photos. Here are some common requirements:
Technical Requirements for Processing Photos Yourself (e.g., Photoshop):
Size

In the United States, an employment authorization photo must be 2x2 inches. Photos that don’t meet these requirements will need to be retaken. A green card application uses the same 2 x 2 inch format, and our green card photo requirements page lists the rest of the USCIS specifications.
Color
Photos must be in color to help officials identify you. The picture should be taken against a white or off-white background. Digital enhancement, including color balance adjustment, is not permitted.
Resolution and File Size
Your photo must be clear and high-quality. Use a resolution of at least 300 DPI, ideally between 300 and 600 DPI. A file size of 1 MB to 15 MB is recommended to ensure clarity.
Attire and Dress Code:

Wear everyday clothes.
Avoid wearing uniforms or camouflage clothing.
Do not wear headwear or glasses unless required for religious or other special reasons.
Ensure your picture is well-lit and of high-quality.
To make the application process smoother it's crucial to follow the photo requirements for United States employment authorization.
Important details include
Photo (taken within the past month) that is 2x2 inches in size, with a simple background, good lighting, a neutral facial expression and a clear view of your full face.
Clarity is key. Make sure your photo is sharp and focused without any blurriness or distortion. Avoid pixelation issues by printing the picture on either matte or glossy photographic paper.
Background, Contrast and Shadows. Your photo should exhibit detail and strong contrast. Opt for a off white backdrop to ensure you stand out in the image. Minimize shadows on the face, for results.
Capturing Your US Employment Authorization Photo
You can easily snap your employment authorization picture at home by following these steps.
1. Take the Shot

Use PhotoGov.com to capture your photograph.
Make sure you're not wearing any hats, sunglasses, uniforms and keep an expression. Stand in front of a background, in a lit area.

Maintain a body with your head and hair fully in view. Position the camera 5-7 feet (1.5-2 meters) away. Capture shots at different distances to choose the best one.
Stand straight yet relaxed and look directly into the camera for a clear facial view.
Ensure lighting with no shadows. balanced lighting from angles is recommended.
Photographing Kids.

For newborns. Place them on a sheet on the floor for the photo.
For babies. Use a childs chair against a background. if needed support their head with a hand, behind the sheet.

children.innerHtml: What Is a Green Card Photo?
The 2×2 inch printed photograph required at a U.S. immigrant visa consular interview or submitted with eligible USCIS filings as part of a green card application.
Created by PhotoGov as a printable file aligned with the U.S. Department of State and USCIS photo specifications for immigrant visa applicants.
Printed at any photo shop, drugstore kiosk, or home printer and presented in person at the consular interview, or included with your USCIS adjustment of status filing.
Your Final Green Card Photo from PhotoGov

PhotoGov automatically applies all official US Department of State and USICS requirements to your original photo. The final image is ready for submission and doesn’t require any adjustments from you. Below are the key technical parameters of your final green card photo from PhotoGov.
For a full overview of official standards, please see our Green Card Photo Requirements Guide.

PhotoGov & the Official Green Card Photo Standards

PhotoGov is a green card photo tool designed to convert a regular selfie into an interview-ready green card photo that meets the U.S. Department of State standards for immigration photographs. It automatically applies all key parameters to your original selfie — 2 × 2-inch (51 × 51 mm) dimensions, white/off-white background, head height of 1–1 ⅜ inches from chin to crown (50-69% of the frame), downloadable as a print-ready file. All photos produced with PhotoGov are also aligned with the international biometric photo standards set out in the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) Document 9303. The final acceptance remains at the full discretion of the issuing authority.

To ensure ongoing compliance, our internal green card photo template is reviewed by our compliance team every eight weeks, following the U.S. Department of State and USCIS photo guidelines, and a broader set of forms — including I-485, I-90, I-130A, and N-400 (naturalization).

The green card interview is a high-priority step, so you can add the Human Verification service, where a senior compliance specialist manually reviews your image and provides expert feedback before submission.
For other US immigration and travel photo services, see our dedicated tools: US Passport Photo Maker, US Visa Photo Tool, DV Lottery Photo Tool.

PhotoGov and U.S. Department of State Standards for Passport Photos

PhotoGov adheres to the official photo rules issued by the U.S. Department of State, as well as the biometric guidelines of ICAO Doc 9303. These rules are regularly monitored and updated by our team. The PhotoGov technical crew adjusts the settings in the photo-making software whenever standards change to keep every template up to date.

For US passports, the images produced by our US passport photo maker are tailored to the 2 × 2 inch (51 × 51 mm / 600 × 600 px) format with a head size of 1 – 1⅜ inches (50-60%), centered in the frame, and a plain white / off-white background with soft, even lighting. The photo is adjusted only in terms of size and crop — the applicant's facial features are not altered in any way. The final file is prepared for printing or digital submission in under a minute.

For users requiring additional reassurance that their photo meets all formal criteria, we offer the Human Verification service. In this mode, our senior compliance specialist manually reviews your picture against the latest U.S. Department of State template before you submit it. This option is particularly suitable for time-sensitive applications, online passport renewal submissions, child or infant passport photos, or situations where a rejection would cause significant inconvenience.
For other US document photos, see our dedicated tools: US Visa Photo Tool, DV Lottery Photo Tool, US Green Card Photo Tool, US Digital Passport Photo Tool.

PhotoGov and U.S. Department of State Standards for Visa Photos

PhotoGov follows the photo rules published by the U.S. Department of State — Bureau of Consular Affairs, as well as the biometric framework described in ICAO Doc 9303. Our team monitors changes to these official guidelines to regularly update the technical parameters of our US visa photo templates.

When you use our US visa photo tool, the output is formatted to the 2 × 2-inch (51 × 51 mm / 600 × 600 px) layout with a head size of 1–1 3/8 inches, centred in the frame, and a plain white or off‑white background with soft, even lighting. The system only adjusts objective technical aspects such as size, crop, and background; it does not retouch skin, change facial features, or add visual effects. The final file is prepared for printing or digital submission within a few seconds.

For applicants who prefer an extra layer of review, we provide the Human Verification service. In this mode, a senior compliance specialist manually checks your photo against the latest U.S. Department of State requirements for DS‑160, DS‑260, and other visa categories before you submit it. This can be especially useful for time‑sensitive travel, online visa submissions, renewals, or situations where a refusal would be particularly disruptive.

children.innerHtml: USA Welding Certificate – 2x2 Inch Format

Applying for a certified welding license in the United States? Whether you're submitting documents to the American Welding Society (AWS) or a local training institution, you’ll likely need to attach a 2x2 inch (51x51 mm) professional photo with your application.  With PhotoGov, you can create this photo at home using your phone. Our platform crops, resizes, enhances, and formats your image according to official US ID photo standards — so your welding certification application goes smoothly and without rejections.

children.innerHtml: How to Create a Welding Certificate Photo
Select Document Type
Choose “USA Welding Certificate – 2x2 inch” on PhotoGov.net
Take the Photo
Use your phone or camera. Stand 1.5–2 meters away from a white wall in a well-lit room
Upload for Processing
Submit your photo — we’ll handle cropping, sizing, and background correction
Auto Enhancement
Our tool sharpens image quality and adjusts brightness and tone automatically
Download and Submit
Save your photo in JPEG or PNG format for uploading or printing
Best Practices for a Certificate Photo
Lighting: Face a window for soft daylight; avoid shadows on the face or background
Framing: Use a tripod or stable surface. Keep your head centered and shoulders even
Clothing: Choose darker, solid colors. Avoid white, logos, or uniforms
Avoid Filters: No retouching or beauty effects. Your face should appear natural and unaltered
No Selfie Angles: Ask someone to take the picture or use a timer
How to take your own USA welding certificate photo

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect welding certificate photo yourself:
1. Take a picture of yourself

Open up the PhotoGov.net photo service and take your picture. Make sure you’re not wearing any headcovers or glasses, do not wear a uniform, and keep your expression neutral. Ensure that the area is well-lit and that you are standing against a neutral background.

Neutral facial expression: closed mouth and wide eyes.

Advice on Getting the Perfect Visa Photo
Lighting & Shadows
Steer clear of shadows by using either naturally occurring daylight or uniformly spaced artificial light.
Make sure the background is clear of patterns or textures and very simple and light-colored.
Use a tripod or a steady surface to stop blurring in your camera.
Alignment and Posture
Either sit or stand straight, directly facing the camera with shoulders level.

Keep hair away from the eyes and make sure the whole face is clear-viewable.
The picture should be sharp and free of pixelation or blurring.
Use our site to confirm your picture satisfies digital submission criteria.
Printing and Submission Rules

Print your photo on high-quality matte or glossy paper, keeping the exact 35x45mm proportions, for physical entries. Before uploading your digital picture for online applications, make sure it conforms with file size and format criteria.

Use a tripod or have someone else snap the picture at eye level
Wear a black, solid top to stand out against the white background
Don't wear earrings or makeup that shine or reflect light
Pull your hair back so that your face is completely visible
How to take Vietnam passport photos for babies and kids

When taking pictures of babies and children for passport, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.

children.innerHtml: Made Simple: Vietnam Visa Photo - 2x2 Inch

Supplying the proper image is absolutely vital if you are seeking a Vietnam visa. Official criteria call for a 2x2 inch (5.08x5.08 centimeter) photo; ignoring these parameters could lead to delays or rejections.
      PhotoGov simplifies this procedure. Your phone makes it simple to produce a suitable Vietnam visa photo. Send us your selfie and we'll crop, resize, and optimize your picture to the approved criteria for digital submission or printing. Vietnam visa photo rules differ across the e-visa, embassy, and visa-on-arrival channels, and our requirements page sets out each one.
Auto-crop the photo to fit the Viet Nam visa size (free online tool)
Full document requirements for photos
How to get a photo - tutorial
Get photo for: Vietnam visa 2x2 inch (5.08x5.08 cm)
Best Practices for Your Vietnam Visa Picture
To prevent severe shadows, use natural light or gentle indoor lighting
Stay out of the sun
Make sure you're facing a plain white or light-colored wall
The camera should be 1.5–2 meters distant and at eye level. The face should be in the middle and cover roughly 70–80% of the height
Avoid white or reflective clothes; wear solid black clothes to contrast with the surroundings
Selfie Advice: Skip selfies. To prevent distortion, use a tripod or have someone snap your picture
Creating Your Vietnam Visa Photo: A Step-by-Step Guide
Choose the Document Type
From our selection of document types on PhotoGov.net, select "Vietnam Visa - 2x2 inch"
Snap Your Picture
Use your camera or phone.  From a white or light-colored background, stand 1.5–2 meters away.  Ensure your expression is neutral and the lighting is consistent
Send the Picture
Post your picture to PhotoGov.  Make sure there are no shadows on your background or face
Resize and Improve Automatically
Our technology will clear the background, crop the image to 2x2 inches, and change brightness and sharpness
Download and Send
Obtain your photo in digital format for submission or print the file for in-person applications
Vietnamese Visa Photo Criteria
These are the official criteria to make sure your photo satisfies Vietnam's consular standards:

children.innerHtml: How to take your own Vietnam visa photo

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect visa photo yourself:
1. Take a picture of yourself

Open up the PhotoGov.net photo service and take your picture. Make sure you’re not wearing any headcovers or glasses, do not wear a uniform, and keep your expression neutral. Ensure that the area is well-lit and that you are standing against a neutral background.

children.innerHtml: 3. Receive your Passport Photo
Finally, you can download your ID photo. These images can be printed off, or you can simply use them as digital photos.
Common Errors to Avoid
Sending a passport photo size rather than 2x2 inches (5.08x5.08 cm)
Grinning or head tilting
Accessories, caps, or glasses that hide facial features
Images that are overexposed or underexposed
Background with patterns or shadows
Taking selfies at strange angles
PhotoGov automatically finds these problems and modifies your picture if necessary.
How to take Vietnam visa photos for babies and kids

When taking pictures of babies and children for visa, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.
PhotoGov Features
Our online passport photo tool offers several features to help you create the perfect photo:
Crop
Our in-built cropping feature allows you to trim new visa photos and ensure that they don’t have uneven edges. This allows you to neaten up your picture and ensure it’s the proper size for your visa.
Resize

You can also resize your picture as needed through PhotoGov, meaning that the end result will be a perfectly proportioned image that will fit just right into your visa. Additionally, you don’t need to worry about stretching or squishing the image and ruining the quality.
Background removal
If you can’t find a neutral background against which you can take a satisfactory picture, don’t worry; we have a background removal tool that can help you achieve the same results.
Auto-adjustment
With the click of a button, you can have our auto-adjustment tool immediately optimize your image to meet brightness, color, and contrast standards.
More Compliance Advice  No Retouching —  Steer clear of altering programs or filters changing your facial features.
Ensure the picture is clear with no pixelation or blurring.
Your face should occupy 70–80% of the height of the picture.
For submission, make sure the photo is under 1 MB and in JPEG or PNG format.
Printing & Submission Policies
Print your image on premium matte or glossy photo paper. Make sure the size is precisely 2x2 inches.
For digital submission: Put the document on the visa site. Make sure it satisfies the requirements for file size and resolution.

How Our Vietnam Visa Photo Maker Works

PhotoGov turns your original selfie into a Vietnam visa photo that matches all Ministry of Public Security Immigration Department requirements. It automatically resizes the image to 4 × 6 cm (472 × 709 pixels), crops and centres your head, replaces the background with plain white, and compresses the file to a JPG under 2 MB for the evisa.gov.vn portal — all without altering your facial features. You can add optional services such as Human Verification or a casual-to-formal clothing change, then download a portrait that is ready to upload or print.

PhotoGov and the Vietnamese Visa Photo Standard

Vietnam visa photo rules are set by the Ministry of Public Security Immigration Department and follow the biometric principles of ICAO Doc 9303. PhotoGov tracks these specifications and keeps its template up to date. The Vietnamese visa photo you prepare with our service matches the exact specifications for applications via the evisa.gov.vn portal, embassies, and for Vietnam visas on arrival.

A Vietnam visa photo made with PhotoGov is 4 × 6 cm (472 × 709 pixels) with your head centred against a plain white background, saved as a JPG under 2 MB. The tool only adjusts the size, crop, and background — it never alters your facial features, as required by the international biometric standards.

For a visa you cannot risk delaying, add Human Verification: a senior PhotoGov specialist checks your Vietnam visa photo against the latest official requirements and gives you an acceptance-likelihood review before you upload.

Appearance Guidelines

Make sure to check how your photo will appear when printed to get the result. Save your photo in the format as instructed. It's important to understand the specifications, for passport and visa photos. Here are some common requirements:
Facial Expression
Neutral – no smile, mouth closed
Eyes
Clearly visible, open, looking straight at the camera
Head Position
Centered and level, no tilting
Face Coverage
Should take up 70–80% of photo height
Glasses
Not allowed
Head Coverings
Only for religious or medical reasons, face must be fully visible
Clothing
Dark solid colors preferred; avoid white or patterns
Lighting
Even lighting, no shadows or overexposed areas
How to Create a Samoa Visa Photo – Step-by-Step
Follow these easy steps on PhotoGov.net to generate a perfect Samoa visa photo:
Choose Your Document
Select “Samoa Visa – 45x35 mm” from the list
Take Your Photo
Use your phone or a digital camera. Stand 1.5–2 meters from a plain wall under soft, natural light
Upload Your Image
Submit the photo to PhotoGov. Make sure your expression is neutral and you’re well lit
Auto Crop & Optimize
Our system will resize the image to 45x35 mm, adjust lighting, and fix the background
Download & Submit
Get your file for print or upload — fully compliant and ready to use
Best Practices for Your Samoa Visa Photo
Lighting: Avoid overhead lighting. Use soft daylight or two lamps placed at 45° angles
Positioning: Make sure your face is centered and shoulders are level
Framing: The face should cover about 70–80% of the image
Clothing: Dark, plain shirts contrast well with a light background
Selfie Tip: Don’t use selfie mode — have someone take the photo or use a timer with tripod

children.innerHtml: Common Mistakes That Lead to Rejection
Submitting a passport-size photo instead of 45x35 mm
Wearing white clothing that blends with the background
Shadows on the background or face
Glasses, hats, or jewelry that obstruct the face
Retouched or filtered photos
Our platform detects and corrects most of these issues automatically.
How to take Samoa visa photos for babies and kids

When taking pictures of babies and children for visa, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.

children.innerHtml: Setting Up the Environment
Select a light-colored or plain white wall
Avoid direct sun or yellow light; use moderate indoor light or sunshine near a window.
Steer clear of shadows on your face or behind you.
Camera Configuration
For greater quality, use the rear camera; either get someone to assist or use a tripod.
About 1.5 m away, keep the phone at eye level.
Your face should occupy 70–80% of the picture.
Personal Presentation
Maintain a neutral facial expression
Ensure hair is off your face
Steer clear of jewelry or cosmetics that could hide your traits.
Wear a black shirt that stands out against the backdrop.
Just post it to PhotoGov.net after snapping the picture.  Guaranteed to satisfy embassy requirements, we will crop, improve, and format your image in minutes.
Steps to Make South Africa Visa Photos Online

If you’d like to make your own photo for a South Africa Visa, saving you the trouble of making an appointment with a professional photographer and turning up in person, there are a few important steps you’ll need to follow. We’ve broken them down for you below:
On PhotoGov.net, first choose what sort of document you are preparing a photograph for—i.e., a passport, visa, etc.
Next, take your photograph and upload it to our South Africa Visa photo maker. Make sure you follow the necessary guidelines for creating a biometric picture.
Refine your picture using our platform. PhotoGov.net automatically optimizes your photograph to help ensure it meets the necessary criteria, such as even lighting and image centering.
Download your image. You are now ready to use the digital file as you like.
Typical Errors to Avoid
Even little problems could cause a denied visa photo.  Here is what to look out for:
Incorrect photo size (e.g., passport size rather than 35x45 mm)
Raised eyebrows or smiling
Light-colored shirt mixing with background
Visible wall or facial shadows
Wearing caps or glasses
Pixelated or low-resolution image
By authenticating your image at every stage, PhotoGov stops all of these mistakes.

children.innerHtml: What is a 1x1 ID Picture?
The official biometric photo format required for a wide range of ID applications, particularly common in the Philippines.
Automatically prepared by PhotoGov as a correctly sized, application-ready file aligned with ICAO and government ID-photo standards.
Suitable for digital upload to online application portals and for professional printing for in-person submissions.
What Makes a Photo Biometric
Our guide answers the question what is a biometric photo and lists the technical parameters that separate one from an ordinary snapshot.
Your Final 1x1 Picture from PhotoGov

PhotoGov automatically applies all key technical requirements to your original photo. The final image is ready for submission and doesn't require any adjustments from you. Below are the key technical parameters of your final 1 × 1 picture from PhotoGov.

PhotoGov: Compliance-Aligned Output for 1 × 1 ID Photos

PhotoGov follows the official ID-photo specifications issued by government agencies and the biometric principles outlined in the ICAO Doc 9303 framework. These guidelines form the basis of our processing rules, and the compliance team keeps them updated as new revisions come into force.

Every file produced by the platform reflects the technical elements expected from an official 1 × 1 ID photo: the correct inch-based dimensions, head proportions, lighting, and a face ratio aligned with identification systems. The tool prepares the final image without altering facial features or cosmetic editing and delivers a ready-to-print or digital file within seconds.

For applications of high importance, PhotoGov offers the Human Verification service. In this mode, our senior compliance specialist manually reviews your picture against the latest ICAO and government ID-photo requirements before you submit it. This option is particularly suitable for time-sensitive applications, online application uploads, child or infant ID photos, or situations where a rejection would cause significant inconvenience.

children.innerHtml: 2x2 cm Photo that is Perfect for Your Official Papers

A lot of official papers, such some ID cards, visas, and other sorts of identification, need a 2x2 centimeter photo. It's important to make sure your photo satisfies the official requirements so that you don't have to wait or get rejected. We make it easier to take a 2x2 centimeter photo that meets the rules at PhotoGov. Just submit a selfie or a high-quality picture, and we'll resize, crop, and optimize it to the right size so you can send it in digitally or physically. Square formats vary by country: our 1x1 picture size requirements page describes the 2.54 x 2.54 cm version used for IDs.
Auto-crop the photo to fit the Others photo size (free online tool)

Why Should You Use Our 2x2 cm Photo Service?
Exact 2x2 cm Size
Your photo is automatically resized to the right size of 2x2 cm
Background Correction
This feature gets rid of shadows and makes sure the background is clear and white or light-colored
Image Enhancements
Makes the picture clearer by changing the brightness, sharpness, and contrast
Digital and print versions
Get both a digital and a print-ready version of your photo to send in
Compliance Guarantee
Meets all the official standards for 2x2 cm pictures for a variety of documents
Requirements for 2x2 cm photos

To make sure your 2x2 cm photo is accepted, it needs to follow certain rules for how it looks and how it works The page on the biometric passport photo meaning explains why the framing, background, and expression rules exist.

children.innerHtml: *Data from government agencies
Rules for how to look
Requirement for Aspect
Expression on the face
Neutral: mouth closed, no smile or frown
Eyes
Open and easy to see
Head Position
Centered and facing forward, with no tilting
Covering the Face
Should take up 70 to 80 percent of the height of the picture
Clothing
Solid colors preferred
Eyeglasses
Not allowed unless it's for medical reasons
Hats and Scarves
Allowed solely for medical or religious reasons and must not cover up facial features
Lighting
The face and background should be evenly lit, with no shadows or reflections
How to Make Your 2x2 cm Picture in Steps
Choose a Type of Document
From the selection of document formats on PhotoGov.net, pick "2x2 cm Photo"
Take a picture of yourself
Use a smartphone or digital camera that works well.  Stand 1.5 to 2 meters away from a white or light-colored background.  Make sure the lighting is even and right
Send the Picture
Send your picture to PhotoGov. Make sure your face is plainly seen and has a neutral look
Automatically resize and optimize
Our system will automatically resize the picture to 2x2 cm, clean up the background, and change the lighting and contrast
Get it and send it in
You can either download your finished photo file and get it ready to send in, or you can print it out to use in person
How to take your own Photo 2x2 cm photo
You can take a job application photo yourself with this setup, though the size and format come from the employer.

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect photo photo yourself:
1. Take a picture of yourself

Open up the PhotoGov.net photo service and take your picture. Make sure you’re not wearing any headcovers or glasses, do not wear a uniform, and keep your expression neutral. Ensure that the area is well-lit and that you are standing against a neutral background.

children.innerHtml: 3. Receive your Passport Photo
Finally, you can download your ID photo. These images can be printed off, or you can simply use them as digital photos.
Best Ways to Take a 2x2 cm Photo
Lighting: To keep harsh shadows off your face or background, use natural light or gentle artificial light
Background: Stand in front of a wall that is simple white or light-colored. Don't let any patterns or things get in the way
Positioning: Your head should be in the middle and pointing straight ahead. Your face should take up roughly 70 to 80 percent of the height of the picture
Wear dark, solid-colored clothes to stand out against the background. Don't wear tops that are white or shiny
Things to Avoid Making Mistakes
Using the wrong size (such passport size instead of 2x2 cm)
Putting on glasses or hats that hide your face
Using photographs that are fuzzy, low-resolution, or too bright
Background with shadows, textures, or things
Smiling or moving your head
PhotoGov automatically finds and fixes these problems while processing photos
How to take Photo 2x2 cm photos for babies and kids

When taking pictures of babies and children for photo, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.
More tips for being compliant
No retouching: Don't use digital filters or programs that change the way your face looks
Sharpness: Make sure the picture is clean and in focus, with no pixelation or blurriness
Face Coverage: Your face should take up 70–80% of the height of the picture
File Size and Type: JPEG or PNG, and less than 1 MB for digital submission
Submission and Printing Guidelines
For Physical Submission: Make sure the size is exactly 2x2 cm and print your picture on high-quality matte or glossy photo paper

To submit digitally, upload your photo to the right gateway and make sure it satisfies the size and resolution requirements US federal forms ask for the larger inch square, and our 2x2 photo guide describes that 51 x 51 mm format.

The official 2×2-inch (51×51 mm) document photo required for U.S. passports, visas, USCIS immigration filings (also used in Philippine, Nigerian, Ghanaian, Caribbean, and Indian OCI applications).
Automatically resized and cropped by PhotoGov to U.S. Department of State and ICAO Doc 9303 specifications.

PhotoGov automatically applies all official U.S. Department of State requirements to your original photo. The final image is ready for submission and does not require any adjustments. Below are the key technical parameters of your final 2x2 photo from PhotoGov.

children.innerHtml: Our platform is designed to align with the U.S. Department of State and USCIS passport and visa photo rules. Final acceptance is at the discretion of the passport authority, consular officer, or issuing agency handling your application.
PhotoGov and Official 2x2 Photo Standards

PhotoGov formats 2x2 passport photos in line with requirements published by the authorities that use this format — primarily the U.S. Department of State and USCIS. They are grounded in ICAO Doc 9303 — the international biometric standard for document photos. PhotoGov monitors changes to official guidelines across all supported countries to keep the built-in parameters of the online passport photo maker up to date.

When you use the PhotoGov 2x2 photo converter, the output is a 2×2 inch (51×51 mm) photo with your head centered and sized at 1–1⅜ inches (25–35 mm) from chin to crown (50-69% of the shot, as required), with a plain white/off-white background. The tool adjusts only size, crop, and background. Facial structure and facial features remain exactly as they appear in your original photo — no retouching, filters, or reshaping are applied.

If you want a manual review before submitting, add Human Verification at checkout. A senior PhotoGov specialist checks your 2x2 passport photo online against the current requirements for your specific document — U.S. passport applications, DS-160 and DS-260 visa forms, USCIS filings. It is particularly useful for time-sensitive applications, renewals, or immigration processes where a rejected photo causes significant delays.

Campus cards are a separate case, and our guide to the student ID card photo walks through the setup and the file settings.

Choose the best photo and upload it to the 2x2 photo converter. Select a country, a 2x2 photo size, and your document type.<\/p>

Download your printable PDF sheet or a digital 2x2 photo and submit it through an official channel. Your photo matches all official requirements and doesn\u2019t need any adjustments.<\/p>"},{"q":"How Do I Make a 2x2 Passport Photo Online for Free?","a":"

Upload a selfie to the PhotoGov 2x2 photo maker on this page. The tool automatically crops and resizes your photo to 2\u00d72 inches, applies a white\/off-white background, adjusts your head size to government specifications \u2014\u00a01\u20131\u215c inches (25\u201335 mm), 50\u201369% of image height, crops it, and reframes for official biometric standards. Basically, it\u2019s your digital home kit for taking professional 2x2 passport photos with no hassle.<\/p>"},{"q":"How to Take a 2x2 Passport Photo on iPhone?","a":"

You can take a 2x2 passport photo on your iPhone in 6 simple steps:<\/p>

Open the Camera app on your iPhone. Turn off the Portrait mode. You can set framing to a 1:1 aspect ratio, but it\u2019s not necessary.<\/p>

Take your glasses off. Wear casual clothes in darker colors.<\/p>

Stand against a plain white or light wall with even lighting \u2014 no shadows, reflections can be on your face.<\/p>

Hold the phone at eye level and take a straight-on shot with a neutral expression, eyes open and mouth closed.<\/p>

Upload the photo to the PhotoGov 2x2 photo converter: it automatically turns your selfie into a 2\u00d72-inch passport photo, adjusting the background to white\/off-white, cropping and framing it according to official biometric requirements.<\/p>"},{"q":"How Do I Take a 2x2 Photo at Home on Android?","a":"

Use your Android camera in standard mode. Stand against a plain white or light-colored wall with even, shadow-free lighting on your face. Take a straight-on photo at eye level with eyes open. Upload it to the PhotoGov 2x2 photo maker \u2014 the tool handles all resizing, head framing, and background removal automatically.<\/p>"},{"q":"How to Crop a Selfie Into a 2x2 Passport Photo?","a":"

Use an online 2x2 photo converter to crop your selfie into a 2x2 passport photo:<\/p>

Select a 2x2 passport photo as a document type<\/p>

Upload your recent photo (no glasses, casual clothing in darker colors, taken within the past 6 months against a plain light background, looking directly into the camera with a neutral expression)<\/p>

Wait while the system processes your selfie, cropping it into a 2x2 passport photo<\/p>

Download a digital 2x2 passport photo or a printable sheet that you can print out in any print shop or at home.<\/p>"},{"q":"Where Can I Get a 2x2 ID Photo Quickly?","a":"

The quickest way to get a 2x2 ID photo is to convert your selfie into it using an online 2x2 photo converter. All you need to do is upload your recent portrait and let the tool take care of the rest: adjust the crop, sizing, and framing, replace the background with white or off-white, and apply all biometric parameters required for a 2x2 ID photo.<\/p>

CVS, Walgreens, Rite Aid, Costco, and Walmart all offer 2x2 passport photo same-day service, but it won\u2019t be as fast as making the photo online.<\/p>"},{"q":"Where to Order Compliant 2x2 Passport Photos Online?","a":"

You can order compliant 2x2 passport photos online from a reliable passport photo maker. At PhotoGov, a built-in official 2x2 passport photo template is used for creating your photos. It is manually reviewed by the compliance team every 8 weeks \u2014\u00a0the final 2x2 passport photo that you get is compliance-aligned and follows all official specs of the U.S. Department of State and USCIS. The final photo is application-ready and doesn\u2019t require any manual adjustments.<\/p>"},{"q":"How Do I Get a Digital 2x2 Photo for Online Applications?","a":"

PhotoGov delivers your 2x2 photo as a digital file you can upload directly to government portals, such as the U.S. passport online renewal system or visa application portals. Check the specific portal for accepted file size and format requirements before uploading.<\/p>"},{"q":"Which Online Service Guarantees Approved 2x2 Visa Photos?","a":"

None of the online services can legally guarantee the acceptance of your 2x2 visa photos, as it is at the full discretion of the issuing authority \u2014 USCIS or the U.S. Department of State. However, at PhotoGov, we offer compliance-aligned outputs with an extra level of assurance before you submit your 2x2 visa photo \u2014 select our Human Verification service upon checkout, and our senior compliance specialist will review your final photo, providing expert feedback on its compliance and acceptance likelihood.<\/p>"},{"q":"What Apps Create Printable 2x2 ID Photos Easily?","a":"

Many apps create 2x2 ID photos; however, by using PhotoGov, you don\u2019t need to download anything, register, or create an account. Our 2x2 photo maker works directly in your mobile browser. Open photogov.net on iPhone or Android, upload your selfie, and get a print-ready 2x2 photo in about 30 seconds. If you prefer a dedicated app, search for passport photo apps on the App Store or Google Play that support the 2\u00d72 inch (51\u00d751 mm) U.S. format.<\/p>"},{"q":"Where to Print a 2x2 Passport Photo?","a":"

You can print your 2\u00d72 passport photo at any commercial print shop, at a pharmacy (CVS, Walgreens, Rite Aid), or at a Costco or Walmart photo center \u2014 just request a 2\u00d72 passport photo print.<\/p>

To print your 2x2 photo at home, use glossy or matte professional photo paper and print at 100% scale without resizing. The PhotoGov file is already formatted to the exact 2\u00d72 inch dimensions.<\/p>"},{"q":"Can I Print a 2x2 Photo at CVS?","a":"

Yes. CVS Photo centers print 2\u00d72 passport photos in-store. Your PhotoGov file is already formatted as a print-ready 4\u00d76 sheet \u2014 simply bring it to any CVS location, or upload it through the CVS Photo website for home delivery.<\/p>"}]

children.innerHtml: What Is a 3x4 Photo?
The official 30×40 mm (3×4 cm) format required for passports, visas, and other IDs in many countries.
Automatically resized, cropped, and adjusted by the PhotoGov 3x4 photo maker to meet all official requirements for your ID.

PhotoGov and Official Standards for 3x4 Document Photos

PhotoGov formats 3x4 photos in line with the official requirements published by immigration and consular authorities in Indonesia, South Korea, Romania, Brazil, Colombia, Japan, and other countries that use the 30×40 mm format. All of these national requirements follow ICAO Doc 9303 as the common biometric baseline. PhotoGov monitors changes to official guidelines and updates tool parameters accordingly. The rules behind every national format come from the same biometric photo standard, and a single guide shows how its parameters work together.

The PhotoGov 3x4 photo maker produces a 30×40 mm image with your head centered at 70–80% of the frame height, against a plain white background. The processing adjusts only size, crop, and background. Facial features, skin tone, and overall appearance remain exactly as in your original photo — no retouching, no reshaping, no visual effects are applied.

For visa and immigration applications where an incorrect photo causes delays or requires rescheduling, add Human Verification at checkout. A senior PhotoGov specialist reviews your photo against the published requirements for your selected country and document type before you print. This service is especially useful for embassy appointments, residence permit renewals, and multi-step immigration processes.

children.innerHtml: What is a 35x45 Photo?
A 35x45 photo (35 × 45 mm, 3.5 × 4.5 cm) is the most widely used ID photo size in the world — the biometric standard for passports, visas, and ID cards in most countries outside the US.

35x45 mm is the required size for Schengen visa, EU and UK passports, Indian passport, visas for France, Italy, and Thailand, ID cards (Belgium ID card), etc. Countries that ask for a square ID photo are covered separately in the guide on how to make a 1x1 picture.

PhotoGov builds your 35x45 mm passport photo to ICAO biometric rules — 32–36 mm head height, plain background, full colour — ready to upload online or print. Our page with the biometric passport photo meaning explained shows what those rules check in the image.
Your Final 35x45 mm Photo from PhotoGov

PhotoGov applies every biometric requirement to your selfie automatically, so the final image is ready to submit without any edits. Here are the exact specifications of your final 35x45 photo from PhotoGov.
For a full overview of official standards, please see our Schengen Visa Photo Requirements Guide.

PhotoGov and the 35x45 mm Photo Standard

The 35 × 45 mm photo follows the biometric principles set out in the ICAO Doc 9303 framework, which most countries adopt for passports, visas, and ID cards. PhotoGov tracks these rules and keeps its official 35x45-mm template up to date. The final 35x45 photo you download from our platform meets all current requirements of international visa and passport authorities and doesn’t need any manual adjustments.

A 35 x 45 photo produced with PhotoGov measures 35 × 45 mm (413 × 531 pixels) with your head 32–36 mm high and centred against a plain white background*. The tool changes only the size, crop, and background — it never reshapes or retouches your face — and delivers the file in under a minute.

For an important passport or visa application, add Human Verification: a senior PhotoGov specialist checks your 35x45 photo against the latest official guidelines for your document, and provides expert feedback on its acceptance likelihood, or recommends a retake. It is a valuable option for time-sensitive applications, submissions of high importance, pre-booked filing, and child ID photos.

*Check your official authorities’ visa or passport photo background colour rules, and choose the exact document type on our Documents page to create a country-specific photo. The background colour for a final 35x45 mm photo from PhotoGov is white by default.

schemaOrg: {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"FAQPage","mainEntity":[{"@type":"Question","name":"What is the Exact Size of a 35x45 Photo?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"A 35x45 photo is 35 × 45 mm — the same as 3.5 × 4.5 cm, about 1.38 × 1.77 inches, or 413 × 531 pixels at 300 DPI. The 35x45 mm photo size is a portrait and is the standard biometric format for passports, visas, and ID cards in many countries."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Where Can I Create a 35x45 Passport Photo Online?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"You can create a 35x45 passport photo online with PhotoGov — an online visa and passport photo maker that supports the 35x45 photo size in any browser. Upload a selfie, choose your document, and download a compliant 35x45 mm visa or passport photo, skipping a studio visit or an app installation."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"How Do I Convert, Resize, or Crop an Image to the 35x45 Format Online?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Upload your portrait, headshot, or selfie to the PhotoGov online photo-making tool and choose the 35x45 format. It converts, resizes, and crops the image to the exact 35 × 45 mm (413 × 531 px) dimensions and applies all official specs, including crop, head positioning, framing, and background colour. You receive a 100% submission-ready photo in a digital or printable format with no manual adjustments or further editing needed."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Can I Generate a Biometric 35x45 Photo Online with Automatic Background Removal?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes. Upload a selfie to a reputable online passport photo maker, and it will generate a submission-ready biometric 35x45 photo with a correct background. PhotoGov automatically removes the original background and replaces it with a plain white one, sets the correct 32-36-mm head size, applies the correct crop and framing, and produces a digital or a printable file for immediate submissions."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"How Do I Make a Compliant, Print-Ready 35x45 Photo for Documents?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Choose your document type in PhotoGov, and the tool applies the matching official biometric 35x45-mm template, producing a compliant, print-ready 35x45 photo for passports, visas, and ID cards. You get a digital JPEG for online forms and a printable PDF sheet for in-person submission. For an extra level of assurance, select Human Verification upon checkout: a compliance specialist manually analyses your photo properties, providing you with feedback on its acceptance likelihood. If the photo doesn’t match the official guidelines, a re-take with clear explanations will be offered."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Where Can I Order or Print 35x45 Visa and ID Photos Online?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"You can order and print 35x45 visa and ID photos at PhotoGov. Once your original photo is processed and adjusted to all current biometric requirements, you download the print-ready PDF file. You can print it at home if you have a professional printer and high-quality photo paper, or have it printed at a local photo counter."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Is There an Instant 35x45 Photo Maker App for Passports and Visas?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes. PhotoGov is an instant digital 35x45 photo maker for documents and visa applications, and it runs in any mobile or desktop browser — you don’t need to create an account, register, or install an app. Simply upload your selfie, and the tool will generate a passport- or visa-ready 35x45 photo in under 30 seconds."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Can I Use the Same 35x45 Photo for a Passport and a Visa?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Generally, yes, because 35 × 45 mm is the shared size for many passports and visas — but background and head-height rules vary by country and the document type (for example, a light grey background is required for the UK passport photo, and a white background can be used in Schengen visa photos). We recommend picking your exact document type at PhotoGov — and you’ll receive a specific ID photo with the exact specs for it."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Is Human Verification Available for My 35x45 Photo?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes. You can choose Human Verification at checkout, and a senior PhotoGov specialist reviews your finished 35x45 photo against the current rules for your document, then either approves it or asks you to upload a fresh one. This service is especially useful for booked visa appointments, time-sensitive applications, first-time passports, or child ID processings."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"What if My 35x45 Photo Is Rejected?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"If the rejection is down to a technical fault on our side, we refund you or give a free retake. If the original selfie is the issue — lighting, head angle, or expression — simply take a new one and upload it again. Adding the Human Verification service before you submit lowers the chance of a rejection."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Is My Personal Data and Photo Safe With PhotoGov?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes. We treat your personal data and images with great care. PhotoGov uses your information solely to generate an official 35x45 photo and deletes it from our servers once the process is complete. children.innerHtml: 45x45 mm Photo: the Perfect Size for your Document needs

A 45x45 mm (4.5x4.5 cm) photo is often needed when you apply for a visa, ID card, or other official documents. To avoid any delays or rejections, it's very important that your photo matches these exact requirements. We make it easy and stress-free to take a 45x45 mm photo that meets all the requirements at PhotoGov. Just send us a selfie or picture, and we'll resize, trim, and optimize it to the right size for digital or printed submission. Smaller square formats work differently: our 1x1 picture size photo requirements page describes the 2.54 x 2.54 cm ID picture.
Auto-crop the photo to fit the Others photo size (free online tool)
Full document requirements for photos
How to get a photo - tutorial
Get photo for: Photo 45x45 mm (4.5x4.5 cm)
Why Use Our 45x45 mm Photo Service?
Exact Sizing
Your photo is automatically resized and cropped to the right size of 45x45 mm
Background Correction
This fixes any shadows, textures, or patterns so that the background is always white or light-colored
Image Enhancement
Changes the brightness, contrast, and sharpness of the image to make it look clear and professional
Digital and print versions
Get your photo ready to send in either format, online or in print
Compliance Guarantee
Meets all official standards for 45x45 mm pictures for a variety of documents
Requirements for 45x45 mm photos

Your 45x45 mm photo must meet certain technical and visual standards in order to be accepted. Our guide to biometric passport photos explains the background, framing, and expression rules behind a machine-readable image.

children.innerHtml: *Data from government agencies
Guidelines about how to look
Requirement for Aspect
Expression on the face
Neutral: lips closed, no frowning or smiling
Eyes
Wide open, plainly visible, and staring straight at the camera
Position of the Head
Centered, looking straight ahead, no tilting
Coverage of the Face
Should take up 70–80% of the height of the picture
Clothing
Don't wear white tops; dark, solid hues are better
Eyeglasses
Not allowed unless it's for medical reasons
Coverings for the head
Face must be fully visible, however religious or medical reasons are fine
Lighting
The lighting should be even, with no shadows or reflections on the face or background
Step-by-step instructions for making your 45x45 mm photo

<b> Choose the Type of Document <b> 
 From the selection of document types on PhotoGov.net, choose "45x45 mm Photo"

<b> Take a Picture<b> 
Use a camera with a high resolution or a smartphone.  Stand 1.5 to 2 meters away from a plain white or light-colored wall.  Make sure the lighting is right

<b> Put the photo up <b> 
 Send in your picture for processing.  Make sure your face is well-lit and your attitude is calm

<b> Resize and optimize automatically <b> 
 Our technology will cut the photo down to 45x45 mm, clean up the background, and change the quality of the image

<b> Get it and send it in <b> 
 Download your finished photo file so you may submit it digitally or print it off to use in person
Best Ways to Use Your 45x45 mm Photo
Lighting: Use soft, even light so that there aren't any shadows on the face. The best light is natural
Background: Stand with your back to a wall that is white or light-colored. Don't have any patterns or textures in the backdrop
Positioning: Make sure your face is in the middle and facing forward. Your face should take up 70–80% of the height of the picture
Wear dark, solid-colored clothes. Stay away from shirts that are white or too shiny
How to take your own Photo 45x45 mm photo
The photo rules for a job application are looser, and a separate guide describes the setup employers expect.

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect photo photo yourself:
1. Take a picture of yourself

Open up the PhotoGov.net photo service and take your picture. Make sure you’re not wearing any headcovers or glasses, do not wear a uniform, and keep your expression neutral. Ensure that the area is well-lit and that you are standing against a neutral background.

children.innerHtml: 3. Receive your Passport Photo
Finally, you can download your ID photo. These images can be printed off, or you can simply use them as digital photos.
Avoid These Common Mistakes
Using a passport-size photo instead of the minimum 45x45 millimeter size
Wearing glasses or other things that block your face
Pictures that are grainy, low-resolution, or too bright
Background with patterns, shadows, or things
Smiling or tilting your head
PhotoGov automatically finds and fixes these problems as it is processing
How to take Photo 45x45 mm photos for babies and kids

When taking pictures of babies and children for photo, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.
More tips for being compliant
No retouching: Don't use applications or filters that change the way your face looks
Sharpness: Make sure your picture is clear and not pixelated or blurry
Face Coverage: Your face should take up 70–80% of the height of the picture
File Size and Type: JPEG or PNG, and less than 1 MB for digital submission
Guidelines for Submission and Printing
For Physical Submission: Make sure the photo is exactly 45x45 mm and print it on high-quality matte or glossy photo paper

To submit digitally, upload your photo to the right portal. Make sure the file size and resolution are correct For US federal forms, our 2x2 photo guide sets out the 51 x 51 mm square and the digital upload specs.
Frequently Asked Questions

children.innerHtml: What Is a 4x4 Photo?
A square biometric ID photo sized 4x4 cm, or 40x40 mm. The shared rules behind every such image, from proportions to eye line, are collected in the biometric photo guide.
Used for official submissions when the form requires this particular format. A photo for an employer is a different task, and our job application photo guide walks through the home setup.
Prepared as a professional-grade ID photo as a digital or a printable file.
Your Final 4x4 Photo from PhotoGov

PhotoGov automatically applies all official standards to your original photo. The final 4x4-cm image is ready for submission and doesn't require any adjustments from you. Below are the key technical parameters of your final 4x4 photo from PhotoGov. US documents ask for a 2 x 2 inch image instead, and our page on how to make a 2x2 photo covers that format.
For a full overview of the format, please see our 4x4 Photo Requirements Guide.

children.innerHtml: If your photo is rejected due to technical issues on PhotoGov's side, we provide a free retake or a full refund.
PhotoGov and the International 4x4 Photo Format

PhotoGov creates a 4x4 cm (40 × 40 mm) ID photograph, based on the International Civil Aviation Organisation Document 9303 standards for biometric photos. Our automated 4x4 checker reviews the square crop, head position, background, lighting, sharpness, and facial visibility before the file is generated. PhotoGov does not alter or retouch facial features. If the source photo is too small, blurred, or cropped too tightly, a reupload would be requested.

Select Human Verification at checkout, and a PhotoGov compliance specialist will manually review your final photo. It is useful when a previous upload was rejected, the application is urgent, or the source photo is difficult to frame. If a prepared 4x4 output is incorrect, a reviewer will recommend a retake, but cannot guarantee its acceptance as it is at the full discretion of the issuing authority.

[{"q":"Can I Make a 4x4 Photo Online for Free?","a":"

Yes. Upload a suitable portrait to PhotoGov, choose the 4 × 4 cm format, and download the finished image. PhotoGov is free outside the U.S., U.K., and Canada; affordable pricing applies in those countries. Human Verification and other optional extras are charged only if you add them.

"},{"q":"How Do I Take a 4x4 Photo at Home?","a":"

Ask another person to take the picture at eye level; this is more reliable than a close handheld selfie. Stand in even daylight, look directly at the camera with a neutral expression, and turn off filters or portrait effects. Leave space around the head and shoulders so PhotoGov can apply a clean square crop.

"},{"q":"How Do I Edit a Photo to 4x4 Online?","a":"

Upload the original full-resolution image to PhotoGov and choose the 4 × 4 cm format. The editor detects the face, crops the picture to a 1:1 square, centres the head, prepares a plain background, and creates the final digital image or printable layout. No manual cropping or desktop editing software is required.

"},{"q":"Does PhotoGov Include a 4x4 Photo Checker?","a":"

Yes. The automated checker reviews the 40 × 40 mm dimensions, 1:1 crop, head position, background, lighting, sharpness, and facial visibility. If the source can be used, PhotoGov prepares the file automatically; if it is too small, blurred, or cropped too tightly, you will need to upload a better photo. Human Verification adds a manual check by a compliance specialist.

"},{"q":"What Is the 4x4 Photo Size in Centimetres?","a":"

A 4x4 photo measures 4 cm wide by 4 cm high, equivalent to 40 × 40 mm, with a 1:1 aspect ratio. It is a square format. The measurement describes the canvas only, so follow any separate rules for head size, background, file type, or file weight.

"},{"q":"Is a 4x4 Photo the Same as a 40 × 40 mm Photo?","a":"

Yes. Four centimetres equals 40 millimetres, so both names describe the same square canvas. Do not confuse 4 × 4 cm with 4 × 4 inches or a 4 × 6 photo, which are different sizes.

"},{"q":"Is a 4x4 Passport Size Photo Valid for Every Passport?","a":"

No. Passport photo dimensions are set by each issuing authority and are not universally square. Use the dedicated country passport profile whenever the application names a country; use the generic 4x4 format only when the instructions explicitly request it.

"},{"q":"Can I Use a 4x4 Photo for an ID or Visa Application?","a":"

Only when the exact form asks for a 4 × 4 cm or 40 × 40 mm image. If the application names a country, visa, residence permit, or ID document, choose that specific PhotoGov profile instead of assuming a generic square file is interchangeable.

"},{"q":"Can I Print a 4x4 cm Photo at Home?","a":"

Yes. Choose the printable option, download the layout, and print at 100% or “actual size” on photo paper. Do not use “fit to page,” because it can change the 40 × 40 mm dimensions. A photo lab or copy shop can also print the file.

"},{"q":"How Many Pixels Is a 4x4 Photo?","a":"

Pixel dimensions depend on resolution. A 4 × 4 cm image is about 472 × 472 pixels at 300 DPI and about 945 × 945 pixels at 600 DPI. For online submission, follow the pixel and file-size limits shown by the form; PhotoGov prepares the output for the delivery option you choose.

"},{"q":"Can I Use the 4x4 Photo Converter on My Phone?","a":"

Yes. The converter works in modern mobile browsers on iPhone and Android, so you can upload the original camera image and download the finished file without installing an app. It also works on Mac and Windows computers.

"},{"q":"What Should I Do If My 4x4 Photo Is Rejected?","a":"

Read the rejection message first. If it concerns blur, lighting, pose, or facial visibility, take a new source photo. If it concerns the dimensions, square crop, or file format, contact PhotoGov Support and include the exact message. If the problem was caused by PhotoGov’s processing, we provide a free retake or refund under the applicable terms.

"},{"q":"Is My Photo and Personal Data Safe With PhotoGov?","a":"

Yes. PhotoGov handles uploaded information under its current Security and Privacy policies. The Privacy Policy explains what data is collected, how it is used, when it may be disclosed, and how long it is retained.

"},{"q":"Is PhotoGov a Government 4x4 Photo Service?","a":"

No. PhotoGov is an independent photo-making service. It does not issue documents, submit applications, or approve photos. It prepares the image file; the organisation receiving your application makes the final decision.

"}]
