children.innerHtml: What is a 5x5 Photo?

A square ID photo 5×5 cm (50 × 50 mm), accepted by the passport, visa, and ID applications in multiple countries. Recruiters ask for a different crop, and our step-by-step guide explains the job application photo size to use.

Produced by PhotoGov to ICAO biometric proportions — right head size, neutral background, full color — and ready to submit. A separate guide explains what makes a photo biometric and why machine reading depends on those proportions.
Can be submitted online via application portals, or printed for an in-person submission. For US documents, our 2x2 photo requirements guide describes the inch-based square and the forms that use it.
Your Final 5x5 Photo from PhotoGov

PhotoGov automatically applies all official requirements to your original photo. The final image is ready for submission and doesn’t require any adjustments from you. Below are the key technical parameters of your final 5x5 photo from PhotoGov.

PhotoGov: Compliance-Aligned Output for 5x5 ID Photos

PhotoGov follows the official ID-photo specifications issued by government agencies and the biometric principles outlined in the ICAO Doc 9303 framework. These guidelines form the basis of our processing rules, and the compliance team keeps them updated as new revisions come into force.

Every file produced by the platform reflects the technical elements expected from an official 5x5 ID photo: the correct 5x5 cm (50x50 mm) size, framing, lighting, and face proportions (70-80% of the shot). PhotoGov prepares the final image without altering facial features or cosmetic editing and delivers a ready-to-print or digital file within seconds. Smaller square formats follow their own specification: the 1x1 picture size rules apply to IDs used in the Philippines and elsewhere.

For applications of high importance, PhotoGov offers the Human Verification service — our senior compliance specialist manually reviews your final photo against the latest ICAO and government ID photo requirements before you submit it. This option is particularly suitable for time-sensitive applications, online application uploads, child or infant ID photos, or situations where a rejection would cause significant inconvenience.

[{"q":"How to Take a 5x5 Photo Using a Phone?","a":"

Stand a couple of steps from a plain, light wall and face a window so daylight falls evenly on you. Hold the phone at eye level, look straight into the lens, keep a relaxed neutral expression with your mouth closed, and switch off any beauty filters. Upload the sharpest shot to PhotoGov, pick the 5x5 photo size format, and the tool takes care of the crop, head size, and background.

"},{"q":"What Does a 5x5 Photo Example Look Like?","a":"

A good 5x5 photo example is a sharp, square image measuring 5 × 5 cm (50 × 50 mm, or 1.97 × 1.97 inches): head centered, eyes open and looking directly into the camera, a neutral facial expression (no smiling), even lighting, and a plain white or light background with no shadows. Avoid headwear (only religious and medical is allowed), preferably, take your glasses off to avoid glare, and wear clothing in darker colors (camouflage and military wear aren’t accepted).

"},{"q":"What is the 5x5 Photo Size in cm, mm, and Inches?","a":"

A 5x5 photo size is exactly 5 × 5 cm, or 50 × 50 mm, or 1.97 × 1.97 inches. It is a 1:1 square format, so be mindful when cropping your photo for submission.

"},{"q":"Can I Make a 5x5 Photo Online for Free?","a":"

Yes. You can use our PhotoGov free 5x5 photo maker: upload your selfie, choose 5x5 photo size as your document type, wait while the software fits it to the 5x5 photo format, and download a digital or a printable photo in under 30 seconds. The service is free in all countries outside the US, UK, and Canada, where our affordable pricing applies for extra prints and premium add-ons.

"},{"q":"How Do I Convert a Photo to the 5x5 Size?","a":"

Open a reliable online 5x5 photo converter, upload your recent selfie, and choose the 5x5 (50 × 50 mm) format. The tool re-crops and rescales it to the exact square proportions and swaps in a clean background. A US 2 × 2-inch photo can be converted too, since the two sizes are very close but not identical.

"},{"q":"Where Can I Print a 5x5 Photo?","a":"

You can print a 5x5 photo at a copy shop, on a home printer with high-quality glossy or matte photo paper, or at retail photo counters like CVS, Walgreens, Walmart, or Costco. PhotoGov produces a professional print-grade PDF file, so you can easily print it out at a convenient location.

"},{"q":"Can I Get a CVS 5x5 Photo Print?","a":"

Yes. CVS Photo supports square prints, so you can order a CVS 5x5 photo print at a CVS photo counter directly. Walgreens and Walmart also offer this option.

"},{"q":"Can I Change My Casual Clothing into Formal Attire in My 5x5 Photo?","a":"

Yes. PhotoGov can replace casual clothing with formal attire upon checkout. As a basic premium feature, you get five formal clothing variations so you can pick the most professional look for your 5x5 photo. For a small additional fee, you can add 9 more professional looks.

"},{"q":"Is There a Free 5x5 Size Photo Checker Online?","a":"

Yes. PhotoGov automatically checks your 5x5 photo for size, head proportions, background, and lighting against ICAO and government ID-photo guidelines, and flags anything that needs a retake. Add Human Verification, and our senior specialist will review the photo manually and provide you with expert feedback on the acceptance likelihood.

"},{"q":"Is Human Verification Available for My 5x5 Photo?","a":"

Yes. You can pick Human Verification at checkout, and a senior PhotoGov compliance specialist reviews your finished 5x5 photo against the current ID-photo rules, then either approves it or offers you to re-upload. It is worth it for booked appointments, first-time applications, or fast-changing children’s photos.

"},{"q":"What Happens If My ID Photo 5x5 cm Is Rejected?","a":"

If the rejection is down to a technical fault on our side, we refund you or provide a free retake. If the original selfie is the issue — lighting, head angle, or expression — just take a fresh one and upload again. Adding Human Verification before you submit lowers the chance of a rejection in the first place.

"},{"q":"Is My Personal Data and Photo Safe With PhotoGov?","a":"

Yes. We treat your personal data and images with great care. PhotoGov uses your information solely to generate your ID photo 5x5 cm and deletes it from our servers once the process is complete. We never share your data with third parties or external AI services. If you have any questions, you can always contact our Customer Support team or read more details in our Privacy Policy.

"},{"q":"Is There an Official Government 5x5 Photo Tool?","a":"

No. Most authorities that accept the 5x5 format publish the specifications and sample photos, but do not run their own online tools. You can use a reliable passport photo maker instead. Choose one based on high Google ratings and positive customer reviews, and check the user-friendliness of the interface — preferably, the one that works right in a browser and doesn’t require uploads or account creation. Reliable services only accept correctly taken photos — check our guide on how to take your own digital photo from home.

"}]

children.innerHtml: Our platform is built to meet all official 600x800 photo rules. However, the final acceptance of your photo is always at the full discretion of the issuing authority.
PhotoGov and International Standards for 600x800 Photos

PhotoGov is a passport photo-making tool built to create compliance-aligned 600x800 photos. We strictly follow key international authorities' 600x800 photo rules, and our built-in templates adhere to the biometric guidelines of the International Civil Aviation Organization Document 9303. These requirements are regularly monitored and updated by our compliance team.
The images produced by our online passport photo maker tool are tailored to the 600x800-pixel format with the head taking 70-80% of the image, centered in the frame, and a plain white background.

Your 600x800 passport photo is adjusted only in terms of size, crop, and background — and your facial features are not altered in any way. The final file is prepared for printing or digital submission in just a few seconds.

If your 600x800-pixel photo submission is time-sensitive, or a photo rejection would cause significant inconvenience, select our Human Verification service upon checkout. Our senior compliance specialist will manually review your 600x800 photo against the latest official requirements of your selected document.

For other ID photos, see our dedicated tools: US Passport Photo Maker, UK Passport Photo Maker, Canada Passport Photo Maker, US Visa Photo Tool, UK Visa Photo Tool, Canada Visa Photo Tool, DV Lottery Photo Tool, US Green Card Photo Tool, US Digital Passport Photo Tool.

children.innerHtml: 6x9 cm Photo – Easy and Free

When applying for various official documents, a 6x9 cm photo is often required. Whether it’s for an ID card, visa, or another official document, submitting a compliant photo in the 6x9 cm size is crucial to avoid delays or rejections.  At PhotoGov, we help you create the perfect 6x9 cm photo effortlessly. Upload a selfie or a high-quality photo, and we will resize, crop, and optimize it according to the required standards, ready for digital submission or physical print.
A job application asks for a different kind of portrait, and the PhotoGov job application photo guide shows how to shoot one at home.
Auto-crop the photo to fit the Others photo size (free online tool)
Full document requirements for photos
How to get a photo - tutorial
Get photo for: Photo 6x9 cm
Why Choose Our 6x9 cm Photo Service?
Exact 6x9 cm Size
Your photo will be automatically resized and cropped to the right size of 6x9 cm
Background Removal
This feature gets rid of shadows and makes sure the background is clean and white or light-colored
Better Image Quality
Makes the image look more professional by changing the brightness, clarity, and contrast
Digital and print versions
Get your photo in both digital and print-ready formats so you can easily send it in
Guaranteed Compliance
Fulfills all the official photo criteria for a variety of documents
*Data from government agencies
6x9 cm Photo Requirements

Your 6x9 centimeter photo must meet the official technical and visual standards in order to be accepted. Every official format rests on the same biometric rules, which PhotoGov explains in a separate guide to biometric photos.
Here is a list of the requirements you must meet:
Size
6 x 9 cm (60 x 90 mm)
Image Format
JPEG or PNG
Resolution
At least 300 DPI
File Size
Usually less than 1 MB
Printable
Yes, for physical submission at local governments or consulates
Digital Submission
Some online platforms or consular systems accept it
Rules for how to look

children.innerHtml: Step-by-Step Guide to Making Your 6x9 cm Photo
Choose the Type of Document
On PhotoGov.net, pick "6x9 cm Photo" from the list
Get Your Picture
Get a good smartphone or digital camera.  Stand 1.5 to 2 meters away from a plain white or light-colored wall.  Make sure the lighting is gentle and even
Send the picture
Send your picture to PhotoGov.  Make sure the face is clear, the expression is neutral, and the light is even
Auto-Resize and Improve
Our platform will cut the picture down to 6x9 cm, clean up the backdrop, and make the picture look better
Download and Send
You can either print the finished photo file or upload it online
Best Ways to Take a 6x9 cm Photo
Use natural daylight or mild artificial light to avoid sharp shadows
Background: Stand in front of a plain white or light-colored wall. Don't have any patterns or things that will distract you in the backdrop.
Positioning: Keep your face in the middle and facing ahead. Your face should take up 70–80% of the height of the picture.
Wear dark, solid-colored clothes that stand out against the pale background. Don't wear tops that are white or shiny.
How to take your own Photo 6x9 cm photo

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect photo photo yourself:
1. Take a picture of yourself

Open up the PhotoGov.net photo service and take your picture. Make sure you’re not wearing any headcovers or glasses, do not wear a uniform, and keep your expression neutral. Ensure that the area is well-lit and that you are standing against a neutral background.

children.innerHtml: 3. Receive your Passport Photo
Finally, you can download your ID photo. These images can be printed off, or you can simply use them as digital photos.
Mistakes to Avoid
Using the wrong size photo (such a passport photo instead of a 6x9 cm one)
Wearing glasses or hats that hide your face
Using photos that are grainy or low-resolution
Background with shadows, patterns, or anything
Smiling or tilting your head
PhotoGov will find and fix these mistakes on its own while it is processing photos
Submission and Printing Guidelines
For Physical Submission: Make sure the size of your photo is exactly 6x9 cm, and print it on high-quality matte or glossy photo paper
For Digital Submission: Make sure the file fulfills the size and resolution requirements before uploading it to the right gateway
How to take Photo 6x9 cm photos for babies and kids

When taking pictures of babies and children for photo, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.
More tips for following the rules
No Retouching: Don't use beauty filters or change the way your face looks
Sharpness: Make sure the picture is clear and sharp, with no pixelation or blurring
Face Coverage: Your face should take up 70–80% of the height of the picture
File Size and Type: JPEG or PNG, and less than 1 MB for digital submission

children.innerHtml: 9x12 cm Photo – Perfect for Submission and Easy to Create

For some applications, such educational certificates, professional licenses, or specialist ID cards, you need to send in a 9x12 centimeter photo. To be accepted, the photo must be the right size, quality, and background. PhotoGov makes it easy to take the perfect 9x12 cm picture. We will resize, crop, and optimize your photo according to the required guidelines so that you can submit it digitally or in person. Smaller ID formats follow their own specification, and the rules for a 1x1 picture size are set out in a separate checklist.

children.innerHtml: Best Ways to Take a 9x12 cm Photo
Lighting: To avoid harsh shadows or too much light, use soft, balanced lighting.
Background: The background should be a solid white or light color with no patterns or textures.

Positioning: Make sure your face is in the middle of the frame and facing the camera directly. Your face should take up 70–80% of the height of the photo. The same framing applies when making a 2x2 photo for US documents, where the head must fill a fixed share of the frame.
Clothes: Wear dark, solid colors to stand out against the background. Don't wear white tops
Step-by-step: How to Make Your 9x12 cm Photo

If you’d like to make your own photo for a Photo 9x12 cm, saving you the trouble of making an appointment with a professional photographer and turning up in person, there are a few important steps you’ll need to follow. We’ve broken them down for you below:
A separate guide describes a job application photo at home, from background and light to the framing employers expect.
Choose the Type of Document
From our list of supported documents, choose "9x12 cm Photo" on PhotoGov.net
Take a Picture
Use a smartphone or a camera with a lot of pixels.  Make sure the lighting is good and stand 1.5 to 2 meters away from a light-colored background
Put Your Picture Up
Send your picture to PhotoGov.  Make sure the face is easy to see and that the expression is neutral
Resize and Optimize Automatically
We will resize the picture to 9x12 cm, fix any flaws in the backdrop, and make the picture look better
Get it and send it
Prepare your picture for digital submission or print it out to use in real life

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect photo photo yourself:
1. Take a picture of yourself

Open up the PhotoGov.net photo service and take your picture. Make sure you’re not wearing any headcovers or glasses, do not wear a uniform, and keep your expression neutral. Ensure that the area is well-lit and that you are standing against a neutral background.

children.innerHtml: 3. Receive your Passport Photo
Finally, you can download your ID photo. These images can be printed off, or you can simply use them as digital photos.
Things You Shouldn't Do:
Using the wrong size photo (such a passport photo instead of a 9x12 cm one)
Smiling or tilting your head
Putting on glasses or other things that block your face
Photos that are too bright, too dark, or grainy
Background with patterns or shadows
PhotoGov finds and fixes these problems automatically while processing photos.
More tips for following the rules
No Retouching: Don't use digital filters or edits that change the way your face looks.
Sharpness: Make sure your picture is clean and in focus, with no pixelation or blurriness.
Face Coverage: Your face should take up 70–80% of the height of the picture.
File Format and Size: JPEG or PNG, less than 1 MB for digital submission
For Physical Submission: Make sure the size is exactly 9x12 cm when you print your photo on high-quality matte or glossy photo paper.
To submit digitally, put the file on the right official system or gateway. Check that the picture is the right size and resolution.
How to take a Photo 9x12 cm photo using a phone
So long as your smartphone has a good quality camera, you can certainly use it to take a picture for your photo. With that being said, however, selfies are not acceptable, so follow these steps:
Ask someone to take your picture for you.
Position them 5-7 feet away so that only your upper body is in the shot.
Alternatively, use a tripod set up between 5-7 feet away. Move it as necessary to get the perfect picture.
PhotoGov Features
Our online passport photo tool offers several features to help you create the perfect photo:
Crop

Our in-built cropping feature allows you to trim new photo photos and ensure that they don’t have uneven edges. This allows you to neaten up your picture and ensure it’s the proper size for your photo.
Resize

You can also resize your picture as needed through PhotoGov, meaning that the end result will be a perfectly proportioned image that will fit just right into your photo. Additionally, you don’t need to worry about stretching or squishing the image and ruining the quality.
Background removal
If you can’t find a neutral background against which you can take a satisfactory picture, don’t worry; we have a background removal tool that can help you achieve the same results.
Auto-adjustment
With the click of a button, you can have our auto-adjustment tool immediately optimize your image to meet brightness, color, and contrast standards.
How to take Photo 9x12 cm photos for babies and kids

When taking pictures of babies and children for photo, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.
How can i convert my photo to photo size?

While you can convert the size of pictures using a variety of methods, the best option is to use our photo photo tool - PhotoGov. That way, you can rest assured you’ll have a high-quality, properly sized end product, one that isn’t distorted or blurred by stretching or compressing.
I already have a digital photo photo. How do i print it?

If you have a digital photograph, unfortunately, you won’t just be able to print it out on printer paper. You specifically need a high-quality print on either matte or glossy photo paper. You can either achieve this by visiting any photo service or by using our tool to print your image off at home.
Where to get a photo photo
Pharmacies and drug stores
Well-known medicinal retail brands, namely Walgreens, CVS, and Rite Aid, proffer immediate passport photo solutions in-store. Do anticipate a charge, with most services priced around the $15 mark.
Shipping centers

Shipping giants like UPS, FedEx, and adjacent shipping facilities also cater to passport photo needs, mirroring the services of typical drugstores. At a going rate of around $15, it stands as a worthy alternative if you're considering external providers for your passport imagery.
Post offices and other passport acceptance agents

It's customary for post offices and agencies of a similar function to be equipped for passport applications, which includes offering photographic sessions. Maintaining the price consistency as observed earlier, you can typically expect a fee around the $15 ballpark.
Retail stores

Retail venues frequently host areas meant for passport photo shoots, assuring quality pictures in line with norms. Even though each establishment might set its own rate, you can usually anticipate a decent pricing range.

children.innerHtml: Getting the Ideal Biometric Passport Photo

Submitting a biometric passport photo is among the most important criteria when seeking a passport. Used for biometric identity and security reasons, this kind of photo has to meet certain criteria. Even tiny errors could cause your passport application to be rejected or delayed.

    But don't be concerned! PhotoGov.net lets you quickly generate a compatible biometric passport photo using only your phone, no photo studio or professional photographer required.

    This post will guide you through the main criteria for biometric passport images and demonstrate how PhotoGov can assist you in achieving accuracy the first time.

The Importance of Your Biometric Passport Photo

A biometric passport photo is not just a regular picture. Your passport, which will be used for security and identification in systems like facial recognition at border control, includes this. This indicates the image has to satisfy rigorous criteria established by the authorities including size, head orientation, background color, and expression. Our guide explains what biometric means for photos, from the parameters that are measured to the standardized form officials receive.

Not satisfying these criteria could cause your passport application to be processed late or possibly denied.  PhotoGov.net guarantees your photo will satisfy all required standards without any inconvenience.
How PhotoGov Enables You to Produce the Ideal Biometric Passport Photo
Your passport photo doesn't have to be difficult.  PhotoGov makes it simple to produce a compliant biometric photo in only a few easy actions:
A workplace portrait uses the same home setup, and our guide to job application photos explains what changes.
Use your phone to snap a well-lit, crisp selfie.  Ensure your face is in the centre and your expression is neutral
Send your selfie to PhotoGov.net
Our system will automatically crop, resize, and modify your photo to fit the particular criteria for a biometric passport photo
Your photo is ready for submission; download it once processing is finished
How to take your own Biometric passport photo photo

If you don’t want to go through the trouble and expense of locating and hiring a professional photographer to take your picture, you can simply take your own from home. So long as you follow the below instructions carefully, you can capture the perfect passport photo yourself:
1. Take a picture of yourself

Open up the PhotoGov.net photo service and take your picture. Make sure you’re not wearing any headcovers or glasses, do not wear a uniform, and keep your expression neutral. Ensure that the area is well-lit and that you are standing against a neutral background.

children.innerHtml: Typical Errors to Avoid
Although many people think taking a biometric passport photo is easy, typical errors could lead to problems with your application.  Here are some things to avoid doing:
The background should be simple white or light gray, with no patterns, textures, or shadows
Your picture has to be precisely 35 mm x 45 mm Square formats are measured differently, and our checklist shows how to check 1x1 picture size before you submit it.
Avoid shadows or dark spots that hide your face or the surroundings under poor lighting
Facial expression: Your mouth should be closed and your eyes open, hence a neutral expression is essential
Glasses with glare: If you wear glasses, check for no glare or reflection obstructing your vision
PhotoGov automatically corrects these errors for you, so guaranteeing that your photo is compliant each time
Main Features of PhotoGov
PhotoGov is the greatest tool for producing your biometric passport photo for the following reasons:
Crop
Crops the image to the proper size (35x45 mm) automatically
Resize
Resizes the picture to fit the official size criteria for biometric passport pictures
Background removal
Removes any distracting background and replaces it with a neutral, conforming hue
Auto-adjustment
Automatically changes contrast, sharpness, and illumination to provide a clear, high-quality image
Advantages of Using PhotoGov.net Quick and Easy
Just send us your selfie; we'll handle everything else.
Affordable: Achieve professional-quality outcomes without the steep cost of photo studios.
Our method ensures your photo will satisfy all the official biometric passport photo criteria every time.
We offer both versions, so you are prepared for any submission technique
How to take Biometric passport photo photos for babies and kids

When taking pictures of babies and children for passport, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.

children.innerHtml: What is a 2x2 Resume Photo?

A professional headshot sized 2 × 2 inches (51 × 51 mm), used in resumes, CVs, and job applications. A passport photo is a stricter format: how to make a biometric passport photo is covered in its own guide.

Prepared by PhotoGov as an HR-ready 2 × 2-inch image with correct framing, head proportions, and background. Official documents in the same format are stricter, so check the requirements for a 2x2 photo before you submit.

Suitable for digital resumes, online applications, company ID badges, profile photos, and for printing alongside a CV. If a form asks for a smaller square image, check 1x1 picture size requirements before you resize the file.
Your Final 2x2 Resume Photo from PhotoGov

PhotoGov automatically applies all official requirements to your original photo. The final image is a 2x2-inch CV-ready photo. It doesn’t require any adjustments from you. Below are the key technical parameters of your final photo from PhotoGov.

children.innerHtml: If your photo is rejected due to technical issues on PhotoGov’s side, we provide a free retake or a full refund.
PhotoGov and Professional Resume Photo Standards

Your photo is a key part of your CV. PhotoGov creates a clean, sharp, professional 2x2 resume photo that makes a real impact on your job application. Before you upload it, the job application photo step by step guide runs through lighting, distance, and expression at home.

If you're applying for a new job right now, our add-on casual-to-formal clothing swap service can be especially useful. The outfit in your original photo is digitally replaced with formal business attire. Premium includes 5 outfit options, with 9 more available for a small additional fee.
These professional photos in a business outfit can be used at your new workspace once you're hired — for badges, internal company websites, work email profiles, and more.

A 2x2 resume photo is 2 \u00d7 2 inches \u2014 the same as 51 \u00d7 51 mm, or 600 \u00d7 600 pixels at 300 DPI and 1,200 x 1,200 pixels at 600 DPI. It is a square headshot, the standard format used when a US resume, CV, or any application has a professional photo.<\/p>"},{"q":"How Do I Make a 2x2 Resume Photo Online?","a":"

How to take Resume Photo 35x45 mm photos for babies and kids

When taking pictures of babies and children for photo, many of the same rules apply; for example, they must still adhere to the dress code, and the photograph must be high-quality and well-lit. With that being said, the State Department is generally more forgiving when it comes to the neutral expression requirement.
If you are photographing a newborn:
Spread a white sheet out over the floor.
Place the baby down on the sheet and take their photograph against it.
For slightly older babies:
Prop them up in a child’s chair against a white sheet.
If they are still unable to hold up their head, prop it up for them using a hand behind the sheet. Ensure no one else is visible in the shot.
